tour.name: Kuari Pass Trek
tour.summary:
Winter Kuari trek is one of the most beautiful winter trek that perfectly capture the grandeur of the snow-landscape. Settled at an altitude of 4264 meters, Kuari Pass boasts of amphitheatre views of Kamet (7756m), Trishul (7120m), Chaukhamba (7128m), and the great divine peak of Nanda Devi (7817m) and its twin Nanda Devi East (7434m). The mountain pass is located in the Garhwal region of the state of Uttarakhand. It lies to the south of the Tibetan Plateau, and is within the enchanting Nanda Devi National Park. Well-known as the Lord Curzon trail, Kuari Pass Trek gives you a chance to view the impressive blue-skyline donned with white landscape.

The trek will start from Joshimath, and will proceed to Akhod Getta which will be your first campsite. The charismatic view of the snow-dressed mountain, Mt. Chaukhamba will be seen from the base camp. Moving on to the goal destination, the trail of Kuari Pass will have great patches of snow and the blowing winds will make the trek even more exhilarating. After walking past snow-covers, you will reach the peak point of Kuari Pass that will offer spectacular views of Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat. The trek isn’t over, as your next destination goal will be the fascinating Auli. The track to reach Auli is laden with dense forests that houses great diversity of flora and fauna, and vast pasturelands. The stupendous views of Auli Himalayan peaks, Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi peak and Dronagiri will make your heart drool with its beauty.

Explore another version of Kuari Pass trek
tour.itineraries:
Day 1: Drive from Haridwar – Joshimath (260 km)​
After arriving in Haridwar, you will drive to Joshimath, a religious city for people going to Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib. The drive will take around 10 hours covering a distance of 260km for you to reach. On reaching, you will check-in at your pre-booked hotel.
Day 2: Drive from Joshimath to Dhak Village (10 Kms) - Trek from Dhak to Akhod getha (6Kms)​

Today morning you will embark your journey for Kuari Pass trek. At first you will have to drive to Dhak village, from where you will walk and snake through beautiful rhododendron, oak and hemlock forest. After walking for a while, you will descent to a grassland which will also be your campsite at Akhod Getha. The magnetizing view of the snow-dressed mountain, Chaukhamba can be seen from your campsite. You will also come across shepherds living here who come down during harsh winters. Strike a conversation with a local, and you will get to hear numerous stories about the place. You will also find a spring line at the crown of the meadow for unlimited water supply. Take pictures of the sweeping mountains, sit at the edge gazing the beauty of nature or take pleasure in the company of your friends midst the beautiful landscape.
Day 3: Trek from Akhod Getha to Kuari Pass to Akhod Getha (10 kms)​

As soon as the morning unfolds, you will set out to continue your trek to Kuari Pass. Post breakfast, your trek leader will give you tips and tricks about the following trek, listen carefully and abide by it throughout the trek. You will trek for 5km, however, in between you will take breaks as the trail today will be quite steep. A trek will ascend till Khullara, from where you will encounter great patches of snow. After walking past the snow covers, you will reach the Kuari top. The winds won’t stop whispering, while you will take in the sweeping vistas of the mighty Himalayas. After clicking pictures of Mt. Nanda Devi, you decent back to the campsite, Akhod Getha and relish your hot dinner at night, post which you spend time with your friends or rejuvenate yourself midst the nature.
Day 04: Trek from Akhod Getha to Gulling (5 Kms)​
Wake up to the beautiful sunrise, and head-out for the next campsite, Gulling. Leaving behind the vistas of Mt. Chaukhamba, you will see Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat when you reach the next base camp. On arriving at the campsite, you can relax in your tent or can choose to indulge in various activities. At night, you will be served with tantalizing dinner, post which you either sleep or spend time with your friends.
Day 05: Trek from Gulling to Auli via Gorson Bugyal (08 Kms) - Drive to Joshimath form Auli (15kms)​

After savouring your breakfast midst natural surroundings, today you will trek to Auli. The magnificent views of Auli will spell-bind you with its splendour. The trail to Auli will meander through dense forests and vast pasturelands. While trekking you will outstanding views of Himalayan peaks, Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi peak and Dronagiri. On the way, click pictures of the ravishing valleys, villages till you reach the lush grassland of Gorson. Cross the grasslands, and continue walking till your reach the verdant meadows of Auli. On reaching Auli, you will be served with hot lunch, after relishing the food, you will take your belongings and drive back to Joshimath
Day 06: Joshimath to Haridwar
Today is the last day of your trip, as after having breakfast, you will drive back to Haridwar taking along ample of memories. You can indulge in evening Aarti at Harki Pauri if you arrive in time. Later, you can spend the rest of the time at your leisure.

output.name: Kuari Pass Trek: Winter Ascent to 4,264 Meters
output.subtitle: Six days across Garhwal's high-altitude pass, connecting Joshimath to Auli through snow fields and rhododendron forest
output.summary: The Kuari Pass trek crosses the high-altitude frontier between the Hindu pilgrimage towns of the Alaknanda Valley and the skiing meadows of Auli. The pass itself sits at 4,264 meters on the southern flank of the Tibetan Plateau, within Nanda Devi National Park, and commands a direct amphitheater view of five major Himalayan peaks: Nanda Devi (7,817m), Kamet (7,756m), Chaukhamba (7,128m), Trishul (7,120m), and Nanda Devi East (7,434m). The route, historically known as the Lord Curzon trail, ascends from the forested slopes above Joshimath through rhododendron and hemlock stands, then climbs into open meadow and snow fields to the pass itself, before descending into the high grasslands of Auli. Winter conditions—significant snow cover and sustained wind—define the character of the trek.
highlights: Ascent to Kuari Pass with direct views of Nanda Devi and four other peaks
Rhododendron and oak forest trekking through Akhod Getha meadow, first camp in the trek
Snow-field crossing with views of Chaukhamba, Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat
High-altitude grassland descent to Auli via Gorson Bugyal, an alpine meadow
Winter alpine terrain: snow patches, high wind exposure, and thin-air acclimatization
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Drive from Haridwar to Joshimath
The trek begins with a 260-kilometer drive from Haridwar, a major city and railhead in the foothills, to Joshimath, a pilgrimage center on the Alaknanda River. Joshimath is the traditional starting point for journeys to Badrinath and Hemkund Sahib. The drive takes around 10 hours, climbing steadily into the Garhwal region. Hotel accommodation in Joshimath for the night.

Day 2 — Dhak Village to Akhod Getha Meadow
A 10-kilometer drive from Joshimath brings you to Dhak Village, where the Kuari Pass trek formally begins. From here, the trail winds through dense rhododendron, oak, and hemlock forest, following traditional shepherd routes through the landscape. After approximately 6 kilometers of walking, the forest gradually opens into Akhod Getha, a sweeping alpine meadow that will serve as your first campsite. The magnetizing views of snow-dressed Chaukhamba dominate the northern horizon from here. You may encounter local shepherds who inhabit these meadows seasonally, descending during the harshest winters. A conversation with them often reveals stories woven into the landscape itself. A spring line runs along the crown of the meadow, providing reliable water supply. Take time to photograph the surrounding peaks, sit at the meadow's edge to absorb the vastness of the terrain, or simply rest in the company of fellow trekkers amid this beautiful alpine setting.

Day 3 — Kuari Pass Day Trek from Akhod Getha
After breakfast, your trek leader will brief you on the day ahead—listen carefully to their guidance on managing the steep terrain. The 5-kilometer ascent to Kuari Pass climbs steeply toward Khullara, where snow patches begin to dominate the landscape. As you gain elevation, wind exposure increases noticeably. The final push brings you to Kuari Pass at 4,264 meters, where the vista opens dramatically: Nanda Devi and Nanda Devi East rise to the northeast, Kamet anchors the north, while Chaukhamba and Trishul frame the western horizon. Take time to absorb the scale of these mountains before retracing your steps back to Akhod Getha. The descent returns you to camp in the late afternoon. Settle into the evening with a hot dinner, then spend time with fellow trekkers or simply rest beneath the open sky.

Day 4 — Akhod Getha to Gulling Meadow
The trek descends to Gulling, a secondary meadow campsite. Views shift from Chaukhamba (left behind to the south) to the broader northern panorama of Dronagri, Hathi Parvat, and Gori Parvat. The terrain remains open grassland with sections of remaining snow. Tented accommodation at Gulling.

Day 5 — Trek to Auli via Gorson Bugyal, then Drive to Joshimath
After breakfast, you'll trek 8 kilometers through dense forests and expansive pasturelands toward Auli. The trail ascends through changing terrain, passing through Gorson Bugyal's lush grasslands before reaching the verdant meadows of Auli. Throughout the walk, the Himalayan peaks dominate the northern horizon—Nanda Devi, Hathi Ghodi, and Dronagiri visible across the valleys. Pause to photograph the ravishing landscape and villages along the way. On arrival at Auli, lunch awaits before you drive the 15 kilometers back down to Joshimath, where you'll spend the night.

Day 6 — Joshimath to Haridwar
Your final day begins with breakfast before the 260-kilometer drive back to Haridwar, a journey of approximately 10 hours. If timing permits upon arrival in late afternoon or evening, you may join the Aarti ceremony at Harki Pauri. The remainder of the day is at your leisure.

The route begins in Trincomalee, where the Indian Ocean provides opportunities for snorkeling and diving among coral ecosystems, followed by a transition into the dry-zone jungle of Wilpattu, home to Sri Lankan elephants, leopards, sloth bears, and substantial populations of resident and migratory waterbirds. output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Colombo & Transfer to Trincomalee
Arrival at Colombo International Airport. A driver meets guests in the arrivals lounge for a six-hour transfer to Trincomalee on Sri Lanka's northeast coast. The route traverses inland terrain before reaching the Indian Ocean. Evening check-in at Jungle Beach in Kuchchuweli, a beachside property set among tropical vegetation.

Day 2 — Trincomalee Beach Rest
A full day at Jungle Beach. The property sits directly on the coast, with the hotel's architecture incorporating existing trees and plant life into its structure. Guests spend the day at leisure on the beach or within the resort grounds. Overnight at Jungle Beach.

Day 3 — Pigeon Island Reef Snorkeling & Diving
An excursion to Pigeon Island, a protected marine reserve offshore from Trincomalee. The coral ecosystem supports over 100 species of tropical corals and approximately 300 species of reef fish, along with Black Tip reef sharks, rays, and sea turtles. Snorkeling and diving options allow direct observation of the underwater habitat. Return to Jungle Beach for overnight.

Day 4 — Trincomalee Beach Rest
Another leisure day at Jungle Beach. Overnight at the resort.

Day 5 — Transfer to Wilpattu National Park & First Safari
A two-hour transfer by private vehicle westward to Wilpattu National Park, Sri Lanka's largest terrestrial protected area. Guests arrive at the park entrance at noon and are driven to the safari campsite. Wilpattu's dry-zone jungle landscape is densely vegetated and dotted with approximately 30 natural freshwater lakes (locally called villus), which sustain populations of resident and migratory waterfowl including garganey, pintail, whistling teal, spoonbill, white ibis, large white egret, cattle egret, and purple heron. The park also hosts gull, tern, owl, kite, and eagle species, plus endemic species such as the Sri Lanka jungle fowl, little cormorant, and painted stork. Mammal species found in the park include Sri Lankan elephant, Sri Lankan leopard, sloth bear, spotted deer, buffalo, sambar, and mongoose. A late afternoon game drive and dinner precede overnight in a safari camp tent.

Day 6 — Wilpattu Safari and Campsite Days

tour.summary: A 10-day cultural adventure that dives deep into truly enriching experiences often overlooked. Traverse Taiwan's remote areas, ancient trails, and waterfalls. Immersive workshops and culinary experiences that most visitors won't find on any other travel offering.
highlights:
Hike Three of Taiwan's Stunning Historic Trails
Deep experience with indigenous hosts at workshops, village visits and classes
Visit some of the biggest temples and night markets in Taiwan
Taste-of-Place culinary and tea tasting experiences
tour.itineraries:
Day One: Taipei (Arrival Day)
Arrive in Taipei and explore the city, including a 300-year-old temple. Enjoy a group welcome dinner as the city lights up, followed by a stroll through a vibrant shopping district.

Day Two: Caoling Historic Trail | Hualien
Hike the 7km Caoling Historic Trail, a 200-year-old trade route. Enjoy coastal views and a visit to Daoist Temple before a transfer to Hualien. Explore Dadongmen Night Market at night.

Day Three: Indigenous Wild Greens | Liyu Lake | Shoufeng
Visit the Indigenous Wild Vegetable Center showcasing the Amis people's efforts in preserving wild vegetable species. Lunch lake side at Liyu Lake, followed by a flat 5km walk around the lake (mostly designated car-free path).

Day Four: Hunter's School | Kiwit Village | Ruishui
Visit a local Hunter's School and learn about the Amis' hunting culture and cuisine. Enjoy a short walking tour with herbal foot bath in Kiwit. Hot spring hotel in Ruisui.

Day Five: Dye Workshop | Tea Tasting | Yuli Hot Springs
Get hands-on at the Ruisui dye workshop creating your own keepsake. After lunch, enjoy a honey-flavored black tea tasting before ending the day at a historic hot spring hotel.

Day Six: Walami Trail | Bunan House | Chishang
Explore the Batongguan Historic Trail, once the site of Japanese-indigenous conflict. Epic suspension bridges, central mountain views, and visit a remote Bunan slate house.

Day Seven: Calligraphy Writing | Amis Cooking | Taitung
Join local elders to learn about rice harvesting traditions. Experience the joy of calligraphy and its connection to the land. Enjoy an evening Amis cooking experience.

Day Eight: Alangyi Historic Trail | Mudan Hot Springs
Hike Taiwan's last undeveloped coastline. This easy coastal hike, Alangyi, weaves together Indigenous, Japanese, and Taiwanese history. Overnight at a hot spring hotel in Mudan.

Day Nine: Sandimen | Buddhist Temple | Taipei
Heading off from our hotel, we'll visit a glass bead cultural workshop in Sandimen before lunch. After lunch, we'll head to Fo Guang Buddhist Temple before taking the High Speed Rail back to Taipei.

Day Ten: Taipei (Departure Day)
Leisurely breakfast and any last minute souvenirs or snacks before jumping on our airport transfer back to Taoyuan International Airport. Say farewell to Taiwan until next time!

tour.name: North India Revealed
tour.summary: Embark on a 22-day odyssey through India’s intoxicating north. Discover sights, smells, and flavours that will blaze their way into your memory and stay there forever. See towering sandstone fortresses, pilgrims praying on riverbanks, Maharajah mementos in a ghostly palace, and silhouettes on a desert landscape. India can be a daunting place at times, even for experienced travellers, but with the guidance of your local leader, you’ll be navigating the crowds, dodging the cows and eating the best chaat from a cart in no time! From the beating heart of Delhi to the holy city of Varanasi – this is north India.
tour.itineraries:
Day 1  Delhi
Namaste and welcome to Delhi! Your adventure begins with a welcome meeting at 6 pm. If you arrive in Delhi with time to spare before the meeting, consider finding your feet with an Urban Adventure. The Hidden Gems of Delhi tour offers something a little different from the standard itinerary, taking you to sights most tourists never see.
Day 2  Delhi – Overnight Train
This morning set off by metro to Old Delhi to explore on a walking tour. Experience the chaos of an Indian traffic jam as you inch your way through the streets around Chandni Chowk marketplace in a traditional cycle rickshaw. Visit the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, then stop by the Sheeshganj Gurudwara (Sikh Temple) to learn about the religion. Tonight, transfer to the railway station and board an overnight train to Bikaner. Local vendors will board the train at various stops to sell snacks, but it’s advised that you bring some of your own food for the journey too.
Day 3  Bikaner
Bikaner a city in Rajasthan still displays its ancient opulence through palaces and forts, built of red sandstone that have withstood the passage of time. Upon arrival in Bikaner this morning, freshen up at your hotel and then head out on a walk with your leader through the old city.

In the afternoon relax or opt to visit Junagarh Fort: Built in 1588 AD by Raja Rai Singh. Constructed in red sandstone and marble, it's courtyard, balconies and windows are a treat to the eye
Day 4  Bikaner to Jaisalmer
After breakfast travel to Jaisalmer by train. On arrival, choose whether to relax or join the group on an optional trip to the Jaisalmer Folklore Museum. This small museum displays a private family collection of printing blocks, musical instruments, religious artifacts, and decorations which offer insights into the cultural heritage of Jaisalmer.
Day 5  Jaisalmer
Enjoy a free day to explore Jaisalmer. The city’s eponymous fort holds twisting alleys with markets where you can wander for hours. You can also find a series of Jain temples dating from the 15th and 16th centuries within the walls of the fort, and it’s easy to spend a few hours admiring their elaborate carvings. The opulent havelis (traditional Indian mansions) found throughout the city make another fine place to spend some time admiring the desert architecture.
Day 6  Thar Desert
Today drive by jeep to the Thar Desert. Meet your local guides, who will cook a traditional Rajasthani dinner with chapati, dal, rice and veggies while you sit back, relax and watch the sunset. Spend the night stargazing and sharing stories in this incredible setting.
Day 7  Jodhpur
Rise early to enjoy the sunrise over the sand dunes. After a simple breakfast, take a private vehicle to the railway station and then a 6-hour train ride across the desert to the blue city of Jodhpur. Jodhpur is home to some of the best lassis in India, so make sure you try one while you’re here.
Day 8  Jodhpur
Today you have the option to visit the colossal Mehrangarh Fort, one of the largest in India. The fort is still run by the Jodhpur royal family. If you’d prefer to see a more down to earth kind of Rajasthani life, it is also possible to spend today touring nearby Bishnoi villages. Spending time in these villages offers a glimpse into rural Rajasthani life and the chance to learn about the rich cultural traditions of the people who live there.
Day 9  Udaipur
This morning take an auto-rickshaw to the bus station and board a local bus for an 8-hour journey to Udaipur. This romantic city is set amid the Aravalli Hills and curls around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century. On arrival, take a guided walk to get your bearings. Explore twisting alleyways filled with shops and bazaars selling things like silver jewellery, shoes, bags, leather goods, and miniature paintings.
Day 10 Udaipur
Enjoy a free day to explore the sights of Udaipur. Perhaps take a short boat ride on the famous Lake Pichola (seasonal) and see the palaces of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas rise out of the water and their own reflections. Otherwise, you could tour the lakeside City Palace complex, the largest palace in Rajasthan, where you can check out vivid murals and royal antiques. Alternatively, learn the secrets behind making the perfect Indian thali during a half-day cooking class.

Maybe you’d like to visit Sajjan Garh (Monsoon Palace), a 19th-century palace perched on a hill overlooking Lake Pichola. Named after Maharana Sajjan Singh of the Mewar Dynasty, Sajjan Garh offers ridiculously great views of the city below. Or perhaps you’re more inclined to visit the nearby village of Shilpgram, an ethnographic museum and arts hubs where traditional crafts are sold, and artists perform.
Day 11  Pushkar
Transfer to the station and travel by train for around 5.5 hours to the city of Ajmer. Hop in a private vehicle for a 45-minute drive to your hotel in Pushkar. One of India's holiest towns and a market centre for the surrounding villages, Pushkar is a great place to immerse yourself in Hindu traditions. On arrival, head out to explore the town on a walking tour, wandering through the main bazaar along the way. Finish with a walk around Pushkar Lake and past the bustling ghats and temples, observing the devout as they worship at the holy waters.
Day 12  Pushkar
Today in Pushkar is free for you to do as you please. Early morning risers can choose to hike up the hill to the Savitri Temple for sunrise views over the town. If the chai man is there, enjoy a steaming cup of tea at the top for breakfast. Later in the day, maybe pay a visit to the colourful Brahma Temple, which is dedicated to the Hindu god. If you’ve planned your tour to coincide with the Pushkar Camel Fair (which changes each year), today will mainly be set aside to experience one of India’s most famous festivals.
Day 13 Jaipur
Return to Ajmer and travel by local bus to Jaipur (approximately 4 hours). On arrival take an auto-rickshaw to your hotel, then head out to explore Rajasthan’s capital on a guided walking tour. This tour includes a visit to the market and opt to visit the beehive-like Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 so that women of the royal family could observe street festivities without being seen by the public. Your evening is free, so perhaps ask your leader to point out the best place to grab dal baati (dal served with wheat rolls).
Day 14  Jaipur
Enjoy a free day in Jaipur, with plenty of optional activities to choose from to fill your day. For many travellers, an optional hot air balloon experience is one of the highlights of Jaipur. If you’d prefer to stay grounded (but still like expansive views) the Amber Fort is both an excellent example of Rajput architecture and a great place from which to see the surrounding area. Or maybe get among the crowds in the city’s bazaars to shop for artisan goods and semi-precious stones. For a true local experience, tonight you could immerse yourself in Bollywood with a movie at a classic cinema.
Day 15  Abhaneri
Head to Abhaneri by private vehicle. This rural town provides a lovely detour from the bigger cities in Rajasthan. Visit the Chand Baori, a 20-metre-deep stepwell where water was collected and locals used to gather to escape the heat. Built in the late ninth century, the baori is a mind-bending feat of construction. Next visit another jewel of Abhaneri, the Harshat Mata Temple. This temple, which is now mostly ruined, was first constructed between the seventh and eighth centuries and dedicated to the goddess of happiness and joy.
Day 16  Fatehpur Sikri – Agra
Head east by private transport for the 2–3-hour journey to Agra, via a stop Fatehpur Sikri where you can opt to go inside. Rich in Mughal heritage, Agra is a city of gardens, temples, and open rooftops. On arrival visit the Taj Mahal, a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz. One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal attracts over three million visitors each year, so be prepared for crowds. If you’re after a cool drink or a light meal, maybe head to Sheroes Hangout. This cafe is staffed by survivors of acid attacks and is located 10 minutes’ walk from the Taj.
Day 17  Agra – Overnight Train
Enjoy a free day before boarding the train this evening. Early risers might want to head back to the Taj Mahal for a very memorable sunrise. While you’re here, be sure to visit the spectacular Red Fort on the banks of the Yamuna River. Built in 1565 by Emperor Akbar, the fort was originally designed to be a military structure. If you have extra time, you may like to continue onto Akbar's Mausoleum to pay your respects to the great emperor. In the evening, board a 12-hour overnight train to Varanasi (Third Class AC).
Day 18  Varanasi
On arrival in Varanasi this morning transfer by auto-rickshaw to your hotel. Head out on a guided walk around the Old City, following your leader through the narrow alleyways. The rest of your day is free to do as you please. This evening, there are two options you should consider, both centred around the holy Ganges. The first is a sunset cruise along the river which allows you to observe life from a unique perspective in the fading light of day. If you’d prefer to stay on land, you could watch local priests perform a Ganga aarti (fire ceremony) at the Dashashwamedh Ghat.
Day 19  Varanasi
Enjoy a free day to explore this holy city. We highly recommend starting very early and take an optional sunrise boat trip along the Ganges, passing pilgrims bathing and praying along the colourful ghats. Alternatively, head out to the ghats on foot to watch the dhobi-wallahs (clothes washers) drying clothes along the riverbank. You could even continue your stroll to the sinking Vishnu temple near the Manikarnika Ghat. Perhaps ask your leader about how to visit Sarnath, about ten kilometres outside of the city, where Gautama Buddha is said to have given his first speech after finding enlightenment.
Day 20  Varanasi – Overnight Train
In the morning, you have some free time to explore more of Varanasi. Perhaps visit the Vishwanath Temple, or simply grab some chaat and watch the world go by. If you’re craving a little peace and quiet before you board another overnight train, consider heading to the Kriti Gallery to check out some contemporary work by local artists. In the afternoon, board the overnight train for a 15-hour journey to Delhi.
Day 21  Delhi


Arrive in Delhi in the late morning and hop in a taxi to the hotel. The rest of the day is free for you to relax or explore the city at your own pace. Tonight, maybe get together with your group and head out for some dinner – your local leader will have plenty of recommendations.
Day 22  Delhi
With no activities planned for today, your North India adventure comes to an end. You are free to depart the accommodation at any time.

output.name: North India: Delhi to Varanasi — 22 Days
output.subtitle: From the capital's layered neighborhoods to the Ganges ghats and Rajasthani desert forts — a 22-day overland journey by train, bus, and local transport
output.summary: This 22-day itinerary moves through northern India's major cities and regions, from Delhi's Old City markets to the Rajasthan circuit of Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur, and Udaipur, then eastward to the temple towns of Pushkar and Jaipur, the ruins of Fatehpur Sikri and Agra's Taj Mahal, and finally to Varanasi on the Ganges. The route combines guided urban walks through busy bazaars and historic quarters, overnight trains between destinations, visits to palaces and forts built in red sandstone and marble, a night camping in the Thar Desert, and time spent watching pilgrims at temples and ghats. A local guide leads the entire journey; accommodation ranges from hotels and guesthouses to overnight sleeper trains and one night of desert camping. The pace allows for both structured exploration and free time within each city to wander independently or participate in optional activities such as cooking classes, boat rides, and visits to lesser-known villages and archaeological sites.

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Delhi
Arrival in Delhi marks the beginning of the journey. A welcome meeting is scheduled for 6 pm at the hotel. Travellers arriving with time before the meeting may visit the city independently or join an optional urban walking tour of lesser-known areas outside the standard tourist circuit.

Day 2 — Old Delhi by Metro and Cycle Rickshaw
The morning begins with a metro journey to Old Delhi for a walking tour. A cycle rickshaw ride through the streets surrounding Chandni Chowk marketplace provides direct experience of Indian traffic and street life. Stops include the Jama Masjid, Delhi's oldest mosque, and the Sheeshganj Gurudwara, a Sikh temple where visitors learn about the religion and its practices. In the evening, transfer to the railway station for an overnight sleeper train to Bikaner. Local vendors board the train at various stops to sell snacks; travellers are advised to bring additional food for the journey.

Day 3 — Bikaner — Red Sandstone Palaces and Forts
Upon arrival in Bikaner in the morning, time is allowed to rest at the hotel before a walking tour through the old city with the local guide. Bikaner displays its historical wealth through palaces and forts constructed from red sandstone. In the afternoon, visitors may relax or visit Junagarh Fort, built in 1588 by Raja Rai Singh using red sandstone and marble. The fort's courtyards, balconies, and carved windows exemplify Rajput architectural design.

Day 4 — Train Journey to Jaisalmer
After breakfast, travel by train to Jaisalmer. Upon arrival, visitors may rest or opt to visit the Jaisalmer Folklore Museum, a small collection of private family artifacts including printing blocks, musical instruments, religious objects, and traditional decorations that document the cultural heritage of the region.

Day 5 — Jaisalmer Fort and Havelis — Free Exploration
The day is unstructured, allowing independent exploration of Jaisalmer. The fort itself contains twisting alleys and markets that can occupy several hours of wandering. Within the fort walls stand Jain temples dating from the 15th and 16th centuries, featuring elaborate stone carvings. Throughout the city, opulent havelis — traditional Indian mansions — showcase desert architecture and interior decoration.

Day 6 — Thar Desert Camp with Sunset and Stars
A jeep drive transports visitors to the Thar Desert, where local guides prepare a traditional Rajasthani dinner of chapati, dal, rice, and vegetables. The evening is spent watching the sunset and spending the night under open sky, with time for conversation and stargazing.

Day 7 — Desert Sunrise and Train to Jodhpur
An early departure allows observation of sunrise over the sand dunes. After a light breakfast, a private vehicle carries the group to the railway station for a six-hour train crossing the desert to Jodhpur, known as the blue city. Jodhpur is noted for traditional lassi — a yogurt-based beverage — available throughout the city.

Day 8 — Jodhpur — Mehrangarh Fort or Bishnoi Villages
The day offers two primary options. Mehrangarh Fort, one of India's largest, remains under management by the Jodhpur royal family and contains extensive architecture and palace rooms. Alternatively, visits to nearby Bishnoi villages provide exposure to rural Rajasthani life and allow observation of traditional cultural practices and agricultural systems in the region.

Day 9 — Auto-Rickshaw and Bus to Udaipur
An auto-rickshaw carries travelers to the bus station for an eight-hour local bus journey to Udaipur. The city sits within the Aravalli Hills and curves around Lake Pichola, a man-made lake created in the 14th century. On arrival, a guided walk provides orientation through the twisting alleyways and bazaars selling silver jewellery, shoes, bags, leather goods, and miniature paintings.

Day 10 — Udaipur — Palaces, Lake, and Optional Activities
This day is free for independent exploration of Udaipur's many sites. A short seasonal boat ride on Lake Pichola offers views of Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas palaces rising from the water. The lakeside City Palace complex, the largest palace in Rajasthan, contains vivid murals and royal antiques. A half-day cooking class teaches the preparation of Indian thali. Sajjan Garh, a 19th-century palace on a hilltop overlooking Lake Pichola and built by Maharana Sajjan Singh, provides expansive views of the city. The nearby village of Shilpgram functions as an ethnographic museum and arts hub where traditional crafts are sold and artists perform.

Day 11 — Train to Ajmer, then Pushkar — Holy Town on the Lake
A train journey of approximately 5.5 hours departs for Ajmer, followed by a 45-minute private vehicle drive to Pushkar. One of India's holiest towns and a market center for surrounding villages, Pushkar is a site of significant Hindu pilgrimage. On arrival, a walking tour leads through the main bazaar and concludes at Pushkar Lake, where devout worshippers bathe and pray at the bustling ghats lined with temples.

Day 12 — Pushkar — Optional Temple Hike and Free Exploration
The day is unscheduled. Early risers may hike to Savitri Temple on a hilltop for sunrise views over the town; local vendors often sell tea at the summit. Later, the Brahma Temple, a colorful structure dedicated to the Hindu god Brahma, is open for visits. If the tour dates align with the Pushkar Camel Fair — an annual festival that changes dates yearly — significant time is devoted to experiencing one of India's largest fairs.

Day 13 — Local Bus to Jaipur and City Walking Tour
A return to Ajmer is followed by a local bus ride of approximately four hours to Jaipur, Rajasthan's capital. An auto-rickshaw takes the group to their hotel; a guided walking tour follows, including visits to the city market and an optional stop at the Palace of the Winds (Hawa Mahal), built in 1799 to allow royal women to observe street events unseen. The evening is free to wander independently; the local guide can recommend dining options.

Day 14 — Jaipur — Amber Fort, Bazaars, and Optional Hot Air Balloon
Jaipur offers numerous optional activities on this free day. Many travellers choose an optional hot air balloon flight for views over the surrounding landscape. Amber Fort, an outstanding example of Rajput architecture, sits on elevated terrain and provides expansive views of the surrounding area. The city's bazaars offer artisan goods and semi-precious stones for purchase. A visit to a classic cinema showing Bollywood films provides a local cultural experience.

Day 15 — Abhaneri — Chand Baori Stepwell and Harshat Mata Temple
A private vehicle transports the group to Abhaneri, a rural town offering a departure from Rajasthan's larger cities. The Chand Baori stepwell — a 20-metre-deep structure built in the late ninth century — demonstrates remarkable engineering precision and served as a water collection and cooling refuge for residents. The Harshat Mata Temple, mostly ruined but originally constructed between the seventh and eighth centuries, was dedicated to the goddess of happiness and joy.

Day 16 — Fatehpur Sikri Detour and Arrival in Agra
A 2-3 hour private vehicle journey heads eastward to Agra, with an optional stop at Fatehpur Sikri, a 16th-century Mughal city. Agra, rich in Mughal heritage, contains gardens, temples, and open rooftops throughout its streets. On arrival, a visit to the Taj Mahal — a white marble mausoleum built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a memorial to his wife Mumtaz — is made. One of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the Taj Mahal draws over three million visitors annually; crowding is substantial. Sheroes Hangout, a cafe 10 minutes' walk from the Taj staffed by acid attack survivors, offers refreshments.

Day 17 — Agra — Red Fort, Akbar's Mausoleum, and Overnight Train
The day is free for exploration. Early risers may return to the Taj Mahal at sunrise. The Red Fort, built in 1565 by Emperor Akbar on the banks of the Yamuna River and originally designed as a military structure, contains extensive architecture and courtyards. Akbar's Mausoleum is located further along the same region. In the evening, a 12-hour overnight sleeper train (third-class air-conditioned) departs for Varanasi.

Day 18 — Varanasi Arrival and Ganges Options
Arrival in Varanasi occurs in the morning. An auto-rickshaw transfers visitors to their hotel, followed by a guided walk with the local guide through the narrow alleyways of the Old City. The remainder of the day is free. Two evening options center on the Ganges River: a sunset boat cruise providing views of life along the water in fading daylight, or attendance at a Ganga aarti — a fire ceremony performed by local priests — at Dashashwamedh Ghat.

Day 19 — Varanasi — Ganges Ghats and Optional Sarnath
This day is unscheduled. An optional early-morning boat trip along the Ganges passes pilgrims bathing and praying along the colorful ghats. Walking to the ghats allows observation of dhobi-wallahs — clothes washers — drying textiles along the riverbank. The partially submerged Vishnu Temple near Manikarnika Ghat can be visited on foot. Sarnath, located approximately 10 kilometers outside the city, is the site where Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon after achieving enlightenment; the local guide can provide directions.

Day 20 — Varanasi Morning Exploration and Evening Train
Free time in the morning allows further exploration of Varanasi, including optional visits to the Vishwanath Temple or simply time spent eating chaat — a savory Indian snack — while observing daily life. The Kriti Gallery, displaying contemporary work by local artists, offers a quieter environment. In the afternoon, a 15-hour overnight train departs for Delhi.

Day 21 — Delhi — Arrival and Free Day
Arrival in Delhi occurs in late morning. A taxi carries travelers to the hotel. The remainder of the day is free to rest or wander at individual pace. The local guide can recommend dining options; group dinners are optional.

Day 22 — Delhi Departure
Your North India adventure concludes today. With no scheduled activities, you are free to depart your accommodation at any time that suits your onward travel plans.

tour.name: Off the beaten Family Adventure Tour of Sri Lanka
tour.subtitle: Chilaw - Habarana - Trincomalee - Ampara - Wasgamuwa - Kandy - Ella - Yala - Galle - Colombo
tour.summary: For families who enjoy nature, wildlife, beaches, culture and have the privilege of long holidays, this is the ultimate family adventure in Sri Lanka which covers highlights, off the beaten experiences, unique local experiences hosted by locals, wildlife encounters at the very heart of the wilderness, exploration of historical ruins & temples, Visit an Indigenous tribal village and also a beach stay in the east coast where you would be able to snorkel to explore the underwater wonders.
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 and 2 in Chilaw
Relax, explore Coconut plantation and chill by the pool. Stay in a Coconut Plantation Lodge.

Day 3, 4 and 5 in Habarana
Visit Monkeys in their Kingdom, explore historical ruined kingdoms and temples of Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa, Explore the rural villages in an open top jeep and take up the challenge of a treasure hunt in the jungle and village to interact with local communities. Stay in an Eco Lodge, in a Tree House.

Day 6, 7, 8 and 9 in Trincomalee
Unwind by the turquoise blue waters and sandy beaches of Trincomalee and snorkel the underwater wonders of Pigeon Island Marine Sanctuary. Stay in a comfortable resort by the beach.

Day 10 in Ampara
Explore the less visited yet exciting natural history of east coast and interact with tribal indigenous community. Stay in a family owned simple guest house.

Day 11 and 12 in Wasgamuwa
Learn about Elephant-Human conflict and stay in an Elephant Conservation centre for an in-depth understanding of this largest land mammal. Stay in a basic volunteer centre.

Day 13, 14 and 15 in Kandy
Trek through terraced rice fields and grassy plateaus of Knuckles mountains and observe centuries old pilgrimage rituals of the Islanders at The Temple of Tooth Relic. Unwind by the pool for a day, a family bonding. Stay in a family owned small hotel.

Day 16 and 17 in Ella
Scenic train journey, centuries old bridges and jaw dropping views of Ella Gap. Take an adventurous Tuk Tuk ride in the mist capped Tea plantation to learn about Ceylon Tea. Stay in a simple guest house.

Day 18 in Yala
Go canoeing in a scenic lake for sunset and take up a morning safari to see elusive Leopards of Yala National Park. Stay in Tented Safari Camp.

Day 19 and 20 in Galle
Explore historical Dutch Fort, release a baby Sea Turtle to the Ocean and unwind. Stay in a stylish boutique hotel.

Day 21 - Flight back home
An experiential journey comes to an end, a learning journey and quality time spent with your family. See you soon in Sri Lanka.

output.name: Sri Lanka: Coast, Kingdom & Wilderness — 21 Days
output.subtitle: Coconut plantations, ancient ruins, wildlife reserves, and east-coast snorkeling across three weeks
output.summary: This 21-day itinerary moves across Sri Lanka's varied terrain and inhabited regions — coconut estates along the west coast, the central highlands with their historical kingdoms and tea plantations, wildlife areas including an elephant conservation zone, and the eastern beaches. The route incorporates stays in small hotels, eco-lodges, guesthouses, and a tented safari camp, with private transfers throughout and local guides from the regions themselves. Activities span monastery visits, village interactions, jungle exploration, snorkeling in a marine sanctuary, train travel through mountain passes, and morning wildlife observation. The itinerary accommodates mixed groups and ages; specific excursions are suited to children eight and older. May through October represents the optimal travel window.
highlights: Monkeys in their natural habitat and the ancient rock fortress of Sigiriya in Habarana
Snorkeling in Pigeon Island Marine Sanctuary off Trincomalee's turquoise coastline
Interaction with Vedda indigenous community in the Ampara region
In-depth elephant conservation experience at Wasgamuwa, learning habitat and conflict dynamics
Trekking through the terraced valleys and grassy ridges of the Knuckles mountain range near Kandy
The Temple of the Tooth Relic in Kandy, site of centuries-old pilgrimage traditions
Train journey through tea plantations with views of Ella Gap in the south-central highlands
Morning safari in Yala National Park for leopard and wildlife observation
Dutch Fort exploration and sea-turtle hatchling release in Galle
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Chilaw: Coconut Plantation Lodge
Arrival in Chilaw, on Sri Lanka's west coast. The day involves settling into a coconut plantation lodge and initial orientation to the region.

Day 2 — Habarana: Monkeys, Ruins, and Jungle Treasure
Three days based in Habarana reveal the region's layered history and wildlife. Visit monkeys in their natural habitat, then visit the ruined kingdoms and temples of Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa by jeep. Open-top drives through rural villages lead to a jungle treasure hunt, offering genuine interaction with local communities. Nights are spent in an eco lodge tree house.

Day 3 — Habarana: Sigiriya, Polonnaruwa, and Village Exploration
Transfer to Habarana, in the central zone. The day includes visits to Sigiriya, a fifth-century rock fortress rising 200 meters from the central plain, and the medieval city of Polonnaruwa, where twelfth-century Buddhist temples and administrative structures remain amid paddy fields. An open-top jeep excursion through rural villages provides direct interaction with local farming communities. Accommodation is in an eco-lodge or tree-house setting.

Day 4 — Habarana: Primate Observation and Jungle Activities
Time spent observing monkey troops in their natural forest environment. A guided jungle and village treasure hunt offers physical challenge and further local community contact. Evening pool time at the lodge.

Day 5 — Habarana: Further Temple and Historical Exploration
Additional temple and historical site exploration in the Habarana region, with focus on sites not covered on Day 3. Return to the eco-lodge.

Day 6 — Transfer to Trincomalee and Coastal Settlement
Travel northeastward to Trincomalee, on the east coast. The day centers on arrival and settlement into a beachfront resort. Introduction to the turquoise waters and sandy beaches of the region.

Day 7 — Trincomalee: Pigeon Island Snorkeling
Full-day snorkeling excursion to Pigeon Island Marine Sanctuary. The sanctuary protects coral reef systems and tropical fish populations visible from the surface and during shallow dives. Return to the resort in Trincomalee.

Day 8 — Trincomalee: Coastal Swimming and Rest
A day of beach time, swimming, and rest by the resort. Optional further snorkeling or exploration of Trincomalee town.

Day 9 — Trincomalee: Beach and Leisure
Final day of coastal time in Trincomalee, allowing further beach and water-based activity or relaxation at the resort.

Day 10 — Ampara: Vedda Community and East-Coast Natural History
Transfer southward to Ampara, on the less-visited east coast. The region offers distinct natural and cultural features. Engagement with Vedda indigenous community is arranged through a family-operated guesthouse, which serves as accommodation base.

Day 11 — Wasgamuwa: Elephant Conservation Center Arrival
Transfer to Wasgamuwa, a wildlife area in the interior. Accommodation is at a volunteer-based elephant conservation center. Initial orientation covers elephant biology, habitat needs, and the nature of human-wildlife conflict in Sri Lanka's protected zones.

Day 12 — Wasgamuwa: Elephant Conservation Study
Full-day engagement at the conservation center, including direct observation of elephants in the sanctuary, discussion of conflict-mitigation strategies, and understanding of the center's research and care protocols.

Day 13 — Kandy: Knuckles Mountain Trekking and Rice Terraces
Transfer to Kandy. Trekking through the Knuckles mountain range incorporates passes through terraced rice fields and grassy plateaus. The landscape rises to modest elevations and offers views across the central highlands. Accommodation is in a small, family-owned hotel.

Day 14 — Kandy: Temple of the Tooth Relic and Pilgrimage Observation
Visit to the Temple of the Tooth Relic, a major Buddhist pilgrimage site housing a relic venerated for centuries. The day observes active worship rituals and the temple's architectural and religious significance. Pool time at the hotel provides afternoon leisure.

Day 15 — Kandy: Mountain Walks and Highlands Exploration
Further trekking or exploration of the Kandy highlands, depending on group preference. Pool time and leisure at the hotel.

Day 16 — Ella: Train Journey Through Tea Plantations
A scenic train journey southeastward to Ella carries travelers through tea-growing regions and crosses nineteenth-century colonial-era bridges. Views encompass layered landscape and mountain terrain. Accommodation is in a simple guesthouse in Ella.

Day 17 — Ella: Tea Plantations and Ella Gap
Exploration of tea plantations in the immediate area around Ella, accessible by local transport. Views of Ella Gap, the pronounced notch in the southern mountain range, dominate the day's vistas. Further walks or rest at the guesthouse.

Day 18 — Yala National Park: Leopards and Sunset Canoeing
Morning safari through scrub forest and grassland searching for leopards and wildlife. Evening canoe on a scenic lake captures sunset and birdlife. Stay at tented safari camp.

Day 19 — Galle: Dutch Fort and Sea Turtle Release
Visit the seventeenth-century Dutch Fort with its intact walls and colonial architecture. Release a baby sea turtle to the ocean through a local conservation program. Settle into a boutique hotel for the evening.

Day 20 — Galle: Coastal Exploration and Rest
Final beach day in Galle, allowing further fort exploration, coastal walks, or rest at the hotel.

Day 21 — Departure from Sri Lanka
Final morning at leisure, then transfer to the airport for departure. The journey spans coconut plantations, ancient kingdoms, wildlife reserves, mountain terrain, and east and south-coast settings, with stays in small local hotels, eco-lodges, guesthouses, and a safari camp.

tour.name: Lower Dolpa Trek – 19 days
tour.summary:
The Lower Dolpa Trek is an extraordinary adventure that delves into one of Nepal’s most remote and untouched regions. Situated in the far-western part of Nepal, this trek offers a rare opportunity to explore an isolated area renowned for its stunning landscapes and unique cultural heritage. The trek provides a fascinating blend of dramatic scenery, high-altitude terrain, and traditional Tibetan-influenced communities.

The journey typically begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, followed by another flight or a lengthy drive to Juphal, the starting point of the trek. From Juphal, you’ll begin your trek, winding through charming villages, terraced fields, and lush green forests. This initial part of the trek offers a gentle introduction to the region’s natural beauty.

One of the key highlights of the Lower Dolpa Trek is the exploration of Shey Phoksundo National Park. The park is home to Shey Phoksundo Lake, Nepal’s largest lake, known for its striking turquoise color and serene setting. The lake, set against a backdrop of snow-capped peaks and steep cliffs, creates a breathtaking vista. A visit to the lake also includes exploring the surrounding areas, such as the impressive Phoksundo Waterfall, one of the highest in Nepal.

As the trek progresses, you’ll traverse a diverse range of landscapes. The lower elevations feature verdant valleys and terraced farmland, while higher altitudes present arid, desert-like environments. This contrast between lush and barren landscapes adds to the trek’s visual and experiential diversity.

The Lower Dolpa region is also rich in cultural heritage. The trek takes you through traditional Tibetan-influenced villages where local customs and lifestyles have remained largely unchanged. The architecture, monasteries, and daily activities reflect a unique blend of Tibetan and Nepali cultures. Engaging with the local communities offers valuable insights into their traditional practices and way of life.

The trek involves navigating challenging terrain, including steep ascents and descents, as well as high-altitude passes. Proper acclimatization is crucial to cope with the demands of the trek. Despite these challenges, the rewards are significant, with spectacular views and a profound sense of achievement.

Typically lasting around 15 to 20 days, the Lower Dolpa Trek provides ample time to explore the region thoroughly. The relatively long duration allows trekkers to fully appreciate the beauty of the landscapes and the richness of the cultural experiences.

Overall, the Lower Dolpa Trek is a remarkable adventure for those seeking a remote and immersive trekking experience. Its combination of stunning natural beauty, diverse landscapes, and rich cultural encounters makes it an unforgettable journey through one of Nepal’s most secluded regions. Whether you’re drawn to the allure of Shey Phoksundo Lake, the challenge of high-altitude trekking, or the chance to experience traditional Tibetan culture, the Lower Dolpa Trek offers an exceptional and memorable adventure in the heart of the Himalayas.
highlights:
Trek along the scenic Bheri River corridor, passing charming villages, terraced fields, gorges, and suspension bridges
Explore Tarakot — an ancient fortress village with deep historical roots as a strategic stronghold
Trek through forested trails of wild roses and juniper bushes to reach Dho Tarap — a historic trade hub between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom
Acclimatization day in Dho Tarap (4,050m) — essential preparation before tackling two high-altitude passes above 5,000m
Cross the mighty Numa La Pass (5,180m) — with breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Dhaulagiri and the Churen Himal ranges
Cross the second challenging Baga La Pass (5,170m) — rewarded with sweeping Himalayan vistas and a first glimpse of the stunning Phoksundo Lake below
Arrive at Ringmo village, home to the rare and endangered Bon religion — one of Nepal's most unique and ancient spiritual traditions
Marvel at the legendary Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,730m) — Nepal's largest lake, famous for its mesmerizing deep turquoise color, towering cliffs, and snow-capped backdrop
Dedicated rest and exploration day at Phoksundo Lake — discover the Phoksundo Waterfall, one of Nepal's highest, and immerse in Bon culture
Fully tented camp experience throughout the entire trek — a true wilderness expedition
A contingency day in Kathmandu built in to protect against weather-dependent mountain flight disruptions
A comprehensive 19-day itinerary — ideal for seasoned trekkers seeking an extreme, culturally rich, and deeply rewarding Himalayan adventure
tour.itineraries:
Day 1: ARRIVAL IN KATHMANDU
At an arrival at the international airport we will be picked up and then transferred to the hotel. Check in at the hotel and stay overnight.

Day 2: FLY KATHMANDU TO NEPALGUNJ [ 1 HRS; / 150 METERS, 492 FT]
Set off from Kathmandu in the early morning to catch the flight to Nepalgunj. After an hour long flight to Nepalgunj and upon arrival at Nepalgunj airport you will be received by the trekking crew and be transferred to Hotel Batika in Nepalgunj. The overnight stay will be at hotel Batika in Nepalgunj. We can spend some time in the city of Nepalgunj exploring the city and the local markets and shops.

Day 3: FLY NEPALGUNJ TO JUPHAL & TREK TO DUNAI [35 MINS - FLIGHT, 3-4 HRS. / 2150 METERS, 7053 FT.]
Fly to Juphal for about 35 minutes in a STOL airport. Then we get our gears ready and set out for the first day of our trek to Dunai village and pass through the small villages and terraced fields down to the Bheri River. We move along the riverside and and reach the Dunai village. Overnight stay will be at the local tea houses/lodges.

Day 4: TREK DUNAI TO TARAKOT [TREK : 5-6 HRS, 10 KM, 2550 METERS /8336 FT.]
From Dunai we will trek through the terraced fields, gorges, suspension bridges and scattered villages through our trail to the Tarakot village. In the local Nepali language, Kot means Fort and Tarakot village also acted as a fort in the ancient times. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 5: TREK TARAKOT TO LAHINI KHARKA [4-5 HRS. TREK; / 3450 METERS, 11318 FT.]
From Tarakot village we follow the trail through the river and reach the Lahini Kharka. A cave called Lahini Odar is in close proximity. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 6: TREK LAHINI KHARKA TO THULO ODAR [4-5 HRS. TREK; / 3550 METERS, 14435 FT.]
Make a short trek from Lahini Kharka/ Odar to Thulo Odar (3550m) and overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 7: TREK THULO ODAR TO DHO TARAP [TREK; 5-6 HRS / 4050 METERS, 13288 FT.]
Our trail passes through the forested path covered with wild roses and juniper bushes before it reaches the Dho Tarap village.. Dho Tarap in ancient times used to be a hub for trade between, Tibet and Mustang Kingdoms. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 8: DHOTARAP ACCLIMATIZATION DAY [4050 METERS, 13288 FT.]
it is the only time during our trek when we stopover for acclimatization. As we will be crossing two high altitude pass above 5000 meters we need to ensure our body and lungs are ready to do so. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 9: TREK DHO TARAP TO NUMA LA BASE CAMP [TREK; 4 HRS. 8 KM / 4350 METERS, 14271 FT.]
Our trek continues to the Numa La Base Camp through the rugged terrain. On reaching Numa La Base Camp we will Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 10: TREK NUMALA BASE CAMP TO DANIGAR VIA NUMA LA PASS [TREK; 18 KM, 7-8 HRS. / 4550 METERS, 14927 FT.]
It is a long and strenuous day of the trek because on this day we will cross the 1st mountain pass of our trek, the Numa La Pass (5180 meteres, 16995 Ft) and from the top we can witness the majestic panoramic view of himalayan ranges including the Mt. Dhaulagiri and Churen Himal ranges. Then we trek a long way down to the Danigar village. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 11: TREK DANIGAR TO ROMAN KHARKA VIA BAGA LA PASS [TREK; 6 HRS, 19 KM / 4000 METERS, 13123 FT.]
This is another strenuous day of our trek we will be crossing another high altitude pass. After leaving the Danigar village, we will be leaving behind Danigar village and then, we head towards Roman Kharka also popularly known as Yak Kharka. To reach Roman Kharka we need to cross the Baga La Pass (5170 meters, 16961 feet) . We can see the view of Himalayan vistas and also the Beutiful Phoksundo lake from the Baga La Pass. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 12: TREK ROMAN KHARKA TO PHOKSUNDO LAKE [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 3730 METERS, 9383 FT.]
From Roman Kharka we will now head towards one of our major attraction of the trek, the Phoksundo Lake. We will reach Ringmo village. Like Luphra in Mustang, Ringmo village is popular for its endangered Bon religion. A short walk from Ringmo leads us to the beautiful turquoise colored Phoksundo Lake. Overnight stay will be at the tented camp.

Day 13: PHOKSUNDO LAKE EXPLORATION [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 3730 METERS, 8760 FT.]
It is a rest day at the Phoksundo Lake to explore the lake surroundings and the Ringmo village. Bon religion is an endangered religion that is still being followed in this Ringmo village, so we can spend the day getting awed by the beauty of the Phoksundo Lake as well as getting to know the Bon religion being followed in the village. Our overnight at tented camp.

Day 14: TREK PHOKSUNDO LAKE TO CHHEPKA [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 2670 METERS, 8760 FT.]
From Phoksundo Lake we trek down to Chhepka village. Before reaching Chhepka village we pass through the Chunuwar and Rechi Village. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 15: TREK CHHEPKA TO JUPHAL [TREK; 6-7 HRS. 18 KM / 2499 METERS, 8198 FT.]
This is the final day of our trek we pass through the Shyangta, Kageni and other small villages before we reach Juphal.

Day 16: FLIGHT TO NEPALGUNJ [FLIGHT; 35 MINUTES ]
After completion of our lower Dolpo trek we will then head to Nepalgunj. . You can use the free time on this day on your disposal for personal activities.

Day 17: FLIGHT BACK TO KATHMANDU [FLIGHT; 1 HRS. ]
After spending a day in Nepalgunj, we will take approx. 1 hrs flight to Kathmandu. You can use the free time on this day on your disposal for personal activities.

Day 18: REST DAY IN KATHMANDU
it is a contingency day in Kathmandu as an precaution to the Juphal Nepalgunj sector flight. As the flight to high mountain regions are highly dependent on weather conditions there might cancellation in flights due to bad weather. So contingency day helps us to ensure we dont miss the international flight. This day can be used for personal activities, shopping and also some sightseeing around the monument sites of Kathmandu valley.

Day 19: DEPARTURE

output.name: Lower Dolpa Trek: Shey Phoksundo Lake & the High Passes of Far-Western Nepal — 19 Days
output.subtitle: Juphal to Phoksundo Lake via Numa La (5,180m) and Baga La (5,170m) passes — 19 days through Shey Phoksundo National Park
output.summary:
The Lower Dolpa Trek covers one of Nepal's most geographically and culturally isolated corridors, traveling from the small STOL airstrip at Juphal through the Bheri River valley, over two passes above 5,000 meters, and down to Shey Phoksundo Lake at 3,730 meters — Nepal's largest lake. The 19-day itinerary is structured around the logistical realities of the region: flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, then onward to Juphal, where the trek begins in earnest through terraced farmland and river gorges before the terrain shifts into the arid, high-altitude plateau country of Upper Dolpa's doorstep.

The route passes through Tarakot, an ancient fortified village, and Dho Tarap at 4,050 meters — historically a trade junction between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom — where a full acclimatization day is built in before the two major passes. Numa La (5,180m) delivers panoramic sightlines to Dhaulagiri and the Churen Himal ranges; Baga La (5,170m), crossed the following day, marks the first view of Phoksundo Lake from above. The lake itself, set beneath steep cliffs and surrounded by snow-covered ridges, is reached via Ringmo village, where the Bon religion — predating Tibetan Buddhism — remains in active practice.

The return follows a different line through Chhepka and back to Juphal, with flights retracing the Nepalgunj–Kathmandu axis. A contingency day in Kathmandu is built into the itinerary to account for the weather-dependent nature of mountain flights in this sector. Throughout the trek, accommodation is fully tented camp, consistent with the absence of lodge infrastructure in the more remote sections of the route.
highlights: Multi-day trekking along the Bheri River corridor, passing terraced fields, gorges, and suspension bridges between Juphal and Dunai
Exploration of Tarakot village, an ancient fortified settlement occupying a strategic position above the river trail
Arrival at Dho Tarap (4,050m), a former Tibet–Mustang trade hub reached through forested trails of wild roses and juniper
Full acclimatization day at Dho Tarap (4,050m) before two consecutive passes above 5,000 meters
Crossing Numa La Pass (5,180m) with direct views of Dhaulagiri and the Churen Himal ranges
Crossing Baga La Pass (5,170m) and first sightline down to Phoksundo Lake from the ridge
Arrival at Ringmo village, where the Bon religion — one of Nepal's oldest surviving spiritual traditions — remains in active practice
Phoksundo Lake (3,730m): Nepal's largest lake, with deep turquoise water set beneath vertical cliffs and snow-covered peaks
Dedicated rest and exploration day at Phoksundo Lake, including access to the Phoksundo Waterfall
Fully tented camp accommodation throughout the trek, reflecting the absence of lodge infrastructure in the remote sections
Built-in Kathmandu contingency day (Day 18) to protect against weather-related flight disruptions on the Juphal–Nepalgunj sector
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kathmandu: Airport Transfer and Hotel Check-In
On arrival at Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport, the group is met and transferred to the hotel for check-in and overnight.

Day 2 — Kathmandu to Nepalgunj by Air (150m / 492ft)
An early morning flight from Kathmandu takes approximately one hour to reach Nepalgunj, in the Terai lowlands of far-western Nepal. On arrival, the trekking crew meets the group and transfers everyone to Hotel Batika. The remainder of the day is free to walk through Nepalgunj's local markets and streets before overnight at the hotel.

Day 3 — Nepalgunj to Juphal by Air, then Trek to Dunai (2,150m / 7,053ft)
A 35-minute mountain flight on a STOL aircraft lands at Juphal airstrip. From there, the first trekking day begins through small villages and terraced fields, descending to the Bheri River and following the riverbank to Dunai village. The walk takes approximately 3–4 hours. Overnight is at local teahouses or lodges in Dunai.

Day 4 — Dunai to Tarakot Along the Bheri River Gorge (2,550m / 8,336ft)
The trail out of Dunai crosses terraced farmland and passes through scattered villages, traversing gorges and suspension bridges over approximately 10 km and 5–6 hours of walking. The destination, Tarakot, occupies the site of an ancient fortified settlement — the Nepali word 'kot' means fort — and the village retains its historically strategic position above the river corridor. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 5 — Tarakot to Lahini Kharka via the River Trail (3,450m / 11,318ft)
From Tarakot, the route follows the river trail to Lahini Kharka. A cave known locally as Lahini Odar lies close to the campsite. The walk takes 4–5 hours. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 6 — Trek Lahini Kharka to Thulo Odar
A short trek of 4–5 hours ascends from Lahini Kharka to Thulo Odar, situated at 3,550 meters. The route offers gradual elevation gain through alpine terrain. Overnight accommodation is at a tented camp.

Day 7 — Thulo Odar to Dho Tarap Through Juniper and Wild Rose Forest (4,050m / 13,288ft)
The trail to Dho Tarap passes through forested terrain covered with wild roses and juniper before opening onto the village at 4,050 meters. Dho Tarap served historically as a trade junction between Tibet and the Mustang Kingdom, and its architecture and cultural character reflect that cross-border heritage. The walk takes approximately 5–6 hours. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 8 — Acclimatization Day at Dho Tarap (4,050m / 13,288ft)
A full rest day at Dho Tarap is the only scheduled acclimatization stop on the itinerary. The following two days involve crossing passes above 5,000 meters, and the day at altitude here allows the body to adjust before those demanding sections. The village itself can be explored during the day. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 9 — Dho Tarap to Numa La Base Camp (4,350m / 14,271ft)
The route continues across rugged terrain for approximately 8 km over 4 hours to reach Numa La Base Camp at 4,350 meters, in preparation for the following day's pass crossing. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 10 — Numa La Base Camp to Danigar via Numa La Pass (5,180m / 16,995ft) — 18 km
The longest and most demanding day of the trek covers approximately 18 km over 7–8 hours. The route climbs to Numa La Pass at 5,180 meters, where clear conditions provide panoramic views across the Dhaulagiri massif and the Churen Himal ranges to the south and east. The descent from the pass is extended, dropping to Danigar village at 4,550 meters. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 11 — Danigar to Roman Kharka via Baga La Pass (5,170m / 16,961ft) — 19 km
A second consecutive high-pass day covers 19 km over approximately 6 hours. Leaving Danigar, the route climbs to Baga La Pass at 5,170 meters — also referred to as Yak Kharka in local usage — where the first aerial view of Phoksundo Lake becomes visible below to the west. Wide Himalayan panoramas open across the ridge before the descent leads to Roman Kharka at 4,000 meters. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 12 — Roman Kharka to Phoksundo Lake via Ringmo Village (3,730m / 12,237ft) — 18 km
The 18 km descent over 6–7 hours brings the route down to Ringmo village, where the Bon religion — one of Nepal's oldest surviving spiritual traditions, predating the spread of Tibetan Buddhism — remains in active practice among the local community. A short walk from Ringmo reaches the shore of Phoksundo Lake, with its characteristically deep turquoise water. Overnight at tented camp beside the lake.

Day 13 — Rest and Exploration Day at Phoksundo Lake and Ringmo Village (3,730m)
A full day at Phoksundo Lake allows time to walk the lake perimeter, visit the Phoksundo Waterfall — one of the highest in Nepal — and spend time in Ringmo village learning about Bon religious practice, which continues here in monasteries and in daily community life. The lake sits at 3,730 meters, backed by steep cliffs and high snow-covered ridgelines. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 14 — Phoksundo Lake to Chhepka via Chunuwar and Rechi (2,670m / 8,760ft)
The return route descends from Phoksundo Lake through Chunuwar and Rechi villages before reaching Chhepka at 2,670 meters. The walk takes approximately 6–7 hours over 18 km. Overnight at tented camp.

Day 15 — Chhepka to Juphal via Shyangta and Kageni Villages (2,499m / 8,198ft)
The final trekking day follows approximately 18 km over 6–7 hours through Shyangta, Kageni, and further small villages before arriving back at Juphal, the airstrip settlement where the trek began. Overnight at Juphal.

Day 16 — Juphal to Nepalgunj by Air (35-Minute Flight)
A 35-minute mountain flight from Juphal returns the group to Nepalgunj. The remainder of the day is at leisure for personal activities.

Day 17 — Nepalgunj to Kathmandu by Air (1-Hour Flight)
An approximately one-hour flight from Nepalgunj returns the group to Kathmandu. The remainder of the day is free for personal activities or rest.

Day 18 — Kathmandu: Contingency Day for Mountain Flight Disruptions
This day functions as a scheduled buffer against weather-related flight cancellations on the Juphal–Nepalgunj sector, which is susceptible to disruption due to high-altitude weather conditions. If the itinerary has proceeded without delays, the day is available for sightseeing at Kathmandu Valley monument sites, personal shopping, or rest before the international departure the following morning.

Day 19 — Kathmandu: International Departure
An airport representative assists with checkout and escorts the group to Tribhuvan International Airport for onward departure from Nepal.

tour.name: K2 BC Concordia Trek via Gondogoro La
tour.summary: Take on one of the most epic and demanding treks on earth — a 20-day odyssey through the Karakoram's crown jewels via the legendary Gondogoro La high pass. Journey deep along the mighty Baltoro Glacier through a corridor of soaring granite towers to reach Concordia, the breathtaking amphitheater of 8,000m giants. Stand at K2 Base Camp, pay tribute at the Gilkey Memorial, then push higher over the formidable Gondogoro La at 5,610m — one of the world's most spectacular high-altitude crossings — descending through wildflower meadows and cedar valleys to Hushe. A truly once-in-a-lifetime adventure reserved for the bold and well-prepared.
highlights:
Trekking the legendary Baltoro Glacier: 62km of ice flanked by Cathedral Towers, Trango Towers and Gasherbrum IV
Reaching sacred Concordia at 4,650m: 360-degree panorama of four 8,000m peaks including the mighty K2
Visiting K2 Base Camp & Gilkey Memorial: tribute site to fallen climbers, vibrant expedition atmosphere in peak season
Overnighting at Broad Peak Base Camp: the closest and most dramatic face-to-face view of K2
Conquering the Gondogoro La at 5,610m: strenuous high-altitude crossing with unparalleled Karakoram panoramas
Descending through Dalzampa's field of flowers: wild roses, cedar, tamarisk and jagged glacial spires
Finishing through Hushe Valley: gateway village of legendary high-altitude porters and guides
tour.itineraries:
Day 01: Islamabad 
Arrive in Islamabad. Meet guide & transfer to the hotel. In the morning take rest to recover from the long flight, in the afternoon Rawalpindi / Islamabad city tour. 
Sightseeing tour in Islamabad will consist of a selection of some of the following sites (depending on available time & your interests): the Faisal Mosque, the Government buildings 
on Constitution Avenue, the Shakar Parian Park with its rose and jasmine garden, the Pakistan Monument, the Lok Virsa heritage museum, Raja Bazaar area in Rawalpindi, Saidpur village Daman-e-Koh to look out over the twin cities. 
Overnight in Islamabad. 

Day 02: Islamabad – Skardu (2300m) 
Transfer to the airport for flight to Skardu. If the weather is clear we will have the opportunity to see some of the majestic mountains of the north from the airplane window incl. Nanga Parbat. In case of flight cancellation we will drive in two days on the famous KKH to Skardu. Trek briefing at Skardu Tourism Department either today or tomorrow. 
Optional: drive to Chilas and then add 2 days to visit Fairy Meadows. 

Day 03: Skardu 
Free day at leisure or drive to Skardu from Chilas. 
Optional sightseeing: Sadpara Lake, Skardu Bazaar, Kharpocho (Skardu) Fort.

Day 04: Skardu – Askoli (3000m) – Jhola (3140m) After breakfast proceed to Jhola in jeeps. It takes about six hours to drive from Skardu to Askoli. Askoli is the last village of Shigar valley, this used to be the starting point for the K2 Concordia trek but recently they have extended the road up to Jhola. The drive through the Braldu Gorge is guaranteed to knock your socks off! We will have lunch on the way, dinner will be in the camp, overnight in tents. 

Day 05: Jhola – Paju (3450m) 
We start on a relatively easy trail for 3 – 4 hours crossing Burdumal campsites along a 2 km stretched sandy river beach. After lunch continue towards Paju for another 2 – 3 hours trek. The trail climbs to a vantage point providing a view of the Snout of Baltoro. In the far distance you can see a magnificent panorama of the Cathedral Towers, Paju can be a crowded campsite. Overnight in camp. 

Day 06: Rest day at Paju (3450m) 
Rest day at Paju for local exploration. Enjoy the traditional music program and dancing by the local porters and other staff of the trekking teams. Overnight in camp. 

Day 07: Paju – Khuburse (3930m) 
Start trekking for 5 – 8 hours. Gradual climb of Baltoro Glacier on the Southern edge. After about 2 hours the path divides at the snout of Baltoro Glacier where the left branch goes to the Base camp of Trango Towers and the Serpo Liligo Pass. Continue to the right climbing up on to the glacier that stretches up the valley 62 km long and 2 km wide. Further 2 – 3 hours steady climb on a long diagonal to the other side. Follow the southern edge to Liliwa and onward to Khuburse – a lovely walk for about 90 min. to the campsite with clear water. Overnight at camp. 

Day 08: Khuburse – Urdukas (4050m) 
4 -5 hours walking, mostly along the crest of lateral moraine with stunning views of Paju Peak, Chorichi Biaho, Trango Tower and so on. Urdukas is a spectacular campsite. Overnight in a tent.

Day 09: Urdukas – Ghoro II (4380m) 
6 – 8 hours walking on a glacier. The first hour of our walk is across difficult terrain with many crevasses; however the way is smoother and easier in the middle. Continue 2 – 3 hours to Ghoro I opposite of Yermanendo Glacier, falling down from the Masherbrum Pass. For the next 3 – 4 hours continue east up the Baltoro Glacier following the telephone wire from Army HQ Ghoro to Gasherbrum IV. Ghoro II campsite is pitched on the rocks and ice in the centre of the glacier with water from the glacier melt. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 10: Ghoro II – Concordia (4650m) 
5 – 6 hours of relatively easy walking with spectacular views and gigantic mountain panorama, including Mustagata Tower, G IV, Matha Peak and the mighty K2. Camp at Concordia named by Martin Conway after the place Dela Concordia in Paris. Overnight in tent. 

Day 11: Concordia – Broad Peak BC (4850m) 
When we leave Concordia we first have to go through a more difficult part where two different glaciers (the Baltoro and Godwin- Austen glaciers) meet, then it is about a 3 hours fairly easy walk over the Godwin-Austen glacier to the base camp of Broad Peak. From the base camp you have an even more spectacular view of the K2 than from Concordia, we set up camp here, the rest of the day the group can take it easy and maybe get something from the different expedition groups. 

Day 12 – Broad Peak BC – K2 BC – Concordia (4650m) 
We leave early towards K2 base camp, about 3 hours walk, on arrival we visit the Gilkey memorial where deceased climbers are commemorated. In June and July there are many expeditions to the K2, the base camp will therefore be very lively and during the visit the group may get a bit of the "expedition atmosphere". After lunch we walk over the Godwin-Austen Glacier the same way back to Concordia (about 5 – 6 hours walk). 

Day 13: Concordia – Ali Camp Vigne Glacier (5010m) 
5 -6 hours continuous walk on Vigne Glacier, providing superb views of Chogolisa and Mitre peak. A rare mountain panorama and the camp will be just below the pass. Overnight in a tent.

Day 14: Vigne Glacier Ali Camp – Gondogoro La (5610) – Khuspang (4680) 
4 - 5 hours, we start very early in the morning for the strenuous and steep ascend to Gondogoro La (high pass), then another 3 – 4 hours descend to the high camp (Khuspang) on the other side. Also BC for Gondogoro Peak. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 15: Khuspang – Dalzampa (4300m) OR (RESERVE DAY) We can make this a reserve day, which means we can skip this part if required. 
From Khuspang to Saicho. 4 – 5 hours easy descend of glacier Moraine to the beautiful campsite of Dalzampa “field of flowers”. A climb to the lateral Moraine provides spectacular views of the glacier and jagged spires. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 16: Dalzampa – Shaicho (3330m) 
Another 4 – 5 hours walk on the lateral moraine through wild roses, gooseberry cedar and Tamarisk bushes. The Charakusa valley joins the Gondogoro at Shaicho and the route leads towards the base camp of K6 and K7. Overnight in a tent. 

Day 17: Shaicho – Hushe (3050m) – Skardu (2300m) This is the last day of the trek, for 4 – 5 hours we follow the east bank of the Hushe River on an easy path through the fields until reaching the village. From here we drive to Skardu by jeep and will make a short stop at Khaplu, the second largest kingdom of old Baltistan guarding the trade route to Ladakh along the Shyok River. Overnight at a hotel in Skardu. Trek debriefing at Skardu Tourism Department.

Day 18: Skardu – Chilas (or Naran) or Islamabad 
It’s time to say goodbye to the beautiful Baltistan region, today we drive to Chilas (or further to Naran) – a small bazaar town from where we can glimpse petroglyphs dating to the 1st century BC. Before reaching Chilas we will make some short photo stops, for example at the junction where the the 3 highest mountain ranges meet (The Himalayas, The Karakoram and The Hindu Kush) as well as at the Nanga Parbat viewpoint. 
In case of preference, it is possible (for the whole group) to fly to Islamabad instead of drive – 1 hour flight, rest of the afternoon can be spend at leisure. Transfer to Skardu airport for the flight to Islamabad, in case of flight cancellation we will drive to Chilas (or Naran) for 
overnight stay and next day onwards to Islamabad. 

Day 19: Chilas (or Naran) – Islamabad or Islamabad 
If the Babusar Pass is open then we will drive from Chilas via the Kaghan Valley and Naran towards Islamabad otherwise we will go over the famous Karakoram Highway (KKH) to Islamabad – this will be a full day of driving but the diverse scenery will make it a nice journey. On arrival in Islamabad we will have a nice farewell dinner and then take rest or have a full overnight stay in the hotel (depending on your flight departure time the next day). 
If we got a flight to Islamabad yesterday then we can spend today at leisure or have some additional sightseeing / souvenir shopping in Islamabad or (at extra charges) go for a day trip to Taxila to see the Taxila museum and various archaeological sites with remnants from the Buddhist Gandhara Kindgom. In case of flight cancellation on day 18 then today we will drive from Chilas to Islamabad. Farewell dinner and take a rest or full overnight stay in hotel. (depending on your flight departure time the next day). 

Day 20: Onward flight 
Midnight / early morning transfer to the airport for return flight home. End of Our Services –
We Hope You Had a Great Trip!

The route passes K2 Base Camp and the Gilkey Memorial, then climbs to the formidable Gondogoro La at 5,610 meters — a high pass requiring alpine fitness and acclimatization discipline — before descending through wildflower meadows and cedar valleys to the Hushe Valley.
