Day 1 — Arrival in Islamabad & Twin Cities Overview
Arrive in Islamabad and meet your guide for transfer to the hotel. The morning is reserved for rest and recovery from your flight. In the afternoon, visit Islamabad and Rawalpindi at a measured pace. Depending on your interests and available time, the sightseeing may include the Faisal Mosque, Government buildings on Constitution Avenue, Shakar Parian Park with its rose and jasmine gardens, the Pakistan Monument, the Lok Virsa heritage museum, Raja Bazaar in Rawalpindi, Saidpur village, and Daman-e-Koh for views across the twin cities. Transfer to the airport for a domestic flight to Skardu at 2,300 meters. Clear weather often permits views of Nanga Parbat and other northern ranges from the aircraft. In the event of flight cancellation, the route switches to a two-day overland journey via the Karakoram Highway. Trek briefing at the Skardu Tourism Department occurs today or the following day. An optional extension to Fairy Meadows via Chilas can be added with two additional days. Overnight in Skardu.

Day 3 — Rest Day in Skardu
Free day in Skardu. Optional sightseeing includes Sadpara Lake, Skardu Bazaar, and Kharpocho Fort. Overnight in Skardu.

Day 4 — Skardu to Jhola via the Braldu Gorge
After breakfast, a six-hour jeep journey departs for Jhola at 3,140 meters via Askoli. The road ascends through the Braldu Gorge, a steep and dramatic canyon, to Askoli — historically the trekking trail's starting point but now extended to Jhola by vehicle. Lunch occurs en route. Camp and overnight in tents at Jhola.

Day 5 — Jhola to Paju: Entry onto Baltoro
A relatively easy 5–7 hour trek begins across Burdumal campsites, following a sandy river beach for 2 kilometers. The route then climbs toward Paju at 3,450 meters over 2–3 hours. A vantage point near Paju provides views of the Baltoro Glacier snout and a distant panorama of the Cathedral Towers. Paju is a frequently crowded campsite. Overnight in tents.

Day 6 — Rest Day at Paju
Rest day at Paju for local exploration and acclimatization. The camp includes a traditional music and dance program by local porters and trekking staff. Overnight in tents.

Day 7 — Paju to Khuburse: Ascending the Baltoro Glacier
A 5–8 hour trek begins with a gradual climb along the southern edge of the Baltoro Glacier. After approximately two hours, the path divides at the glacier snout; the route continues right onto the main Baltoro, which stretches 62 kilometers long and 2 kilometers wide. A long diagonal ascent climbs to the glacier's far side over 2–3 hours. The southern edge is followed to Liliwa and onward to Khuburse at 3,930 meters, a 90-minute walk with clear glacial meltwater. Overnight in tents.

Day 8 — Khuburse to Urdukas: Lateral Moraine Traverse
A 4–5 hour walk follows the crest of lateral moraine, offering views of Paju Peak, Chorichi Biaho, and Trango Tower. Urdukas at 4,050 meters is a spectacular campsite. Overnight in tents.

Day 9 — Urdukas to Ghoro II: Upper Baltoro Crossing
A 6–8 hour glacier traverse begins with difficult, crevassed terrain for approximately one hour, then transitions to smoother ground mid-glacier. After 2–3 hours, Ghoro I sits opposite the Yermanendo Glacier, which descends from Masherbrum Pass. The route continues east up the main Baltoro for 3–4 hours, following an Army HQ telephone wire toward Gasherbrum IV. Ghoro II at 4,380 meters is a rocky and icy campsite in the glacier's center, with water from glacial melt. Overnight in tents.

Day 10 — Ghoro II to Concordia: Amphitheater of 8,000-Meter Peaks
A 5–6 hour relatively easy walk leads across the upper Baltoro with expanding panoramic views. Concordia at 4,650 meters lies at the convergence of multiple glaciers and opens to a 360-degree vista of K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II, and surrounding peaks. Named by mountaineer Martin Conway after the Piazza della Concordia in Rome, the site is a natural amphitheater. Overnight in tents.

Day 11 — Concordia to Broad Peak Base Camp
Departure from Concordia requires passage through difficult terrain where the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers meet. A 3-hour generally easy walk follows the Godwin-Austen Glacier to Broad Peak Base Camp at 4,850 meters. This elevated site offers an even more direct view of K2's north face than Concordia. The afternoon allows rest and informal interaction with other expedition groups. Overnight in tents.

Day 12 — K2 Base Camp Visit and Return to Concordia
An early departure leads to K2 Base Camp, approximately 3 hours distant. Upon arrival, the group visits the Gilkey Memorial, where fallen mountaineers are commemorated. During June and July, numerous climbing expeditions operate from the base camp, creating visible expedition activity and atmosphere. Following lunch, the return walk to Concordia retraces the Godwin-Austen Glacier over 5–6 hours. Overnight in tents at Concordia.

Day 13 — Concordia to Ali Camp: Vigne Glacier Approach
A 5–6 hour continuous walk on Vigne Glacier offers extended views of Chogolisa and Mitre Peak. The rare mountain panorama continues to expand. Ali Camp at 5,010 meters is positioned just below the Gondogoro La. Overnight in tents.

Day 14 — Crossing the Gondogoro La
An early start begins a strenuous 4–5 hour ascent to the Gondogoro La at 5,610 meters — a high-altitude pass requiring alpine fitness and proper acclimatization. The descent on the far side spans 3–4 hours to Khuspang at 4,680 meters, the high camp and base for Gondogoro Peak. Overnight in tents.

Day 15 — Khuspang to Dalzampa: Descent into Flower Meadows
A 4–5 hour easy descent follows lateral moraine from Khuspang toward the beautiful campsite of Dalzampa at 4,300 meters, known as a field of flowers. A climb to the lateral moraine provides views of glaciers and jagged spires. This day can function as a reserve day if conditions or group pace require additional time. Overnight in tents.

Day 16 — Dalzampa to Shaicho: Descent Through Cedar and Tamarisk
A 4–5 hour walk on lateral moraine descends through wild roses, gooseberry, cedar, and tamarisk scrub. The Charakusa Valley joins the Gondogoro at Shaicho at 3,330 meters, and the route heads toward the base camps of K6 and K7. Overnight in tents.

Day 17 — Shaicho to Hushe Valley and Return to Skardu
A 4–5 hour easy walk follows the east bank of the Hushe River through agricultural fields to the village of Hushe at 3,050 meters, marking the trek's final stage. A jeep transfer then travels to Skardu at 2,300 meters, with a brief stop at Khaplu, the second-largest historical kingdom of Baltistan, which guards the historic trade route to Ladakh along the Shyok River. Trek debriefing occurs at the Skardu Tourism Department. Overnight in a hotel in Skardu.

Day 18 — Skardu to Chilas or Islamabad
Today marks your departure from Baltistan. The group travels by jeep toward Chilas, a small bazaar town positioned near ancient petroglyphs dating to the first century BCE. The route offers several notable stops: at the junction where three of Asia's greatest mountain ranges converge—the Himalayas, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush—and at viewpoints overlooking Nanga Parbat, the world's ninth-highest peak. For groups preferring to fly, a one-hour domestic flight to Islamabad is available as an alternative to the full overland journey. Those choosing the flight arrive with the afternoon free for rest or independent exploration. Should the flight be cancelled, the group proceeds overland to Chilas for an overnight stay, continuing to Islamabad the following day.

Day 19 — Chilas to Islamabad via Karakoram Highway or Kaghan Valley
The final overland day departs Chilas toward Islamabad. If the Babusar Pass is open, the route traverses the Kaghan Valley and Naran, a scenic alternative. Otherwise, the famous Karakoram Highway is used, offering diverse landscapes over a full day of driving. Arrival in Islamabad is followed by a farewell dinner. Overnight accommodation at the hotel depends on the flight departure time the following morning. If a flight to Islamabad occurred on Day 18, today may be spent at leisure in the capital, with optional sightseeing, souvenir shopping, or a day trip to Taxila to visit the museum and archaeological sites of the Buddhist Gandhara Kingdom (extra fees apply). Overnight in Islamabad.

Day 20 — Departure
Midnight or early morning transfer to the airport for the return international flight. End of services.

tour.name: Tibet Encompassed
tour.summary: To make the pilgrimage to and circumambulation of Mount Kailash is one of the most sacred journeys in the world. The trip itself is one of the most fantastic you can make – starting in the heart of China travel to Lhasa; city of colour and life – monasteries, teahouses, markets and people. From the beauty of central Tibet head west across the vastness of the Tibetan Plateau to where Kailash stands alone. Here join the pilgrims on their kora before turning south to Mount Everest (home to a fairly minor deity) and then on to Kathmandu.
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 Beijing Arrival & Beijing Duck Dinner
Nihao! Welcome to Beijing, the capital of China. Your tour begins with a welcome meeting at 6 pm in your hotel lobby. Your guide will go over more details about your trip including meeting up with your guides in each city. This evening take an orientation walk around the hotel area followed by a Beijing Duck dinner.

Accommodation:
•Chongwenmen Hotel or similar (2 nights)
Meals Included:
•Beijing Duck dinner
Day 2 Beijing Great Wall of China at Mutianyu
Travel about 2 hours out of Beijing to the Mutianyu Great Wall. This is one of the best-preserved and restored sections so it is easy to climb, but you can still appreciate the difficulty of its construction. A picnic lunch on the Wall is provided.
Return to Beijing in time for a fantastic acrobatic show.

Accommodation:
• Chongwenmen Hotel or similar (2 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 3 Explore Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City and Hutongs, train to Xi'an
There will be a lot of walking today as well as using the subway to get around some of Beijing’s most famous sights. Tiananmen Square, one of the world's largest public squares, is home to the Monument of the People's Heroes and the Great hall of the People. From here enter the Forbidden City (built 1406-1420), the ceremonial and political center of the Chinese government for more than 500 years. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 1987 and is listed by UNESCO as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world.
After the Forbidden City, stroll through the alleys formed by lines of traditional courtyards known as Hutong and experience the local lifestyle of Old Beijing.
In the evening, head to the train station for overnight train to Xi’an.
Accommodation:
• Overnight on soft sleeper train Beijing-Xi’an (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 4 Xi'an - Terracotta Warriors, Muslim Quarter
Arriving in Xi’an head to the hotel for breakfast. First on our Xi’an itinerary are the Terracotta Warriors. This incredible archaeological find, discovered in 1976, comprises more than 6,000 warriors, chariots and horses - each individually sculpted from clay with different costumes, height and even facial expressions – all in battle formation. 3 main pits displaying over 2,000 of the warriors are open for you to view.
After lunch in a local village visit one of the best-preserved old residences in Xi’an dating back 400 years. The courtyard was home to seven generations of the Gao family – notable officials of the royal court. Get a taste of the traditional local lifestyle through period furniture, pottery, porcelain, and paintings.
Later, in Xi’an city, wander around the Muslim Quarter with its narrow streets lined with small shops, markets and restaurants.

Accommodation:
• Manxin Hotel Bell Tower or similar ( 2 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 5 Train to Lhasa
This morning we will board the train to Lhasa. The Qinghai-Tibet railway (Xining to Lhasa) is one of China’s greatest engineering feats. It is the highest railway in the world, crossing the high altitude Changtang Plateau – the highest pass is 5069m.
From Xi’an the route travels northeast to Xining, then west to Golmud before turning south to Lhasa. The whole trip from Xi’an takes about 31 hours.

Accommodation:
• Overnight on train Xi’an-Lhasa (1 night)
Meals Included:
•Breakfast
Day 6 Across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa
Wake to find yourself well inside Tibet as you travel across the Tibetan Plateau. The passes may be covered by snow at any time of year and in summer the lakes are surrounded by vast grasslands.
On arrival at Lhasa station, on the outskirts of the city, you are warmly welcomed with a pure white katak (prayer scarf). There will be time to relax and adjust to the altitude before a late afternoon orientation walk.

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Dinner
Day 7 Jokhang Temple, Sera Monastery
Start the day with a visit to the Jokhang; the spiritual heart and most sacred temple of Tibet which always attracts a steady stream of pilgrims. Spend some time exploring this large World-Heritage listed site and learn of its rich history. According to legend, the temple was built over a lake after many failed attempts to build monasteries in other nearby locations. Feast your eyes on the golden Buddha which stands in the center. After the visit join the pilgrims walking around the Barkhor Street (in a clockwise direction) considered a sacred kora by Tibetans.
Then, in the late afternoon, we will visit the great university monastery of Sera where you will witness lively philosophical debating (except Sundays).

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 8 Lhasa Potala Palace
One of the most iconic structures ever built; the Potala Palace was the seat of government and winter residence of the successive Dalai Lamas. A visit is an awe-inspiring experience. Perched 130meters above the city, it is divided into two parts, the White Palace (secular) and the Red Palace (religious - home to chapels, shrines, and tombs of Dalai Lamas). Although you must stick with your guide whilst exploring, this in no way lessens the impact of seeing what is a true architectural wonder.
Free afternoon to explore the city.

Accommodation:
• Shang Bala Hotel or similar (3 nights)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 9 Lhasa/Gyantse -- Khambala Pass, Yamdrok Lake, Karola Pass, Gyantse Dzong
Today we will drive to Gyantse and there will be many photo stops as this is a spectacular route. From the top of the Khamba-la (4750m) the views of the beautiful turquoise lake, Yamdrok Tso, are superb. Descent to skirt the lake before climbing again to the Karo-la (5045m) for a close-up view of NojinGangzang glacier.
Arriving in Gyantse take a walk around to explore the town and hike up to the Dzong (fort) from where you will have fantastic views of the town and surrounding countryside.

Accommodation:
• Gyantse Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 10 Pelkor Choede Monastery, to Shigatse, Tashilumpo
Pelkhor Choede Monastery was founded by the King of Gyantse in the C15th. It does not belong to a specific tradition of Tibetan Buddhism and whilst much reduced from its original size it remains a very active center. Within the complex stands Gyantse Kumbum (meaning 100,000 images), it is an eight-story structure containing a seemingly endless series of tiny chapels full of Buddhist images – Buddhas, demons, protectors, and saints.
A short drive through small villages to Shigatse, Tibet's second-largest city. Upon arrival, we will first visit the Tashilumpo Monastery, home to the Panchen Lamas. Tour the buildings, each with their own intricate decorations, legends and religious imagery. After that, you can opt to do a “kora” around the monastery or visit the local market.
Accommodation:

Accommodation:
• Tangka Hotel Shigatse or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 11 Shigatse/Sakya/Lhatse – drive Shigatse to Lhatse via Sakya Gompa
It is about 3 hours to the Tibetan town of Sakya; site of Sakya Gompa and birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect of Tibetan Buddhism and very distinctive in its colouring. It is also known as the “second Dunhuang,” for its huge collection of over 40,000 volumes of sacred Buddhist scripts, and just one single, long bookshelf holds around 10,000 ancient scriptures.
After the guided monastery tour take an optional hike up the hillside to visit a small nunnery.
Then we will continue on to Lhatse and overnight in this small town.

Accommodation:
• Vienna Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 12 Lhatse to Saga
It is about 4.5 hours drive to Saga. The surrounding grasslands support a wealth of bird life as well as rarer Tibetan antelope, wild Yak … Roads in Tibet are under continual development and are quite different from what you might expect. Virtually all roads you will travel are paved, but there can be delays due to road works (the climactic extremes make maintenance ongoing).
Arrive early in the afternoon to the typical Chinese and Tibetan town of Saga (4640m). Saga is an important stop-off point on the way to Mount Kailash and is always busy with pilgrims and tourists.

Accommodation:
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 13 Saga/Darchen-driving west, first views of Mt Kailash & Lake Manasarovar
Another travel day across the vast highland plain toward Darchen, our base for the kora trek. All day the views are of the great Himalayan range to the south and, to the north, the vast dry Changtang Plateau (which turns briefly and stunningly green with the summer monsoon) and which is home to nomads whose lifestyle remains almost unchanged by the centuries. In the afternoon you will be rewarded with the first spectacular views of Mt Kailash and Lake Manasarovar.
Arrive at Manasarovar Lake, one of the holiest lakes in the world, in the late afternoon. Sacred to Buddhist, Bonpo, Hindu and Jain; every year it receives thousands of pilgrims from all corners of Tibet and India. From the lake several prominent peaks are visible, including Gurla Mandata (7694m). We will continue to drive to Darchen (4675m), a small town and the starting point of the Mt Kailash kora.

Accommodation:
• Chengbao Hotel Darchen or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Lunch
Day 14 Kailash Kora - Trek to Dirapuk Monastery
In the morning, take the shuttle bus from Darchen to Sarshung Valley where we will we start our trek. Walk the path with pilgrims who have saved money their whole lives for this moment. After 4 hours we reach Tamdin (4780m) where nomad tents serve a simple lunch and boiled water. From here it is only 4km to Dirakpuk monastery, but this stretch has the some of the best scenery of the entire kora. Dirakpuk (5210m), located on the north side of the Lha-chu River facing the north face of Mt. Kailash was rebuilt in 1985. The name of Dirakpuk originates from the word Dira which means female yak horn and Puk a cave. Legend says a female yak opened the cave. We will visit Drirapuk and stay overnight in a basic local guesthouse.

Accommodation:
• Dirapuk Guesthouse (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 15 Kailash Kora - Trek from Dira Phuk to Zutrul Puk Monastery
Today is the most challenging part of the kora as we cross the Drolma-la (5630m). Although not too long or steep an ascent, it feels very tough due to the altitude. Climbing to the Drolma-la the many pilgrims on the kora will undergo a symbolic death until they reach the pass and are symbolically reborn. One of the most difficult sections of the Drolma-la is the very steep descent once you have crossed the pass – take care! Finally reaching the valley floor we rest and have lunch at Shabjay Dakpo nomad tent. It is then a long, but flat, hike down the valley to Zutrul Phuk monastery where we overnight in the local guest house.

Accommodation:
• Zutrul Puk Guesthouse (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 16 Kailish Kora - Trek from Zutrul Phuk to Darchen, Drive to Lake Manasarovar
Today is an easy walk back to Darchen to complete the Kailash kora. From Zutrul Puk follow the ever- widening valley alongside lines of mani walls and prayer flags. After reaching Darchen make the short drive back to Lake Manasarovar where you will overnight at a guest house near the lake.

Accommodation:
• Guesthouse Manasarovar ( 1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 17 Lake Manasarovar/Saga - return journey across the Tibetan Plateau
Retrace the outward drive back to Saga for the night.

Accommodation:
• Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 18 south across the grasslands towards the Himalaya, Rombuk & Everest Views
From Saga turn south across the grasslands surrounding lake Paiku-tso. Crossing the Friendship Highway it is a steep climb to Rombuk; a day of stunning scenery. The world’s highest monastery, at 5000m, was first built in 1902 by a Nyingma Lama and originally housed more than 500 monks. Today, only about 50 monks and nuns remain, sharing a prayer hall, but maintaining separate residences. The nuns here are great fun and will be delighted to have you join their evening prayers. From here the view is directly up the valley to Base Camp and Qomolangma/Mount Everest (8849m).

Accommodation:
• Rombuk guesthouse ( 1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast & lunch
Day 19 Rombuk/Kyirong - Tasuwa border
Today is another long days’ drive of 350km. It will take 6-7 hours to get to Kyirong where we spend the night before crossing the border to Nepal.

Accommodation:
• Kyirong Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast, Dinner
Day 20 Kyirong-Rasuwa, to Kathmandu
This morning after breakfast, we will cross the border from China to Nepal. This can be a slow process, especially the Nepal side.
Namaste! Welcome to Nepal. It is a long day’s drive to Kathmandu, much of the road in very bad condition. Explore this alluring city on a walking tour with your local leader. Check out the Newari architecture at Durbar Square, the vast plaza opposite the old Royal Palaces if time permit.

Accommodation:
• Mulberry Hotel or similar (1 night)
Meals Included:
• Breakfast
Day 21 Depart Kathmandu
There are no activities planned for today and you can depart at any time.

Meals Included:
Breakfast

output.name: Tibet: Beijing to Kathmandu — 21 Days
output.subtitle: From the Great Wall and Forbidden City through the Tibetan Plateau to Mount Kailash, Lake Manasarovar, and Mount Everest
output.summary: This journey moves from China's imperial centers across one of the world's highest plateaus to stand at the foot of Mount Kailash — a mountain held sacred by four religions — and walk the ancient pilgrimage circuit known as the kora alongside devotees who have saved for years to make this crossing. The route begins in Beijing with the Great Wall and Forbidden City, continues by rail to Xi'an and its terracotta warriors, then ascends via the Qinghai-Tibet Railway — the world's highest standard-gauge line — to Lhasa. From there, the itinerary moves west across grassland and high pass to Darchen, the staging point for the kora trek around Mount Kailash. After the kora, the path turns south to Rombuk monastery, the world's highest at 5,000 meters, which sits directly across a valley from Mount Everest's north face. The final descent crosses into Nepal and ends in Kathmandu.
highlights: Walk the Mutianyu section of the Great Wall, one of the best-preserved restored segments near Beijing
Tour the Forbidden City, built 1406–1420 as the political and ceremonial center of imperial China, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
View the Terracotta Warriors in Xi'an — over 6,000 individually sculpted clay figures discovered in 1976, displayed across three excavated pits
Ride the Qinghai-Tibet Railway at altitudes up to 5,069 meters, the world's highest standard-gauge railway crossing the Changtang Plateau
Visit Jokhang Temple in Lhasa, Tibet's most sacred shrine, and walk the Barkhor Street kora with pilgrims
Visit the Potala Palace in Lhasa, seat of the Dalai Lamas, perched 130 meters above the city with its White Palace and Red Palace
Cross Khambala Pass (4,750 m) for views of turquoise Yamdrok Tso lake and approach Karola Pass (5,045 m) for views of Nojin Gangzang glacier
Visit Tashilumpo Monastery in Shigatse, home to successive Panchen Lamas, with intricate decorations and religious imagery
Tour Sakya Gompa, birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect, known as the 'second Dunhuang' for its collection of over 40,000 volumes of Buddhist scriptures
Complete the three-day kora (circumambulation) of Mount Kailash, trekking from Darchen through Dirapuk and Zutrul Puk monasteries, crossing Drolma-la pass at 5,630 meters
Stay overnight at Rombuk monastery (5,000 m), the world's highest, with direct views up the valley to Mount Everest's north face
Cross the Sino-Nepal border at Kyirong and descend to Kathmandu
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Beijing Arrival and Welcome Dinner
Arrive in Beijing and check into your hotel. At 6 pm, meet your guide in the lobby for a briefing on the 21-day itinerary ahead and logistics for guides and accommodations in each city. Walk the immediate hotel area to orient yourself, then dine on Beijing duck this evening.

Day 2 — Mutianyu Section of the Great Wall
Travel two hours north of Beijing to Mutianyu, one of the best-preserved and restored sections of the Great Wall. The restored stonework makes climbing manageable while the construction's difficulty remains evident. Picnic lunch is served on the wall itself. Return to the city in time for an acrobatic performance.

Day 3 — Tiananmen Square, Forbidden City, and Hutongs — Night Train to Xi'an
A walking-intensive day through central Beijing. Begin at Tiananmen Square, one of the world's largest public plazas, anchored by the Monument of the People's Heroes and the Great Hall of the People. Enter the Forbidden City, built between 1406 and 1420 as the ceremonial and political seat of Chinese government for over 500 years. UNESCO recognizes it as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world and designated it a World Heritage Site in 1987. After touring the palace complex, visit the nearby Hutongs — narrow lanes lined with traditional courtyard residences — to experience the domestic life of historic Beijing. In the evening, transfer to the train station for an overnight soft-sleeper train to Xi'an.

Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors and Muslim Quarter
Arrive in Xi'an and breakfast at the hotel. The morning focuses on the Terracotta Warriors, an archaeological discovery from 1976 comprising over 6,000 life-size clay figures — warriors, chariots, and horses — each individually sculpted with distinct costumes, heights, and facial expressions and arranged in battle formation. Three main excavation pits display more than 2,000 of these figures. After lunch in a local village, visit a 400-year-old residence that housed seven generations of the Gao family, prominent royal court officials. The preserved courtyard displays period furniture, pottery, porcelain, and paintings that convey traditional domestic life. In the city, walk the Muslim Quarter, characterized by narrow streets, small shops, markets, and restaurants.

Day 5 — Qinghai-Tibet Railway: Xi'an to Lhasa
Board the train to Lhasa. The Qinghai-Tibet Railway is one of China's major engineering achievements and the world's highest standard-gauge line. The route from Xi'an travels northeast to Xining, then west to Golmud before turning south toward Lhasa, crossing the high-altitude Changtang Plateau with a highest pass at 5,069 meters. The entire journey takes approximately 31 hours.

Day 6 — Across the Tibetan Plateau to Lhasa
Wake to find yourself well inside Tibet as the train crosses the high Tibetan Plateau. The passes may be covered by snow at any time of year; in summer, the lakes are surrounded by vast grasslands. On arrival at Lhasa station, on the outskirts of the city, you receive a pure white katak (prayer scarf). There will be time to rest and adjust to the altitude before a late afternoon orientation walk, allowing you to begin acclimatizing to Lhasa's elevation while exploring the immediate surroundings.

Day 7 — Jokhang Temple and Sera Monastery
Begin the day at Jokhang, the spiritual heart of Tibetan Buddhism and its most sacred temple. A steady stream of pilgrims moves through this large World Heritage site. The temple's history includes a legend of its construction over a lake after multiple failed attempts to build monasteries at other nearby locations. A golden Buddha stands at the center. After exploring the temple interior, join pilgrims walking clockwise around Barkhor Street, a ritual circuit considered sacred in Tibetan practice. In the late afternoon, visit Sera, a major monastic university, to witness philosophical debates among monks (except on Sundays).

Day 8 — Potala Palace and Lhasa
The Potala Palace commands the Lhasa skyline from 130 meters above the city — a major architectural achievement. This former seat of government and winter residence of successive Dalai Lamas divides into two distinct sections: the White Palace, devoted to secular administration, and the Red Palace, housing religious spaces, chapels, shrines, and the tombs of the Dalai Lamas. A guide accompanies you through the palace's ornate interior. The afternoon opens for independent exploration of Lhasa's streets and neighborhoods.

Day 9 — Lhasa to Gyantse: High Passes and Yamdrok Lake
Drive to Gyantse with planned photo stops along the route. From Khambala Pass (4,750 m), views extend across the turquoise waters of Yamdrok Tso lake. Descend to skirt the lake's edge, then climb again to Karola Pass (5,045 m) for views of Nojin Gangzang glacier. Upon arrival in Gyantse, walk the town, then hike up to the Dzong (fort) for views across town and surrounding countryside.

Day 10 — Gyantse to Shigatse: Pelkor Choede and Tashilumpo Monastery
Visit Pelkhor Choede Monastery, founded by the King of Gyantse in the 15th century. Unlike other Tibetan monasteries, it does not align with a single Buddhist tradition and is now much reduced from its original size but remains an active center. Within the complex stands Gyantse Kumbum, an eight-story structure containing numerous small chapels filled with Buddhist images — Buddhas, protective deities, and saints. Drive through small villages to Shigatse, Tibet's second-largest city. Upon arrival, tour Tashilumpo Monastery, home to successive Panchen Lamas, with buildings featuring intricate decorations, religious legends, and imagery. You may choose to walk the kora circuit around the monastery or visit the local market.

Day 11 — Shigatse to Lhatse via Sakya Gompa
Drive three hours to Sakya, site of Sakya Gompa and birthplace of the Sakya-pa sect of Tibetan Buddhism. The gompa's distinctive architecture sets it visually apart. It holds a significant collection of Buddhist sacred texts housed in the monastery library. After a guided monastery tour, there is an optional hike uphill to visit a small nunnery. Continue onward to Lhatse, a small town where you overnight.

Day 12 — Lhatse to Saga across High Grassland
A 4.5-hour drive carries you across the Tibetan plateau to Saga (4,640 m), an important waypoint for pilgrims heading toward Mount Kailash. The surrounding grasslands support varied birdlife and rare sightings of Tibetan antelope and wild yak. Most roads across Tibet are paved, though ongoing development and harsh climatic extremes mean maintenance work can cause delays — a reminder that infrastructure here is constantly evolving. You arrive early afternoon in this typical Chinese and Tibetan town. The altitude here is significant; take time to acclimatize. You stay at Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar. Breakfast and lunch are included.

Day 13 — Saga to Darchen: First Views of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar
Continue west across the vast highland plain toward Darchen, the base for the Kailash kora trek. The landscape frames views of the Himalayan range to the south and the dry Changtang Plateau to the north, which briefly turns green during the summer monsoon. The plateau is home to nomadic communities whose lifestyle has remained largely unchanged for centuries. In the afternoon, you reach views of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar. One of the holiest lakes in the world, Manasarovar is sacred to Buddhist, Bonpo, Hindu, and Jain traditions and receives thousands of pilgrims annually from across Tibet and India. Several prominent peaks are visible from the lake, including Gurla Mandata (7,694 m). Continue to Darchen (4,675 m), the small town serving as the starting point for the Kailash kora.

Day 14 — Kailash Kora: Darchen to Dirapuk Monastery
Take a shuttle bus from Darchen to Sarshung Valley to begin the kora trek. Walk alongside pilgrims on this sacred circuit. After four hours, reach Tamdin (4,780 m), where nomad tents serve simple lunch and boiled water. From here, walk 4 kilometers to Dirapuk monastery. Dirapuk (5,210 m) sits on the north side of the Lha-chu River facing Mount Kailash's north face. Rebuilt in 1985, the monastery's name derives from 'Dira' (female yak horn) and 'Puk' (cave). Overnight in a basic local guesthouse.

Day 15 — Kailash Kora: Crossing Drolma-la Pass to Zutrul Puk
Today presents the kora's most challenging section. Cross Drolma-la pass (5,630 m), not exceptionally steep or long but demanding due to altitude. The descent after the pass is notably steep; care is needed. Once in the valley floor, rest and have lunch at a Shabjay Dakpo nomad tent. A long, flat hike down the valley leads to Zutrul Phuk monastery, where you overnight in a local guesthouse.

Day 16 — Kailash Kora: Return to Darchen and Lake Manasarovar
Walk the final section of the kora back to Darchen. From Zutrul Puk, follow the widening valley past lines of mani walls and prayer flags. Upon reaching Darchen, complete the three-day circuit. Drive the short distance to Lake Manasarovar, staying overnight at a guesthouse near the shore.

Day 17 — Manasarovar to Saga: Return Across the Tibetan Plateau
Retrace the outward drive back across the Tibetan Plateau to Saga for the night. Accommodation at Saga Yalong Zangbu Hotel or similar. Breakfast and lunch included.

Day 18 — Saga to Rombuk: Mount Everest and High-Altitude Monastery
Turn south from Saga across grasslands surrounding Lake Paiku-tso. Cross the Friendship Highway and climb steeply toward Rombuk in a day of varied scenery. Rombuk sits at 5,000 meters as one of the world's highest monasteries, first built in 1902 by a Nyingma Lama and originally housing over 500 monks. Today, approximately 50 monks and nuns remain, sharing a prayer hall but maintaining separate residences. The nuns are welcoming and may invite you to join evening prayers. From the monastery, views extend directly up the valley toward Everest Base Camp and Qomolangma/Mount Everest (8,849 m).

Day 19 — Rombuk to Kyirong: Border Approach
A long 350-kilometer drive stretches across six to seven hours, carrying you toward Kyirong. You'll overnight here at Kyirong Hotel or similar, resting before tomorrow's border crossing into Nepal. Breakfast and dinner are included.

Day 20 — Border Crossing and Descent to Kathmandu
After breakfast, cross from China into Nepal. Border procedures can be slow, particularly on the Nepal side. Welcome to Nepal. The descent to Kathmandu is a long drive on roads in variable condition. Upon arrival, take a walking tour to see Durbar Square, a vast plaza opposite the old Royal Palaces, and observe Newari architecture if time allows.

Day 21 — Depart Kathmandu
No activities are scheduled for today. You are free to depart Kathmandu at any time that suits your travel plans. Breakfast is included.

tour.name: Luang Prabang - Hoi An
tour.subtitle: Luang Prabang, Phonsavan, Konglor Cave, Hue, Hoi An
tour.summary:
About This Tour 
Terrain: Tarmac Road

This tour is a great way to see the best of both Central  Laos and Vietnam, you take in the famous sites of Luang Prabang, Phonsavan along with the cultural glamour and bustle of Hoi- An and  Hue 

The difference in cultural and opportunity between the two countries  is striking as you cross the border.

This route through Laos takes you on a journey of remote discovery far away from the swarms of Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh CIty

We take in Natural wonders such as Kong lor Cave ( 7km river cave)  and  Phong Nha National Park home to some of the most spectacular nature in Vietnam
highlights:
Kong Lor Cave 
UNESCO site the Plain of Jars 
Teak Forest Ride
UNESCO World Heritage town of Luang Prabang
Historic Hue
tour.itineraries:
DAY 01:
Luang Prabang (D)
We meet at the airport then check in to our accommodation to brief everyone thoroughly and make sure the bikes fit.  We can take an hour or two if time permits to explore the Unesco Zone by bike and perhaps take in some of the Temples and the Hmong Night Market. 
Dinner is served at a local Vocational training Restaurant that provides exquisite food and employment opportunities to marginalized youth. Ride: 20km

Overnight in Luang Prabang

DAY 02: 
Luang Prabang - Phou Khoun (B)
The day begins with a 1 hour transfer to get over the first mountain, after 65km in a van we begin our mountain top ride to a simple guesthouse and a local restaurant. High in the mountains in the cross road town of Phoukhoun.
Overnight in PhouKhoun


DAY 03: 
Phou Khoun - Phonsavan (B,L)
This  road is known for big climbs and challenging riding. 
The views are spectacular from the limestone peaks as we enter the high plateau of Xiang Khouang Province, we stay the night in Phonsavan, a rapidly  developing destination . There is a lot of road to cover this day so a Transfer is used to begin the ride and a short van ride into the city at the end of the day is necessary.

Ride:  80 km 
Overnight in Phonsavan 

DAY 4: 
Plain Of Jars Round Trip (B,L)
This is a perfect ride to get used to the new climate as we are over 1000 meters above sea level. The Plain of Jars remains a place whose mysterious past has led to diverse speculations. Why did people make these amazing stone formations and what were they used for? 
Ride: 65 km 
Overnight in Phonsavan

DAY 5: 
Phonsavan - Muang Khoun- Thathom(B,L)
We leave the city by van and begin our ride south, we begin the Ride at That Foun a 16th century Buddhist stupa situated on a remote plain, from here we cycle 90km on challenging mountain roads to the little town of Thathom. 
Overnight in Thathom 

DAY 6: 
Thatthom - Khoun Kham (B,L,D)
From Xiang Khounang to Bolikhamxay province in the shadow of Nam Kadding forest. We travel by van and bicycle to the village of Ban Nahin  and a welcoming riverside guesthouse and the best red curry in the province! 
Cycle 80km
Overnight in Ban Nahin 


DAY 7: 
Konglor Cave Road Trip (B,L)
The New tarmac road from Khoun Kham is a joy to ride the livestock and villages smile and wave and welcome us with friendly calls the limestone karst peaks loom over the valley. 
At the end of the road KongLor cave gaps wide. One of the longest water cave systems is navigated expertly by the pilots of the native longboats , there is an illuminated section so you can experience the stalagmites. The Journey through the cave is one of the highlights of Laos.
Ride: 84 KM 
Overnight in Ban Nahin


DAY 8: 
Ban Nahin - Lak Seo (B,L)
We follow Route 8 east to the Vietnam border there is lots to see on the way as this road is part of the famous motorbike ride the Thakhek loop. 
Lunch is served at ‘Cool Pool’ here we can swim in the crystal blue waters and take a picnic with locals. 
The bustling border town of Lak Seo is our last stop in Laos and in the morning we will leave early to cross the border into Vietnam
Ride 74KM
Overnight in Lak Seo


DAY 9
Lak Seo - Vinh (B,L)
A short Cycle  to border point 
We say goodbye to our Laos team and meet up with your new crew after crossing the border into Vietnam. From the border, we drive toward Vinh for overnight. On the way, we will stop at Kim Lien village, the birthplace of Ho Chi Minh to visit his house and a museum dedicated to him. After the visit transfer by road out of the mountains on to Vinh arriving late this afternoon. Dinner and overnight in Vinh.
Ride 30km
       


DAY 10
Vinh – Huong Khe (B,L)
Following breakfast, transfer 40 km by bus to the Ho Chi Minh highway to the town of Pho Chau, the start of today’s ride. The journey winds through lush jungle and beautiful villages nestled under the Truong Son mountain range. During the ride, take your time to admire the stunning scenery and the intricate karst formations. After a long day of pedalling, arrive in the remote town of Huong Khe. Located in Nghe An province, this small town is a quiet place to rest up for another busy day of riding. Overnight in Huong Khe.
80KM CYCLING


DAY 11
Huong Khe– Phong Nha (B,L)
Continue along the Ho Chi Minh Highway today to Phong Nha. The route is still a dream to ride on and you’ll appreciate the smooth tarmac as the mountains rise and the road winds up, down and along the hillsides. The scenery is spectacular and the road is tranquil. After cycling around 80km, trade in your bike for a restful 1 hour bus journey to Phong Nha National Park. The park contains one of the most spectacular caves in Vietnam - a true natural wonder with 65 kilometres of tunnels and underground rivers. Formed approximately 250 million years ago Phong Nha was used as a hospital and ammunition depot during the war, and the entrance still shows evidence of attacks from fighter aircraft. There are also community projects underway with Flora and Fauna International and it may be possible to visit village initiatives and learn more about the forests of the national park before the end of today. 
Ride 80km
Overnight in Phong Nha.

DAY 12         
Phong Nha – Cam Lo – Khe Sanh (B,L)
After an early morning exploration of Phong Nha Cave, transfer 1.5 hours by road to the Ho Chi Minh Trail to resume your ride. Pedal across the DMZ (also known as the 17th Parallel) to Cam Lo. Stop en route to visit Truong Son cemetery, a memorial to the tens of thousands of North Vietnamese soldiers who were killed in the Truong Son Mountains. From there it’s only 14 kilometres further to the town of Cam Lo and here the trail heads across the country into Laos. Finish today with a short transfer to Khe Sanh, a former US marine base and site of the infamous 1968 battle of the same name.
Ride 80km
Overnight in Khe Sanh.

DAY 13
Khe Sanh – A Luoi (B,L)
Begin this morning with a visit to the Khe Sanh combat base where relics of the war are exhibited and see the airstrip. Then ride through spectacular scenery, mainly downhill, from the Laos border to the Dakrong River. Cross the river by bridge and ride along the waterway to what was considered the southern part of the Ho Chi Minh Trail. Again enjoy a traffic-free road with rolling terrain, a nice contrast to the flat plains of the previous day’s ride. 
Overnight in A Luoi.
65KM CYCLING 

DAY 14        
A Luoi – Hue (B,L,D)
Due to the bad roads south of A Luoi, today you venture off the Ho Chi Minh Trail and head across the country to Hue. The 60km ride through the middle of Vietnam is on back roads before hitting Highway 1 just a few kilometres south of Hue. Here there is the option of transferring by road or continuing by bike to the centre of Hue. 
60KM CYCLING 
Overnight in Hue.

DAY 15
Hue (B,L)
Following breakfast, enjoy a relatively easy cycle on the back roads of Hue through lush countryside on a mix of footpaths and quiet country lanes. The day begins with a visit to the Imperial Citadel where you will explore the ruins of this grand monument to the emperors. Then, ride along backstreets, following the banks of the Perfume River to Thien Mu Pagoda. Continue through the quiet roads of Hue’s countryside to visit the royal tomb of Minh Mang a former Nguyen emperor, and loop back across the river to Hue via the funerary monument to Khai Dinh. Return to central Hue early this afternoon for time at your leisure to relax or tour more on your own. 
Ride 25km 
Overnight in Hue.


DAY 16        
Hue – Hoi An (B,L,D)
Today is an epic ride with two small hills to conquer before the intense 11 km climb uphill to the top of Hai Van Pass where you will be rewarded with stunning views of the coast. With a recently opened tunnel through the mountain, there is now very little traffic on this uphill road. Cruise down the pass to Lang Co beach for a swim and lunch. Then transfer the final 35 kilometres by car to Hoi An, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The remainder of this afternoon and evening is at your leisure to explore the narrow streets and lanes of this charming town. 
Ride 90KM 
Overnight in Hoi An.

DAY 17        
Hoi An - My Son – Hoi An (B,L)
The last day of the journey is an easy ride My Son, the ancient centre of Cham civilization. Transfer a bit out of town to avoid the highway before cycling along scenic country back roads, past rice paddy fields, through a eucalyptus forest and passing many picturesque villages. The meandering road eventually leads us to My Son, once Champa’s greatest city and now an impressive archaeological site. Enjoy lunch near the temples and an afternoon spent touring around the crumbling temples before transferring back to Hoi An by bus. Overnight in Hoi An.
40KM CYCLING
END OF SERVICES

output.name: Laos & Central Vietnam by Bike: Luang Prabang to Hoi An — 18 Days
output.subtitle: From the 16th-century temples of Luang Prabang through the Plain of Jars and Kong Lor Cave, then across Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh Trail to the imperial city of Hue and the riverside town of Hoi An.
output.summary: This 18-day cycling route connects Laos and Vietnam by tarmac road, moving from the UNESCO-protected temples and night markets of Luang Prabang southeast through the high plateau of Xiang Khouang Province—home to the mysterious Plain of Jars—and into the limestone karst valleys where Kong Lor Cave's seven-kilometre river passage cuts through the landscape. The route then crosses into Vietnam at Lak Seo, picks up the Ho Chi Minh Trail from Vinh northward, and traces the historical DMZ to Khe Sanh, site of the 1968 battle and former U.S. marine base. From there, the tour descends through A Luoi and Hue—the former imperial capital whose royal tombs and citadel remain embedded in the countryside—before climbing Hai Van Pass and finishing in Hoi An, the well-preserved 16th-century trading port now a UNESCO World Heritage town. Total cycling distance is split across 14 riding days; the remainder involve transfers to navigate mountains or reach new regions. The road is consistently paved, though terrain varies from flat valley runs to sustained mountain climbs. Accommodation ranges from riverside guesthouses in remote Laotian villages to heritage hotels in Vietnam's larger towns.
highlights: Cycling 65 kilometers around the Plain of Jars at 1,000 metres elevation—a vast plateau studded with megalithic stone urns of unknown origin
Kong Lor Cave: a seven-kilometre river cave navigated by traditional longboat, with an illuminated section revealing stalactite and stalagmite formations
UNESCO World Heritage town of Luang Prabang, with cycling access to Wat Xieng Thong and the Hmong Night Market
Cycling sections of the Ho Chi Minh Trail across the DMZ (17th Parallel), including a stop at Truong Son Cemetery
Khe Sanh Combat Base, a former U.S. marine stronghold, with exhibits of war-era relics and the original airstrip
Hai Van Pass: an 11-kilometre uphill climb rewarded with coastal views, now less trafficked due to a recently opened tunnel through the mountain
Phong Nha National Park, home to a 65-kilometre cave system formed 250 million years ago, used as a hospital and weapons depot during the Vietnam War
Cycling the backroads around Hue through the Perfume River valley, past the Imperial Citadel and royal tombs of emperors Minh Mang and Khai Dinh
My Son: the archaeological ruins of Champa's ancient capital, approached by cycling through rice paddies and eucalyptus forest from Hoi An
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Luang Prabang: Airport Transfer & Town Orientation
Meet at the airport and proceed to accommodation for bike setup and tour briefing. Time permitting, a guided 20-kilometre cycle through the UNESCO zone visits the town's temple quarter and passes the Hmong Night Market. Evening meal is at a local vocational training restaurant that combines quality cooking with employment opportunities for marginalized youth. Overnight in Luang Prabang.

Day 2 — Luang Prabang to Phou Khoun: First Mountain Crossing
A one-hour van transfer covers the first mountain pass before cycling begins on the high plateau. Sixty-five kilometres by van, then a mountain-top ride concludes at a simple guesthouse in Phou Khoun, a remote crossroads town. Overnight in Phou Khoun.

Day 3 — Phou Khoun to Phonsavan: High Plateau Approach
This stage demands sustained climbing and technical riding as the route enters the high limestone peaks of Xiang Khouang Province and the 1,000-metre Phonsavan plateau. A transfer navigates the steeper opening section; 80 kilometres of cycling follow, with another short van leg into town at day's end. Phonsavan is a rapidly expanding destination marking the transition from remote mountain passes to established towns. Overnight in Phonsavan.

Day 4 — Round Trip to the Plain of Jars from Phonsavan
A 65-kilometre loop ride across the UNESCO-listed Plain of Jars allows acclimatization to the high elevation and climate. The plain is covered in hundreds of large stone urns, their origin and purpose still debated—theories range from funerary vessels to rain-collection containers, their construction and purpose remain unexplained. The plateau itself rises to 1,000 metres and offers expansive horizons. Overnight in Phonsavan.

Day 5 — Phonsavan to Thathom: Southern Descent into Bolikhamxay
A van transfer departs Phonsavan southward, dropping the group at That Foun, a 16th-century Buddhist stupa positioned on an isolated plain. From here, 90 kilometres of challenging mountain roads lead south through changing terrain to Thathom, a small town marking the transition into Bolikhamxay Province. Overnight in Thathom.

Day 6 — Thathom to Ban Nahin: Forest Road to Nam Kadding
A combination of van and bicycle travel crosses from Xiang Khounang into Bolikhamxay Province, skirting the Nam Kadding forest. The group cycles 80 kilometres to Ban Nahin, a riverside village with a welcoming guesthouse. Local cuisine—notably the province's red curry—anchors the evening. Overnight in Ban Nahin.

Day 7 — Kong Lor Cave Road Trip: Through Limestone Karst
Fresh tarmac from Khoun Kham rolls through valleys where livestock herds and village residents offer casual greetings as limestone karst peaks frame the landscape. Eighty-four kilometres of easy-paced riding lead to Kong Lor Cave, one of the region's longest navigable water caves. Local longboat pilots guide visitors through the passages; an illuminated section reveals stalactite and stalagmite formations. The journey through the cave—water flowing beneath the mountain, the canopy of rock overhead—stands as one of Laos's signature geological experiences. Return to Ban Nahin for the night.

Day 8 — Ban Nahin to Lak Seo: Route 8 to the Vietnamese Border
Following Route 8 eastward toward the Vietnam border, the road passes villages, river crossings, and viewpoints; this section is part of the famous Thakhek Loop motorcycle route. Seventy-four kilometres of cycling include a midday stop at 'Cool Pool,' a swimming spot with water clear enough for a picnic with local families. Lak Seo, a bustling border town, is Laos's final stop. Overnight in Lak Seo.

Day 9 — Lak Seo to Vinh: Border Crossing into Vietnam
A short 30-kilometre cycle reaches the Vietnam border. After handover to the Vietnamese team, the group drives into the mountains toward Vinh, with a stop at Kim Lien village—birthplace of Ho Chi Minh—to visit his house and a small museum. The drive descends from the mountains onto Vinh's coastal plains, arriving in the late afternoon. Dinner and overnight in Vinh.

Day 10 — Vinh to Huong Khe: Jungled Valleys and Mountain Foothills
After breakfast, a 40-kilometre bus transfer moves the group to Pho Chau, the day's cycling start. Eighty kilometres follow through lush jungle and quiet villages set beneath the Truong Son Mountains. Karst formations rise and fall along the route; the road winds through forested terrain with minimal traffic. Huong Khe, a small town in Nghe An Province, provides a quiet rest point in remote terrain. Overnight in Huong Khe.

Day 11 — Huong Khe to Phong Nha: Mountain Climbs and Cave Exploration
The Ho Chi Minh Highway continues southward with fresh tarmac; eighty kilometres of cycling wind through hills and down through quiet forest as mountains rise on either side. The road itself is notably smooth and low-traffic, creating a rare tranquility on a major route. After cycling, a one-hour bus ride delivers the group to Phong Nha National Park. The park's signature cave—Phong Nha Cave—extends 65 kilometres underground with tunnels and subterranean rivers formed approximately 250 million years ago. During the Vietnam War, the cave functioned as a hospital and ammunition depot; scarring from fighter-aircraft attacks still marks the entrance. Community conservation initiatives with Flora and Fauna International operate within the park; visits to village projects may be arranged to learn about forest restoration efforts. Overnight near Phong Nha.

Day 12 — Phong Nha to Khe Sanh: Cycling the DMZ and Ho Chi Minh Trail
An early-morning cave exploration precedes a 1.5-hour bus ride to the Ho Chi Minh Trail. Eighty kilometres of cycling follows across the DMZ—formally the 17th Parallel—the former demarcation line between North and South Vietnam. En route, the group visits Truong Son Cemetery, a memorial to tens of thousands of North Vietnamese soldiers killed in the Truong Son Mountains. From Cam Lo, the trail heads inland toward Khe Sanh (a 14-kilometre ride beyond), a former U.S. marine base and site of the 1968 siege—one of the war's most intense battles. Overnight in Khe Sanh.

Day 13 — Khe Sanh to A Luoi: Combat Base to Dakrong River Valley
The morning opens with a visit to Khe Sanh Combat Base, where exhibits display war-era relics and the original airstrip remains visible. Sixty-five kilometres of predominantly downhill cycling then traverse spectacular terrain from the Laos border to the Dakrong River. A bridge crossing gives way to a ride along the riverbank, skirting what was once the southern section of the Ho Chi Minh Trail. Traffic-free roads and rolling terrain create a marked contrast to the flat plains of the previous day. Overnight in A Luoi.

Day 14 — A Luoi to Hue: Cross-Country Transition on Back Roads
Poor road conditions south of A Luoi prompt a departure from the Ho Chi Minh Trail; instead, a 60-kilometre ride cuts across central Vietnam on quiet back roads before joining Highway 1 just south of Hue. Riders have the option to transfer the final kilometres or continue by bike into Hue's centre. Overnight in Hue.

Day 15 — Hue: Imperial Citadel, Royal Tombs & Perfume River Loop
An easy 25-kilometre loop on back roads and country lanes visits Hue's imperial heritage. The day begins at the Imperial Citadel, where the ruins of this monument to the Nguyen emperors stand amid the working city. Cycling follows backstreets and the Perfume River's banks to Thien Mu Pagoda, then continues through countryside to the royal tomb of Minh Mang, a former Nguyen emperor. The return passes the funerary monument of Khai Dinh before crossing the river back to central Hue, allowing an afternoon at leisure to rest or independently wander further. Overnight in Hue.

Day 16 — Hue to Hoi An: Hai Van Pass and Lang Co Beach
Ninety kilometres of riding, including two moderate climbs, culminates in an 11-kilometre ascent of Hai Van Pass, the prominent geographical barrier between Hue and the southern coast. A recently opened tunnel has substantially reduced traffic on the pass road; the climb now rewards riders with clear views toward the coast and Da Nang. Descent leads to Lang Co Beach, a suitable point for a swim and meal. The final 35 kilometres transfer by road to Hoi An, a UNESCO World Heritage Site preserving 16th-century architecture and streetscapes from its era as a Southeast Asian trading port. Evening and the following morning are free to wander the narrow lanes and riverside quarter. Overnight in Hoi An.

Day 17 — Hoi An to My Son: Ancient Champa Ruins via Rice Paddies
A final 40-kilometre ride approaches the archaeological site of My Son, once Champa's greatest city and now a sprawl of crumbling brick temples. The route avoids the main highway; instead, scenic back roads pass rice paddies, a eucalyptus forest, and numerous small villages. The meandering path builds toward the ruins gradually, culminating in a lunch near the temple grounds and an afternoon spent walking among the structures—remnants of a civilization that flourished centuries before Vietnamese expansion southward. A bus transfer returns the group to Hoi An for the final night. End of services.

A short descent along the Caoling Historic Trail brings guests to our pick-up location, Dali Visitor Center. Here guests can explore a local temple, grab some refreshing snacks from local food vendors, before jumping in our private van and return to Taipei Main Station.

output.name: East Sumida Half Day: Gardens, Museums & Shrines
output.subtitle: A half-day cycling route through Tokyo's eastern neighborhoods — Kiyosumi Garden, Fukagawa Edo Museum, and Tomioka Hachimangu Shrine
output.summary: This half-day cycling route crosses the Sumida River into Tokyo's quieter eastern districts, visiting three distinct landmarks that trace the city's cultural geography. The route begins with a crossing of the Sumida—either via the Kiyosu Bridge or Eitai Bridge—and moves through Kiyosumi Garden, a traditional Japanese garden with a central pond, designed and once owned by Iwasaki, founder of the Mitsubishi group. The Fukagawa Edo Museum follows, presenting replica buildings and domestic structures from the mid-1800s that document how residents lived during the Edo period. The route then passes through Kiba Park, a green space built on the site of a former timber pond at the confluence of two major canals, before concluding at Tomioka Hachimangu Shrine, a significant historical site where sumo wrestling was historically held. Departure times are 9:00 AM or 1:00 PM, with returns at noon or 4:00 PM. The route is suited to families with younger children and to visitors with limited time in Tokyo.

output.subtitle: A single day moving through 2,000 years of Xi'an's history: archaeological site, medieval fortifications, and working food culture.
output.summary: Xi'an's layered past can be sampled in a single day without feeling rushed. Begin at the Terracotta Warriors and Horses Museum, where nearly 2,000 of an estimated 6,000 clay figures stand in formation—each individually sculpted, each bearing different height, costume, and facial features—after being buried for two millennia until a farmer's well-digging accident revealed them in 1976. Lunch follows in a village restaurant. The afternoon brings a bicycle circuit of the Old City Wall, a 600-year-old structure and the most intact ancient defensive system of its scale remaining in China. Evening unfolds in the Muslim Quarter's narrow streets, where local food vendors and family-run stalls operate much as they have for centuries. The day reads as a practical cross-section of Xi'an rather than a survey—enough time at each stop to absorb its particular character without the feeling of passing through.

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Terracotta Warriors, City Wall & Muslim Quarter
The day begins with a private vehicle transfer to the Terracotta Warriors and Horses Museum, located outside the city center. The site contains three main excavation pits, each revealing roughly 2,000 of an estimated 6,000 clay figures originally buried in formation. Each warrior—whether infantry, cavalry, or charioteer—was individually sculpted from clay, with distinct height, facial features, and costume details. The discovery came by chance in 1976 when farmers digging a well struck the terracotta. Walking among the standing figures, the scale of the workforce and technical precision become apparent. A midday meal takes place in a local village restaurant. In the afternoon, bicycles are provided for a circuit of the Old City Wall, the 600-year-old fortification that remains the most complete medieval defensive system of its size in China. The ride traces the perimeter of the ancient city, offering views both inward and across the modern urban landscape beyond. As evening settles, the route moves into the Muslim Quarter—a dense network of narrow streets and alleyways where restaurants, small food vendors, and family-run shops operate. The quarter represents centuries of settlement and commerce, and offers a direct view of how Xi'an's residents eat and move through daily life.

This tour takes you through the most scenic parts of this enchanting valley, including the popular hill station of Malam Jabba, the charming town of Kalam, and the stunning Mahodand Lake. You'll also explore the rich cultural heritage of Swat, visiting ancient Buddhist stupas, the Swat Museum, and traditional Swati villages. The tour offers a perfect blend of natural beauty, cultural experiences, and outdoor activities in one of Pakistan's most accessible and picturesque regions.

The valley's primary town, Mingora, anchors the route; from there, roads climb to Malam Jabba, a ski resort, and to Kalam, a smaller mountain settlement used as a base for trekking and lake visits. The valley holds considerable Buddhist archaeological history—ruined stupas and carved sites dating to the 1st century CE remain visible across the landscape. This five-day itinerary combines these elements: museum visits and site walks in Mingora, highland views and short hikes from Malam Jabba, and a full-day excursion to Mahodand Lake. The route follows the Swat River for much of its length and involves mixed terrain—paved valley roads, steep mountain passes, and rough jeep tracks to the lake. highlights: Khustai National Park is located 120km from Ulaanbaatar city amongst the mountains that maintain their natural beauty, unharmed by human activities. Nowadays, there are approximately 350 horses thriving within the safety of the National Park.

Drive deeper into the National Park to see these magnificent creatures in person. They are easiest to spot in the morning or near sunset when they go for watering near the local streams. 

After seeing the horses, return to Khustai ger camp for lunch and return to the city.

output.name: North India Wildlife & Heritage — 8 Days
output.subtitle: Ranthambore, Corbett, and Keoladeo Ghana — tigers, elephants, and 350+ bird species across three national reserves
output.summary: This eight-day journey moves through North India's three primary wildlife reserves, combining tiger and elephant sightings with extensive birdwatching and visits to significant historical sites. The itinerary begins in Delhi, proceeds to Jaipur and Ranthambore National Park for morning and evening safaris, continues to Keoladeo Ghana Bird Sanctuary near Bharatpur, and closes with Agra's major monuments before returning to Delhi. Guides are trained wildlife naturalists; accommodation is located within or immediately adjacent to park boundaries. The trip operates year-round, though tiger and migratory bird sightings vary by season.
highlights: Morning and evening jeep safaris in Ranthambore National Park searching for Bengal tigers, leopards, and wild boar
Keoladeo Ghana Bird Sanctuary near Bharatpur — over 350 documented bird species, including migratory waterfowl from Central Asia
Elephant ride to the summit of Amber Fort in Jaipur, overlooking the Aravalli Valley
Walking tours through Keoladeo Ghana with a naturalist guide, spotting sambar deer, nilgai, and sarus cranes
Taj Mahal and Agra Fort in daylight, viewed after eight days in wildlife reserves
Fatehpur Sikri — Mughal royal complex en route to Agra
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Delhi and City Monuments
International flights arrive in Delhi, where travelers are transferred to their hotel. After breakfast, a guided walking tour covers major monuments: Raj Ghat, India Gate, the President's House exterior, Humayun's Tomb, the Lotus Temple, Qutub Minar, Mahavir Ahinsa Sthal, and Chhatarpur Temple. Overnight in Delhi.

Day 2 — Delhi to Jaipur
A 250-kilometer drive south from Delhi leads to Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan. After hotel check-in, the group travels to Chokhi Dhani, a village resort on the outskirts, for an evening of Rajasthani folk performance and traditional crafts. Overnight in Jaipur.

Day 3 — Jaipur: Forts, Temples, and City Palace
A guided day begins at Amber Fort, where an elephant ride ascends the hillside to the fort's upper levels. The afternoon includes City Palace, Birla Temple, Jantar Mantar, and Hawa Mahal. Overnight in Jaipur.

Day 4 — Jaipur to Ranthambore National Park
A 160-kilometer drive east reaches Sawai Madhopur and the lodge bordering Ranthambore National Park. The evening allows acclimatization and rest. Overnight near the park.

Day 5 — Ranthambore National Park Safaris
Morning and afternoon jeep safaris through Ranthambore National Park, searching for Bengal tigers, leopards, and birdlife. Guides navigate based on recent sightings. Overnight at lodge.

Day 6 — Ranthambore to Bharatpur: Keoladeo Ghana Bird Sanctuary
Drive 225 kilometers to Bharatpur. Visit Keoladeo Ghana with a naturalist, spotting migratory birds, sambar deer, and wetland wildlife. Overnight in Bharatpur.

Day 7 — Bharatpur to Agra via Fatehpur Sikri
Travel south to Fatehpur Sikri, where the sandstone complex reveals palace courtyards and a grand mosque. Continue to Agra, settle in, and enjoy a local magic show in the evening.

Day 8 — Agra Monuments and Return to Delhi via Mathura & Vrindavan
After breakfast, visit the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort. Drive toward Delhi with stops at Sikandra, Mathura, and Vrindavan—Krishna pilgrimage sites along the Yamuna—before arriving in Delhi to conclude the tour.

tour.subtitle: Bentota - Yala - Kitulgala - Knuckles - Sigiriya - Kalpitiya - Colombo
tour.summary: A little over two weeks of pure adventure topped up with stylish and luxury accommodation options with a scenic value. tour.itineraries:
Day 1, 2 and 3 in Bentota
Upon arrival in Sri Lanka our chauffer will transfer you to Bentota, interesting beach destination in the south coast of Sri Lanka. You have one full day of relaxing by the beach followed by an experiential walk across quaint local villages all the way to the border of Sinharaja Rain Forest where you would be able to witness some great scenery and understand the local way of life. Stay in a stylish boutique hotel by the beach.

Day 4 and 5 Yala National Park
You will be driven to Yala National Park with an enroute visit to Galle Dutch Fortress. Take a guided afternoon and morning safari in Yala National Park to see the elusive Leopard and Sloth Bears. You would also be able to go fishing with a local fisherman to learn the traditional way of fishing. Stay in a luxury tented safari camp.

Day 6 and 7 in Kitulgala
Take part in adventurous Canyoning expedition in Makandawa rain forest jumping and sliding in to natural water pools followed by an adrenaline rushed White water rafting trip in River Kelani. Stay in a stylish boutique hotel by the border of Makandawa rain forest.

Day 8 and 9 in Knuckles mountains
In to the mountains of Knuckles Range. Go trekking and explore the cloud forest and swim in a waterfall, a full day adventure in the Knuckles Mountains. Stay in a luxury mountain camp.

Day 10, 11 and 12 in Sigiriya
Cycle with villager, across rural villages passing paddy fields, farming fields and lakes all the way to Sigiriya Rock. Climb and explore the architectural masterpiece of Sigiriya Rock Fortress. Day 13, 14, 15 and 16 in Kalpitiya

Day 17 - Departure
An experiential journey comes to an end, a learning journey in the nature and quality time spent with your family, see you soon in Sri Lanka.

output.name: Sri Lanka: Coast, Rainforest & Mountain — 17 Days
output.subtitle: Bentota, Yala, Kitulgala, Knuckles, Sigiriya and Kalpitiya with private transfers and local guides
output.summary: This 17-day journey traces Sri Lanka's central regions and coasts, moving between the southern beaches of Bentota, the wildlife habitat of Yala National Park, the rainforest terrain around Kitulgala, the montane landscape of the Knuckles Range, the archaeological site at Sigiriya, and the Indian Ocean margin at Kalpitiya. The itinerary pairs terrestrial activities—trekking, canyoning, white-water rafting, cycling—with coastal and wildlife-focused excursions. Accommodation moves between small hotels, tented safari camps, mountain lodges, and beach properties. All transfers are by private vehicle with an English-speaking driver; activities are led by local guides and specialists. The route is open year-round but optimal between November and March. Itineraries can be modified in scope and activity selection to suit traveller preference and fitness level.
highlights: Beach and village walking from Bentota toward the Sinharaja Rainforest border
Guided safari in Yala National Park for leopard and sloth bear sightings
Visit to the 17th-century Dutch Fortress at Galle
Canyoning and natural pool descent in the Makandawa Rainforest
White-water rafting on the Kelani River
Cloud forest trekking and waterfall swimming in the Knuckles Range
Cycling through paddy and farming fields toward Sigiriya Rock Fortress
Ascent and architectural exploration of Sigiriya Rock
Boat-based dolphin and whale watching in the Indian Ocean from Kalpitiya
Cycling along coastal backroads in the Kalpitiya peninsula
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Bentota
Private transfer from Colombo airport to Bentota, a coastal town on the south shore. Upon arrival in Sri Lanka our chauffeur will transfer you to Bentota, an interesting beach destination on the south coast of Sri Lanka. Bentota is sited on a lagoon system and has been a tourism destination since the colonial era. Check-in to a small beachfront hotel. Remainder of the day at leisure by the beach or within the hotel grounds.

Day 2 — Bentota Beach and Local Villages
A full day unscheduled for rest and swimming by the beach. In the afternoon, a guided walk through quaint settlements adjacent to Bentota, moving inland toward the edge of the Sinharaja Rainforest. This walk passes through working agricultural areas and fishing communities, offering a view of daily life and local land use. Return to the hotel by late afternoon. Accommodation in the same beachfront hotel.

Day 3 — Bentota to Galle and Yala
Transfer southward via the coastal road to Galle, a port town on the southwestern coast. Visit the Dutch Fortress, a 17th-century fortified compound built by the Dutch East India Company, with ramparts, cannons, and colonial-era architecture still intact. Proceed onward to Yala National Park, located in the southeast. The total driving time from Bentota to Yala is approximately 4 to 5 hours with the Galle stop. Check-in to a tented safari camp within or near the park boundary. Remainder of the day at leisure.

Day 4 — Yala National Park Safari and Local Fishing
Early morning guided safari into Yala National Park. The safari targets leopard and sloth bear sightings, though wildlife viewing cannot be guaranteed. Guides use 4x4 vehicles and track animals on foot. Safari duration is typically 4 to 5 hours. Return to camp for midday rest. In the late afternoon or early evening, participate in traditional fishing with a local fisherman on a lagoon or coastal waterway adjacent to the park, learning net casting and trap techniques. Accommodation in the tented safari camp.

Day 5 — Yala National Park Morning Safari
A second guided morning safari in Yala National Park, again targeting leopard and sloth bear. Timing and route may differ from Day 4 to increase sightings. Duration approximately 4 to 5 hours. Afternoon is at leisure or available for a lighter activity within or near the camp. Late afternoon transfer begins the northwestward journey toward Kitulgala, traveling inland away from the coast. Depending on route and road conditions, this leg takes 4 to 5 hours. Check-in to a small hotel near the Makandawa Rainforest border. Overnight in Kitulgala.

Day 6 — Canyoning and Rafting in Kitulgala
A full-day adventure combining a canyoning expedition into Makandawa Rainforest—jumping and sliding into natural pools—with white water rafting on River Kelani. Return to a stylish boutique hotel set by the rainforest border.

Day 7 — Departure
Your journey through Sri Lanka's natural wonders concludes. Reflect on time spent with family and lessons learned before your departure.

Day 8 — Trekking and Swimming in Knuckles Mountains
Trek through Knuckles Range cloud forest. Swim in a waterfall before settling into your luxury mountain camp for the night.

Day 9 — Trekking in Knuckles Cloud Forest
Full-day guided trek through the Knuckles Range, traversing cloud forest habitat at elevation. The route varies by guide choice and group fitness but typically includes ridge walks, descents into moss-covered valleys, and sections of dense vegetation where visibility is limited by persistent mist and cloud cover. Duration is 6 to 7 hours of active walking. A key component is a visit to a mountain waterfall where participants can swim in a pool fed by cascade. Return to the mountain lodge by late afternoon. Accommodation in the Knuckles.

Day 10 — Knuckles to Sigiriya by Cycling
Transition day involving a transfer from the Knuckles mountains westward toward the central plateau and then to Sigiriya, a journey of approximately 2 to 3 hours by vehicle. Upon arrival in the Sigiriya region, begin a guided cycling tour through rural villages, passing paddy fields, farming plots, and small lakes. Cycle through different village routes, passing through paddy and farming fields. Participants cycle on a mix of paved village roads and unpaved tracks. The cycling is interrupted by photo stops and brief village interactions. Late afternoon check-in to a small hotel in or near Sigiriya. Accommodation in Sigiriya.

Day 11 — Sigiriya Rock Fortress Ascent and Exploration
Early morning ascent of Sigiriya Rock, a 5th-century fortress and palace site rising approximately 200 meters above the surrounding plain. The structure was built by King Kasyapa and includes a network of stairs carved or constructed into the rock face, leading through defensive gates, landscaped terraces, and mirror wall galleries to the summit palace platform. The site contains frescoes, water features, and views across the central plateau. A guide contextualizes the archaeology and layout. Return to the hotel by midday. Afternoon at leisure or available for a lighter activity such as a visit to a nearby village or cultural site. Overnight in Sigiriya.

Day 12 — Cycling and Scenic Picnic near Sigiriya
A second day in the Sigiriya region. Cycle with villagers across rural villages passing paddy fields, farming fields and lakes all the way to Sigiriya Rock. The route culminates at a scenic viewpoint overlooking lakes and rural landscape. A picnic lunch is provided at this vantage point. Afternoon return to the hotel by vehicle. Remainder of the day at leisure. Accommodation in Sigiriya.

Day 13 — Transfer to Kalpitiya Peninsula
Transfer westward from Sigiriya toward the coast, traveling to Kalpitiya, a peninsula on the northwestern shore facing the Indian Ocean. Kalpitiya is known as a marine wildlife and fishing hub. Check-in to a beachfront property. Remainder of the day at leisure or spent exploring the beach and local surroundings. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 14 — Dolphin and Whale Watching from Kalpitiya
Early morning or midday boat-based marine excursion departing from Kalpitiya into the Indian Ocean. The trip aims to sight dolphins (spinner and bottlenose species are present seasonally) and whales (sperm whales and blue whales migrate through the region, particularly between November and March). Go for a Dolphin and Whale watching boat trip in the Indian Ocean. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed. Guides identify species and explain marine ecology. Return to shore by late morning or early afternoon. Remainder of the day at leisure. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 15 — Coastal Cycling and Leisure in Kalpitiya
Cycle along the backroads of the area. Routes pass through fishing villages, lagoon edges, and agricultural plots. Time allows for stops and village interaction. Remainder of the day is unscheduled, available for swimming, rest, or informal exploration of the local area. A meal featuring local seafood can be arranged through the hotel but is not obligatory. Overnight in Kalpitiya.

Day 16 — Final Day in Kalpitiya
A full day at leisure in Kalpitiya. Options include swimming, beach walks, informal cycling, reading, or resting at the hotel. Optional activities such as an additional boat trip or a visit to a local fishing harbor can be arranged depending on interest and availability. Accommodation in Kalpitiya.

Day 17 — Departure
Transfer by private vehicle from Kalpitiya to Colombo International Airport. Depending on location of departure and check-out time, the drive takes 3 to 4 hours. Farewells and journey conclusion. The itinerary ends upon airport drop-off.

output.seo_meta: A 17-day Sri Lanka itinerary covering Bentota, Yala, Kitulgala, Knuckles, Sigiriya and Kalpitiya with trekking, wildlife safari, canyoning and cycling.
