tour.summary: A 5-day / 4-night adventure for those who want to experience Taiwan's remote natural beauty, dive deep into the country's unique Indigenous cultures and indulge in hot springs across southern Taiwan.
highlights:
Visit "Potential UNESCO World Heritage Site", Tjuvecekadan, a unique indigenous village with 50 slate stone houses
Traverse unique ecological reserves with chances to see deer, monkeys, pangolins and many rare and endemic orchids
Hike two of southern Taiwan's most famous ancient trails
Stay 3 nights in 3 and 4-star hot spring hotels
tour.itineraries:
Day One: Kaohsiung | Tjuvecekadan | Fangliao
Guests picked up at Zuoying High Speed Rail Station. Guided hike and unique community tour by indigenous hosts in one of the most spectacular sites in the country. Aboriginal lunch overlooking the mountains. A DIY activity before traveling to hotel for rest/relax before dinner.

Day Two: Jinshuiying National Trail | Taitung
Spend the day hiking a 16km National Trail renowned as a habitat for endemic, endangered animals and plants. Traverse three nature reserves, suspension bridges and arrive at Taiwan's East Coast. Transfer to a Zhiben Hot Spring Hotel.

Day Three: Taitung | Zhiben National Forest
Local indigenous tour helps guests delve deeply into the mystical Paiwan Shaman culture and distinct cuisine. Visit local wood carving studio and the first church in Taitung that merges Paiwan cultural symbols with Western beliefs. Explore Zhiben National Forest or soak in hot springs before dinner.

Day Four: Alangyi Historic Trail | Mudan
Set off to hike the famous Alangyi Historic Trail along one of Taiwan's last undeveloped coastlines. Local indigenous guide will lead group along this trail. Transfer to hot spring hotel for post-hike rest and relaxation.

Day Five: Mudan | Kaohsiung
Visit Shimen Battlefield, the site of a historic event between indigenous tribes and Japanese sailors. Hike to an abandoned village believed to once inhabit a lost pygmy tribe. Enjoy final meal in Mudan. Transfer to Zuoying High Speed Rail Station for drop off at the end of the tour.
tour.inclusions:
Private return transportation from/to Zuoying High Speed Rail
12 Meals, x2 guided community tours and DIY activities
4-nights accommodation (3-4 star hotels & hot spring hotels)
Mountain and Police Permits
Licensed, bilingual mountain guide & Indigenous Guide (Alangyi)
$3,000,000ntd daily travel agency liability insurance

output.name: Taiwan's Southern Rim: Indigenous Trails, Hot Springs & Coastal Wilderness — 5 Days
output.subtitle: Jinshuiying and Alangyi trails, three hot spring hotels, and guided access to Tjuvecekadan village across southern Taiwan
output.summary: This five-day journey traces two of southern Taiwan's established trekking routes—Jinshuiying National Trail and Alangyi Historic Trail—while staying in thermal spring accommodations and spending time in Tjuvecekadan, a Paiwan community of roughly 50 slate-stone structures. The itinerary pairs guided hikes through protected forest reserves with cultural exchanges led by Indigenous hosts, visits to local woodworking studios, and opportunities to understand Paiwan religious practice and cuisine. Transportation by private vehicle connects each stage, beginning and ending at Zuoying High Speed Rail Station near Kaohsiung.
highlights: Guided community tour of Tjuvecekadan village with Paiwan hosts, including a meal in the settlement
Jinshuiying National Trail: 16 kilometers across three nature reserves with suspension bridges, endemic flora, and access to Taiwan's East Coast
Zhiben National Forest exploration and bathing in natural hot springs near Taitung
Alangyi Historic Trail hike along Taiwan's undeveloped southern coastline, led by Indigenous guide
Visit to Shimen Battlefield and hike to an abandoned settlement with documented historical significance to the region
Stays in three separate hot spring hotel properties (3-4 star)
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Kaohsiung to Tjuvecekadan: Indigenous Village Tour and Community Meal
Private pickup occurs at Zuoying High Speed Rail Station. A guided hike leads to Tjuvecekadan, a Paiwan settlement roughly 50 minutes from the station, where a Paiwan host conducts a walking tour of the village's slate-stone architecture and settlement layout. A meal is served within the community. A hands-on activity follows before transfer to the evening's accommodation in Fangliao, where the first night is spent at a hot spring hotel.

Day 2 — Jinshuiying National Trail: 16 Kilometers Across Three Forest Reserves to the East Coast
The day is spent hiking Jinshuiying National Trail, a 16-kilometer route through three protected forest reserves. The trail passes suspension bridges and descends toward Taiwan's East Coast. Wildlife includes deer, monkeys, and pangolins; endemic and endangered orchid species grow along the route. Transfer follows to Taitung and check-in at a Zhiben hot spring hotel for the evening.

Day 3 — Taitung and Zhiben: Paiwan Culture, Woodcarving, and Forest Access
A local Indigenous guide leads a cultural tour focused on Paiwan religious practice and traditional food preparation. A visit to a local woodcarving studio follows. The group also visits the first Christian church in Taitung, which incorporates Paiwan cultural symbols into its design. The afternoon remains unstructured, allowing time to visit Zhiben National Forest or relax in the hotel's hot spring facilities before dinner.

Day 4 — Alangyi Historic Trail: Coastal Hike Along Southern Taiwan's Undeveloped Shoreline
The Alangyi Historic Trail traverses one of Taiwan's least-developed coastal sections. An Indigenous guide leads the group through the route's terrain and points of historical reference. Following the hike, transfer occurs to Mudan and a third hot spring hotel for evening rest.

Day 5 — Mudan: Shimen Battlefield, Abandoned Village, and Return to Kaohsiung
The morning begins with a visit to Shimen Battlefield, a site of documented conflict between Indigenous groups and Japanese forces. A hike follows to a nearby abandoned settlement with historical ties to early settlement patterns in the region. A final meal takes place in Mudan before private transfer returns the group to Zuoying High Speed Rail Station.
output.seo_title: Taiwan Hot Springs & Indigenous Trails — 5-Day Southern
output.seo_meta: Trek indigenous trails with Paiwan guides, relax in three hot spring hotels, and experience coastal wilderness in southern Taiwan, over 5 days.

output.name: Central Visayas Circuit: Cebu, Sumilon & Bohol — 15 Days
output.subtitle: Island and countryside journey linking Cebu's heritage sites, a three-day island stay, and Bohol's Chocolate Hills and river landscape — 15 days
output.summary: This circuit moves through the central islands of the Visayas, beginning in Cebu with its concentration of Spanish colonial churches, forts, and heritage buildings before shifting to a residential stay on Sumilon Island and a coastal stretch in Argao. The second half crosses to Bohol by ferry, where a countryside tour accesses the Man-made Forest, Chocolate Hills overlook, and a cruise on the Loboc River. The itinerary balances structured day-long excursions with longer rest periods at two accommodation bases, allowing for both guided activity and unscheduled time within each location.
highlights: Fort San Pedro and Magellan's Cross in Cebu City, Spanish colonial structures
Taoist Temple in Cebu, set on a hilltop overlooking the city and port
Three-day stay on Sumilon Island, accessible by 30-minute boat transfer from Mactan
Southern Countryside Tour from Argao including basket-weaving workshops and carabao rides
Baclayon Church in Bohol, a stone structure
Chocolate Hills panorama from the dedicated view deck on Bohol's interior plateau
Loboc River cruise with lunch, passing through mangrove channels and limestone formations
Man-made Forest near Tagbilaran, a 30-hectare planted grove accessible by ground transfer
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Cebu
Arrival at Mactan Cebu International Airport with transfer to hotel in Cebu City. Check-in and remainder of day at leisure.

Day 2 — Cebu City Heritage Tour
Morning departure on guided city tour visiting Fort San Pedro, a military fortress; Magellan's Cross, housed in a chapel; and the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño, a Roman Catholic church in the Philippines. Additional stops include the Cebu Heritage Monument, the Taoist Temple overlooking the city, and a choice between two colonial residences: Yap San Diego or Casa Gorordo. The itinerary concludes in Mactan with a visit to the Mactan Shrine and the Alegre Guitar Factory, where local artisans craft instruments from tropical wood. Lunch at a local restaurant. Return to Cebu City hotel for overnight stay.

Day 3 — Transfer to Sumilon Island
Morning transfer from Cebu City hotel to Bluewater Sumilon Jetty Port (approximately 141 kilometres, 5 hours by vehicle through coastal road). Boat transfer from the jetty to Sumilon Island Resort, approximately 30 minutes crossing open water. Check-in at resort and overnight stay.

Day 4 — Sumilon Island — Leisure Day
Full day at resort with breakfast and dinner provided. No scheduled activities.

Day 5 — Cebu — Sumilon Island
Settle into Sumilon Island for the day. Breakfast and dinner are served at the resort. Overnight stay on the island.

Day 6 — Sumilon to Argao with Southern Countryside Tour
Morning boat transfer from Sumilon Island Resort to jetty port, then ground transfer to Argao. En route, Southern Countryside Tour includes stops in Carcar for lunch at a local restaurant, followed by hands-on activities: basket-weaving demonstration, short tricycle ride through residential areas, tuba tasting at a local distillery, and carabao (water buffalo) ride. Check-in at Argao resort or guesthouse for overnight stay.

Day 7 — Argao — Leisure Day
Breakfast at hotel. Day at leisure with no scheduled excursions. Overnight stay in Argao.

Day 8 — Cebu to Bohol by Ferry
After breakfast, transfer to the seaport and board the fast craft ferry to Bohol. Check in at your resort upon arrival.

Day 9 — Argao to Bohol by Ferry
Morning transfer from Argao resort to seaport for fast-craft ferry crossing to Tagbilaran, Bohol. Upon arrival, transfer to resort for check-in and overnight stay.

Day 10 — Bohol Countryside Tour: Hills, Church & River Cruise
Guided countryside tour visiting Baclayon Church, the Man-made Forest, and Chocolate Hills View Deck. Visit the Blood Compact Shrine before an afternoon Loboc River cruise with lunch onboard. Return to resort for overnight stay.

Day 11 — Bohol — Leisure Day
Breakfast at hotel. Day at leisure; optional tours available but not included in standard itinerary. Overnight stay in Bohol.

Day 12 — Bohol — Leisure Day
Breakfast at hotel. Day at leisure; optional tours available but not included in standard itinerary. Overnight stay in Bohol.

Day 13 — Bohol — Leisure Day
Breakfast at hotel. Day at leisure; optional tours available but not included in standard itinerary. Overnight stay in Bohol.

Day 14 — Bohol to Cebu by Ferry
Morning transfer from Bohol resort to Tagbilaran seaport for return ferry crossing to Cebu. Upon arrival in Cebu City, transfer to hotel for check-in and overnight stay.

Day 15 — Departure from Cebu
Breakfast at hotel, then transfer to Mactan Cebu International Airport for onward flight.

tour.name: Uncover Korea: K Pop & Hanok Villages
tour.summary: Join the crew as we hit all the best spots in South Korea. From the markets in Seoul, the hanok village in Jeonju, through the beautiful coast along Busan and the incredible island of Jeju. With bright city lights and relaxing island sights, this tour will make you fall in love with every single thing South Korea has to offer.
highlights:
Explore the best of Seoul at HiKR Ground and Gwangjang Market
Stay overnight in a Hanok Village
Dive into a mountainside full of color with a visit to Gamcheon
Get way off the beaten track and explore Jeju island
tour.itineraries:
Day 1   Seoul
Arrive at any time and welcome to South Korea's largest metropolis. There are no activities planned until the evening welcome meeting, so spend the day exploring on your own time. In the evening, meet your group and your CEO at the welcome meeting. After, head out for an orientation walk and welcome dinner to get to know your group and the city of Seoul. After filling up on some delicious Korean food, opt to join your CEO & new friends out on the town for your First Night Out. Maybe grab a beer or choose to test your singing voice at karaoke.

Your First Night Out Moment: Connect With New Friends
Connect with new friends on your first night out in a new destination. Only available on 18-to-Thirtysomethings tours.

Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group
Your opportunity to meet your CEO and fellow travellers, and learn more about your tour. Opt to join the group for a local meal afterwards. Don't forget to see the notice in the lobby (or ask reception) for the official time and place to meet up with the group.

Accommodation
Below is an example of the hotel we may use in this city. For the actual hotel your specific departure will be using, please check your voucher.

Dream Guest House (or similar)  Guesthouse
Meals included: Dinner
Day 2   Seoul
Start your day channeling your inner K Pop star at HiKR Ground. Then head to what may be the cutest street in all of Seoul, Ikseon-Dong Alley. After some shopping, instagrammable moments, and free time for lunch, explore the Gwangjang market and try some iconic Korean snacks. Then enjoy a free evening in the city.

HiKR Ground                 Seoul
Explore the 5 story, immersive experience dedicated to all things Korea. Think K-Pop, K-Drama and the most popular parts of Korean culture. Witness incredible art, listen to your favorite K-Pop band, and learn about Korean pop-culture.

Ikseon-dong Alley          Seoul
Stroll through the narrow alleys of Ikseon-dong where traditional hanok houses, modern cafes and hip restaurants coexist. Relax in quaint cafes or shop in local craft stores while admiring the beautiful hanok architecture. Hop in and out of local boutiques and galleries, stopping at the perfect photo stops at every turn.

Free Time                       Seoul
Enjoy free time in Seoul. Check out N Seoul Tower, Gangnam neighborhood or Han River Park.

Gwangjang Market Visit      Seoul    1h
Gwangjang Market is one of the oldest and largest traditional markets in South Korea, with more than 5,000 shops. Famous for its fabric, local treasures, and noted to be one of the best places to go for authentic Korean street food in Seoul, you don't want to miss Gwangjang Market.

Optional Activities - Day 2

Gangnam District Visit       Seoul
Gangnam has plenty to do and see in this historically rich, fast-developing neighbourhood. Gangnam Station is the busiest subway station in Seoul and has a huge underground shopping centre, so feel free to shop until you drop. Choose to visit Bongeunsa, a Buddhist Temple in the centre of Gangnam, or enjoy the nightlife and restaurants in this area.

N Seoul Tower Visit            Seoul
Take the cable car to visit the most iconic landmark in Seoul! Located at the top of Mt Namsan, and standing at 480m above sea level, what used to be a broadcasting station before it was open to the public, is now a beautiful observatory. If you'd like to go up the tower to the observatory an additional fee is required.

Accommodation
Dream Guest House (or similar)
Day 3   Seoul
Seoul is yours to explore today. With endless options, there's no bad way to enjoy this city. Opt to visit the DMZ, take a K Pop dance class, go on a Seoul City Tour or try your hand at some Korean delicacies at a cooking class.

Free Time             Seoul           Full Day
The day is yours to enjoy Seoul as you wish.

Optional Activities - Day 3

Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) VisitDemilitarized Zone (DMZ)
Visit the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) the de facto border between North and South Korea, which cuts the peninsula in half. Created in 1953, it is the most heavily militarized border in the world.

K-Pop Dance Class          Seoul
Channel your inner pop star at a K-pop dance classes. Learn the latest K-pop choreography with professional instructors and feel the energy of K-pop & K-pop culture. Classes are available for various skill levels, so even beginners can participate easily. These classes often end with a recording session, allowing participants to take home a video of their performance as a special souvenir.

Seoul City Tour                 Seoul
Enjoy a bus tour of the bustling capital of South Korea. Visit different areas of the city including Gyengbokgung Palace, National Folklore Museum, Jogyesa Temple, Bukchon Hanok Village and Insadong alley.

Accommodation
Dream Guest House (or similar)    Guesthouse
Day 4   Seoul/Jeonju-si
In the morning, take the train to Jeonju, maybe the prettiest city in South Korea. After checking into your Hanok stay, take a CEO led tour of the town. Afterwards, take some time to explore the city on your own. Opt to wander through Jeonju Nambu Traditional Market, try your hand at Korean traditional handicraft at the Hanok Village Craft Museum or head to a local shop to try on a traditional Hanbok. This evening enjoy the comforts of traditional Korea and Korean culture at your hanok stay.

Jeonju Hanok Village Orientation Walk                              Jeonju
Join your CEO on a walk through some of Jeonju's special attractions, like the Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeondong Catholic Church, Korean Liquor museum and Jeonju handicraft exhibition hall. Stroll through the beautiful hanok streets and admire the traditional architecture.

Free Time                                                          Jeonju-si
Enjoy free time in Jeonju Hanok Village.

Your Local Living Moment: Hanok Village Stay
Staying in a traditional hanok gives an amazing insight to Korean history and culture. With natural material and historic architecture, it will feel like you've been transported in time.

Optional Activities - Day 4

Hanbok Wearing                   Jeonju-si
Immerse yourself into the colorful and beautiful culture of South Korea. Dress in the traditional Korean Hanbok clothing in no better place than the picturesque town of Jeonju Hanok Village. With your hair done and your hanbok on, head out into the town for some pictures.

Jeonju Hanok Village Craft Museum                  Jeonju-si
Visit the Hanok Village Craft Museum and choose to experience some of the many hands on, traditional Korean crafts activities. Choose to make Hanji, traditional Korean paper, or try the pottery wheel and shape your own ceramic bowl, vase or plate. Opt to try the art of traditional Korean calligraphy with a brush and ink to create beautiful characters. Or try your hand at fan crafting & painting. Create and decorate your very own vibrant, colorful Korean fan. Its common to see designs like flowers, birds and landscapes, so choose your favorite design and decorate how you'd like.

Accommodation
Jeonju Goeul Hanok Accommodation (or similar)        Homestay
Day 5   Jeonju-si/Busan
Today, travel by bus to Nampodong, the centre of the coastal city of Busan. After dropping your luggage off at the hostel, we'll head to the colorful mountainside village of Gamcheon. This unique artistic village is full of colorful houses, murals and galleries. It's the perfect place for photos, art and culture lovers. Spend the evening exploring Busan as you'd like.

Local Bus       Jeonju-si – Busan    3h260km
Climb aboard, grab a seat, and enjoy the ride.

Free Time       Busan
Enjoy free time in Nampodong, downtown Busan.

Gamcheon Culture Village          Busan
Explore the pastel-coloured village of Gamcheon, nestled in the side of a mountain, with uniquely painted houses, murals, cafes, and shops.

Optional Activities - Day 5

Haeundae Beach and Dongbaek Island (APEC House) Visit             Busan
Visit Haeundae Beach, one of Korea's most beautiful beaches. Enjoy a walk along the shore, or take a swim (don't forget your suit!) And see the famed APEC House built to host the Asia-Pacific Economic Corporation (APEC) summit meeting in 2005 on Dongbaek Island.

Jjimjilbang                    Busan
Treat yourself in one of Busan's jjimjilbans, a Korean spa bath house, with an array of hot spring tubs to rejuvenate mind, body, and soul.

Accommodation
EZ Stay Guest House (or similar)    Hote
Day 6    Busan
Explore the incredible city of Busan today, visiting the beautiful cliffside Buddhist complex, Haedong Yonggung Temple. See Busan from a bird's-eye view on the Songdo Cable Car. Explore Jagalchi Fish Market for some tasty Korean snacks and Gukje Traditional Market, one of Korea's biggest markets. The rest of the day is yours to enjoy some free time in Busan before flying to the beach tomorrow.

Haedong Yonggungsa Temple Visit                    Gijang-gun
Originally built in 1376, this picturesque, cliffside Buddhist temple overlooks the East China Sea. Opt to grab a bizarre local snack at the traditional market. Legend foretells that should you pray here, at least one of your wishes will come true.

Songdo Maritime Cable Car Ride                      Busan
Ride the mile long gondola up to Songo Sky Park for an amazing view of the Busan coast. Visit the Observatory deck and then take the Cable car back down.

Jagalchi Fish Market                                  Busan
Discover this market and major attraction at Nampo Port. Wander through the rows of stalls selling everything you can dream of from the sea. Watch as locals haggle for the best price and fishmongers hawk their wares.

Gukje Traditional Market                             Busan
Gukjesijang or Gukje Market is nestled near Biff Square, a well-known modern movie district in Busan. The market once was a place for refugees to earn a living over the period of the Korean War. Now, it's a bustling international market where loads of food, home goods, clothes, souvenirs and more can be found.

Optional Activities - Day 6

Skyline Luge                 Busan
Jump in a kart and cruise down the track in South Korea's Skyline Luge. Choose your path, and control your speed as you zoom down the track. Choose to ride it multiple times to experience the different tracks and don't forget to look up for an ocean view. While the luge is the main attraction, you can also zipline or ride the scenic chairlift.

Taejongdae Zip Line                 Busan
Soar above the waters of Gamji Beach at 653 meters on the various thrilling zip lines.

Accommodation
EZ Stay Guest House (or similar)   Hotel
Day 7    Busan/Jeju-si
After a free morning in Busan, fly to the subtropical island of Jeju. We'll spend the next three nights in downtown Jeju City. Settle in, then join your CEO at Dongmun Market, followed by a free night out on the town. You can opt to visit Dongmun Market at night, too, and witness the vibrant food stalls under the stars. Try some delicious black pork and wash it down with Jeju's famous orange juice. Five stars if you can find the dancing lobster stall!

Jeju Dongmun Market            Jeju-si
Visit this famous traditional market where you can try local specialties and fresh seafood - an excellent place to experience the flavors and culture of Jeju. Taste Jeju’s unique delicacies such as black pork and hallabong (tangerines) while enjoying the vibrant market atmosphere. Make sure you don't miss the famous Red Lobster Fire Dance Show while exploring the market.

PlaneBusan / Gimhae International Airport – Jeju International Airport
Look! Up in the sky! It's a bird! It's a plane! It's... yup, it is a plane, actually.

Accommodation
Visitor Guest House Jeju (or similar)   Guesthous
Day 8    Jeju-si
Spend today getting a special inside look at the cultural side of Jeju. Start today with a tour of Seongeup Folk Village and learn about life of the people of old Jeju. Then we'll hike up the volcanic pathways to the top of Seongsan Sunrise Peak, an easy but rewarding hike. output.name: South Korea: Seoul, Hanok Villages & Island — 10 Days
output.subtitle: Seoul to Jeju via Jeonju and Busan, with overnight stays in traditional hanok and visits to Gamcheon, Haedong Yonggung Temple, and Seongsan Sunrise Peak.
output.summary: This 10-day route moves through South Korea's most recognizable cultural landmarks and lesser-trafficked districts in sequence. Begin in Seoul with visits to HiKR Ground and Gwangjang Market, then take the train to Jeonju for an overnight stay in a traditional hanok house in the village's preserved quarter. The itinerary then shifts to the coast: Busan's clifftop Buddhist temple, its markets and cable car, and the pastel-painted houses of Gamcheon stacked on a mountainside. The final three days settle on Jeju Island, where the route includes a guided walk through Seongeup Folk Village, a hike to Seongsan Sunrise Peak, and a performance by haenyeo—traditional female divers who harvest seafood by breath-hold. Free time is built into most days, and optional activities (DMZ visit, K-pop dance class, cooking class) are available in Seoul and scattered throughout.
highlights: K-pop culture and Korean contemporary art at HiKR Ground, Seoul
Overnight stay in a traditional hanok house, Jeonju Hanok Village
Gamcheon Culture Village: pastel-painted houses and murals on a mountainside, Busan
Haedong Yonggungsa Temple: clifftside Buddhist complex overlooking the East China Sea, built 1376
Songdo Maritime Cable Car: one-mile gondola ride above Busan's coastline to Sky Park Observatory
Seongsan Sunrise Peak: UNESCO-designated volcanic formation on Jeju, 1–2 hour beginner hike
Haenyeo women divers: live performance and cultural exchange with Jeju's traditional female divers
Seongeup Folk Village: guided tour of traditional Jeju architecture and village life
Gwangjang Market: over 5,000 stalls of fabric, crafts, and Korean street food in Seoul
Dongmun Market: evening visit to Jeju's traditional market with local specialties and seafood
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Seoul
Arrive at any time in South Korea's capital and largest metropolis. With no planned activities until evening, you have the day free to visit Seoul independently at your own pace, whether that means wandering neighbourhoods, visiting museums, or simply adjusting to the city.

In the evening, meet your CEO and fellow travellers at the welcome meeting—your opportunity to learn more about the tour ahead and connect with your group. After the meeting, join an orientation walk through Seoul's streets to familiarize yourself with the city's layout and energy.

Dinner follows at a local Korean restaurant, where you'll share your first meal with the group and begin getting to know one another. The evening is yours to shape: those interested can opt to join your CEO and new friends for a First Night Out, exploring Seoul's bar scene or testing your singing voice at karaoke. Participation is entirely optional—if you prefer an early night, that's equally welcome.

Accommodation will be at Dream Guest House or similar.

*Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group—your chance to connect with fellow travellers and learn what lies ahead. Your First Night Out Moment (available on 18-to-Thirtysomethings tours): Connect with new friends as you visit your new destination together.*

Day 2 — Seoul: K-pop, Markets & Street Culture
Begin your morning at HiKR Ground, a five-story immersive space dedicated to Korean pop culture. The exhibition moves through K-pop performances, K-drama media, and contemporary art installations that capture what defines modern Korean culture. From there, head to Ikseon-Dong Alley, a narrow district where traditional hanok houses now sit alongside modern cafes, boutiques, and independent galleries. The architecture creates a distinctive atmosphere—each corner offers something to photograph and wander. Spend time drifting between local craft stores and quaint cafes, getting a sense of how Seoul blends heritage with contemporary life.

Lunch is yours to structure. Continue exploring Ikseon-Dong's cafes and shops, or move ahead to Gwangjang Market at your own pace. Once you arrive at Gwangjang Market, you're in one of Seoul's oldest and largest traditional markets, operating with over 5,000 vendors. The market sprawls across multiple sections: textiles and fabrics fill certain alleys, while other areas concentrate on handicrafts and local treasures. But Gwangjang is most renowned for its street food stalls—this is considered one of Seoul's best places for authentic Korean snacks and casual meals. Plan an hour to navigate the market, try local dishes, and absorb the energy of one of the city's most vital commercial and culinary spaces.

Your evening is unscheduled, leaving room to rest or pursue optional activities. If you want to visit N Seoul Tower, take the cable car up Mt. Namsan to the 480-meter observation deck—an additional fee applies for entry to the observatory. Alternatively, venture into Gangnam District, a historically rich neighborhood now defined by rapid development and constant activity. Gangnam Station itself is the city's busiest subway hub and contains an enormous underground shopping center. The district also hosts Bongeunsa, a Buddhist temple set in the neighborhood's center, and numerous restaurants and nightlife venues if you prefer to spend your evening in this area. Otherwise, simply rest at your accommodation and recharge for the days ahead.

Day 3 — Seoul: A Day of Your Own Design
Seoul is yours to wander at your own pace. With the city's efficient subway system and distinct neighborhoods, there's no bad way to spend your time here.

If you'd like structure, several optional activities are available. Visit the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), the de facto border between North and South Korea and the world's most heavily militarized frontier since its creation in 1953. Or channel your inner pop star at a K-pop dance class, where professional instructors teach the latest choreography at various skill levels. Most classes culminate in a recording session—a special souvenir to take home.

Alternatively, join a guided Seoul City Tour by bus, visiting Gyengbokgung Palace, the National Folklore Museum, Jogyesa Temple, Bukchon Hanok Village, and Insadong Alley. You might also try a Korean cooking class to learn the fundamentals of local delicacies, or simply wander neighborhoods that call to you.

Return to Dream Guest House (or similar) in the evening, having spent the day exactly as you wished.

Day 4 — Train to Jeonju & Hanok Village Overnight
Take the morning train to Jeonju, a city in the southwestern region known for its preserved traditional quarter and often called one of South Korea's prettiest cities. After checking into your hanok accommodation, your CEO leads a walking tour of Jeonju Hanok Village, pointing out key cultural landmarks including the Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeondong Catholic Church, Korean Liquor Museum, and Jeonju Handicraft Exhibition Hall. The stroll reveals the beautiful hanok streets and their distinctive traditional architecture, offering an immersive introduction to the area.

The afternoon and evening are yours to wander at your own pace. Wander through Jeonju Nambu Traditional Market to experience local commerce and daily life, or head to the Hanok Village Craft Museum to engage with Korean traditional craftsmanship firsthand. Here you can try your hand at hanji (traditional Korean paper-making), work at the pottery wheel to shape your own ceramic vessel, practice the meditative art of traditional calligraphy with brush and ink, or craft and paint your own decorative Korean fan—choosing from designs like flowers, birds, and landscapes.

If you prefer, visit a local shop to try on a hanbok, the lively traditional Korean dress, and have photographs taken in the picturesque hanok setting. The colorful, layered garments offer an authentic way to experience Korean cultural dress in its most fitting environment.

This evening, settle into the comforts of your traditional hanok house. Built with natural materials and historic architecture, the accommodation offers genuine insight into Korean history and culture—a stay that feels like stepping back in time. The experience of sleeping in a hanok is itself part of your journey through Korea's past, allowing you to absorb the aesthetic and spatial principles that have defined Korean domestic life for centuries.

Day 5 — Busan: Gamcheon Culture Village & Coastal Exploration
Travel by local bus from Jeonju to Busan, a 3-hour, 260-kilometer journey down to Korea's southern coast. Upon arrival, drop your luggage at your accommodation in Nampodong, the lively downtown district, then make your way to Gamcheon Culture Village. This artistic neighborhood clings to a mountainside, its narrow lanes lined with pastel-colored houses, hand-painted murals, small cafes, and independent galleries. The village draws photographers and art lovers alike, offering endless opportunities to wander and see. Spend the late afternoon and early evening exploring the village's atmospheric streets before returning to downtown Busan for the night.

If you prefer a more active evening, two optional activities await. Haeundae Beach is one of Korea's most celebrated stretches of sand—ideal for an evening walk along the shore or a swim, depending on season. Adjacent Dongbaek Island features the APEC House, a distinctive structure built to host the 2005 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Alternatively, experience a traditional Korean jjimjilbang (spa bath house), where you can soak in hot-spring tubs and rejuvenate after your travel day.

Day 6 — Busan: Temples, Cable Car & Markets
Start your day at Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, a striking Buddhist complex built in 1376 and perched on cliffs overlooking the East China Sea. The temple's seaside setting is singular in Korea—legend holds that prayers offered here will grant at least one wish. From the temple, make your way to the Songdo Maritime Cable Car for a one-mile gondola ride up to Songdo Sky Park. The observatory deck provides sweeping views across Busan's coastline and harbor.

In the afternoon, head to Jagalchi Fish Market at Nampo Port, where fishmongers sell fresh seafood from countless stalls. This is where locals come to haggle for the best catch; watching the negotiation unfold offers genuine insight into daily Busan life. Nearby, visit Gukje Traditional Market, set close to BIFF Square (named after the Busan International Film Festival). The market's roots trace back to the Korean War, when it served as a refuge for displaced people seeking livelihood. Today it's a lively bazaar offering food, home goods, clothing, and souvenirs alongside the history.

The remainder of your day is unscheduled, leaving space to rest or wander at your own pace before tomorrow's transfer to the beach.

If you want more activity, two options stand out: Skyline Luge lets you control a kart down a mountaintop track with ocean views—you can ride multiple courses and even try the adjacent zipline or scenic chairlift. Alternatively, Taejongdae Zip Line offers a more intense rush: soar 653 meters above Gamji Beach on one of several thrilling lines suspended over the water.

Day 7 — Flight to Jeju & Dongmun Market
After a free morning in Busan, fly south to Jeju, the subtropical island off Korea's southern tip. Settle into your accommodation in downtown Jeju City, where you'll stay for the next three nights. This evening, join your CEO at Dongmun Market, one of Jeju's most lively traditional markets. The market pulses with energy after dark—neon signs illuminate food stalls, vendors call out their wares, and the air fills with the aroma of grilling black pork, a local specialty. Sample hallabong, Jeju's famous tangerines, and wash them down with fresh orange juice. Keep an eye out for the Red Lobster Fire Dance Show, a street performance that appears among the stalls. The market offers a genuine slice of local culture and flavour; wandering its lanes unguided lets you see what catches your interest. The rest of the evening is yours to wander further or rest after your journey.

Day 8 — Jeju: Folk Village, Sunrise Peak & Haenyeo Divers
Today unfolds as a deep immersion into Jeju's cultural landscape, beginning with the tangible past and ending with living tradition.

Start with a guided tour of Seongeup Folk Village, a living museum that preserves the domestic life of old Jeju. Walk through traditional homes built with volcanic stone, observe harubang—the well-known stone statues that dot the island—and examine lava walls that shaped settlement patterns for centuries. The village offers an unfiltered view of how Jeju residents organized their homes, worked their land, and structured daily life before modernization.

From there, make your way to Seongsan Sunrise Peak (Seongsan Ilchulbong), a UNESCO World Heritage Site that rises dramatically from the coastal plain. The hike covers 1–2 kilometers on a well-maintained trail suitable for all fitness levels. As you ascend the volcanic pathways, you'll learn that this peak formed roughly 5,000 years ago during an underwater volcanic eruption—a geological event that created one of Jeju's most distinctive landmarks. The views from the summit extend across the island's volcanic terrain and out toward the sea, making the modest effort entirely worthwhile.

In the afternoon, transition to Hamdeok Beach. Here you have flexibility: spend time on the white sand and in the turquoise water, or take a shorter walk along the Olle Trail, the famous 437-kilometer loop hiking network that circumnavigates Jeju's perimeter. The Olle sections are well-marked and offer coastal perspectives that complement the morning's interior exploration.

As evening approaches, gather for the haenyeo performance—arguably the day's centerpiece. Haenyeo are Jeju's female divers, a tradition spanning centuries. Watch these women, some well into their 80s, descend into the sea and hold their breath for extended periods while harvesting abalone, conch, sea cucumbers, and other seafood. Their technique is both meditative and physically demanding, elegant through generations. After the performance concludes, you'll have time to interact directly with the divers—ask questions, observe their catch up close, and if inclined, purchase fresh seafood directly from them.

Finally, your guide will lead the group into downtown Jeju for the evening. This is your Big Night Out—a chance to celebrate with new friends and reflect on the day's experiences. Karaoke venues dot the area; local beer and fresh juice are both excellent options. Participation is entirely optional: some may prefer quieter reflection at a café or early rest before the next day's adventures. Either way, the evening belongs to the group to share as you wish.

Day 9 — Jeju Island: Your Choice of Exploration
This full day is yours to spend however you wish, with plenty of compelling options across the island. Whether you prefer active adventure, cultural immersion, or simple relaxation, Jeju offers something for every traveler.

Beach lovers should consider Geumneung Beach or Hyeopjae Beach, both offering peaceful settings to unwind and take in the island's coastline. If you're seeking more active pursuits, the Olle Trail presents an excellent opportunity. This 437 km loop circumnavigates the island's edge, featuring nature walks, cultural sites, waterfalls, and spectacular coastal views. Routes 6 and 7 are among the most popular sections. Your CEO can advise on logistics for reaching trailheads and can help you plan either a half-day or full-day hike suited to your fitness level.

For those interested in volcanic geology, the oreums—small dormant volcanic cones scattered across Jeju—offer accessible hiking with rewarding rewards. Seongsan Ilchulbong and Darangshi Oreum are particularly popular, with trails ranging from easy to moderate difficulty. The hikes showcase lush vegetation and diverse wildlife while providing commanding views across the island's landscape.

Culturally minded visitors should visit Bunker des Lumières, an immersive art exhibition housed in a former bunker in Jeju-si. The space uses advanced projection technology to display famous artworks across the bunker's interior walls, creating a mesmerizing experience as lively, moving images of masterpieces surround you as you walk through. The exhibition rotates its themes regularly, offering fresh perspectives with each visit.

Alternatively, you might spend time exploring Jeju City itself, wandering its neighborhoods and discovering local cafes, shops, and street-level culture at your own pace.

Your CEO has additional suggestions and can help with transportation logistics to reach various sections of the island, whether you're heading to a specific trailhead, beach, or attraction. The key is to take the day at your own rhythm and experience Jeju in whatever way appeals to you most.

Day 10 — Departure from Jeju
Depart at any time. Your guide can assist with onward travel arrangements or suggestions for extending your stay on Jeju or elsewhere in South Korea.

tour.subtitle: Mesmerizing View from the Poonhill
tour.summary: The Ghorepani Poonhill Trek stands out as one of Nepal’s most favored short treks. Situated in the Annapurna region, it is renowned for its vibrant Rhododendron forests that add a brilliant touch to the trail in spring. This trek is especially celebrated for its iconic viewpoint at Poonhill, offering stunning sunrise vistas and a sweeping panoramic view of the Himalayan ranges including majestic peaks like Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiun Chuli, Dhampus Peak, Nilgiri, and Machhapuchre.
highlights:
Iconic sunrise view from Poonhill (3,210m) overlooking a panorama of major Himalayan peaks including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Manaslu, Machhapuchhre, and more
Trek through vibrant Rhododendron forests, especially stunning in spring when in full bloom
Scenic 25-minute flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara with aerial Himalayan views
Pass through Banthati village on an uphill trail rich in natural scenery
Visit the Deurali viewpoint en route from Ghorepani to Tadhapani
Explore Ghandruk, a traditional Gurung community village, and visit the Gurung cultural museum
Relax and rejuvenate at the natural Jhinu Hot Spring, perfect for soothing tired muscles after days of trekking
Trek through diverse terrain — forests, streams, ridgelines, and mountain villages
Suitable for beginner to moderate trekkers — no technical climbing required
Total trek duration of approximately 5–6 days on trail, covering scenic routes between Ulleri, Ghorepani, Tadhapani, Ghandruk, and Jhinu
Full 8-day itinerary including arrival, flights, and rest days in both Kathmandu and Pokhara

Day 1: ARRIVAL IN KATHMANDU
At an arrival at the international airport we will be picked up and then transferred to the hotel. Check in at the hotel and stay overnight.

Day 2: FLIGHT TO POKHARA AND DRIVE TO ULLERI [25 MINUTES FLIGHT, 3 HRS. DRIVE; 52 KMS / 2050 METERS, 6726 FT]
From Kathmandu you take a flight to Pokhara with a scenic view of Himalayan ranges, from the window seat. On reaching Pokhara, we will drive to Ulleri and stay overnight.

Day 3: TREK ULLERI TO GHOREPANI [4-5 HRS. TREK; 10 KM / 2874 METERS, 9429 FT.]
We will make a uphill trek to Ghorepani via Banthati village. It is a short yet scenic hike to Ghorepani, with blooming rhododendron flowers enhancing the beauty of the trek route. Stay overnight in Ghorepani.

Day 4: TREK GHOREPANI TO TADHAPANI [6-7 HRS. TREK; 11 KM / 2680 METERS, 8792 FT.]
We will wake up early this morning to enjoy the sunrise view from the Poonhill (3210 m, 10532 ft.) view point. The sunrise view over Mt. Dhaulagiri (8167m.), Tukuche Peak (6920m.), Nilgiri (6940m.), Varaha Shikhar (7847m.), Annapurna I (8091m.), Annapurna South (7219m.), Annapurna III (7855m.), Machhapuchhre (6993m.), Annapurna IV (7525m.), Annapurna II (7937m.), Lamjung Himal (6931m.), Manaslu (8156m) ranges and other snowcapped mountain peaks looks majestic from Poonhill. After returning to Ghorepani after a sunrise view, we start a trek to Tadhapani with a uphill climb till we reach Deurali view point. Then through the forests and downhill through the streams and a gentle uphill at the end to reach Tadhapani.

Day 5: TREK TADHAPANI TO GHANDRUK [3-4 HRS. TREK; 6.3 KM / 1950 METERS, 6398 FT.]
Ghandruk is a Gurung community village. We can witness the local culture and lifestyle of Gurung community by exploring the Gurung community museum. It is a short trek to reach Ghandruk

Day 6: TREK GHANDRUK TO JHINU HOTSPRING [5-6 HRS. TREK; 9.8 KM / 1750 METERS, 5741 FT.]
On this day we will set out for the Jhinu Hotspring via Komrong Danda (2220 m, 7284 ft.). The trail is a gentle uphill on this day. We can relax and loosen our muscle and joint pains if any gotten during the treks. It is nearly 5-6 hours trek.

Day 7: HIKE TO MOTKYU & DRIVE TO POKHARA [TREK; 1 HRS, DRIVE; 3-4 HRS., 55 KM / 822 METERS, 2696 FT.]
After breakfast we will leave Jhinu hotspring and hike to Motkyu to catch a jeep back to Pokhara. On reaching Pokhara we will leave you free for the day for relaxation and personal activities.

Day 8: FLY BACK TO KATHMANDU AND REST DAY
After spending relaxing day in Pokhara we will then head to
Kathmandu. We will take a short flight back to Kathmandu and
stay overnight. You can use the free time on this day on your
disposal for personal activities.

output.name: Ghorepani Poonhill Trek — 8 Days in the Annapurna Region
output.subtitle: Alpine ridgeline trek from Ulleri to Jhinu Hot Spring, with sunrise from 3,210m Poonhill and rhododendron forests in spring
output.summary: The Ghorepani Poonhill Trek is a five- to six-day walk through Nepal's Annapurna region, bookended by stays in Kathmandu and Pokhara. The route moves upward from the village of Ulleri through rhododendron forest — thick with bloom in spring — to the ridge settlement of Ghorepani, where a pre-dawn ascent to Poonhill viewpoint (3,210 meters) offers clear sight lines to a line of major peaks: Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I through IV, Machhapuchre, Manaslu, Nilgiri, and Lamjung Himal. From there, the trek descends through forests and streams toward the traditional Gurung village of Ghandruk, then continues to the thermal springs at Jhinu, where trekkers can soak in natural hot water before departing overland to Pokhara. output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kathmandu
You'll be met at Kathmandu's international airport and transferred to your hotel. Check in and settle in for your first night in Nepal's lively capital.

Day 2 — Flight to Pokhara and Drive to Ulleri
A 25-minute flight from Kathmandu to Pokhara offers window views of the Himalayan ranges. On arrival, a three-hour drive (52 kilometers) northward reaches the village of Ulleri (2,050 meters), the starting point for the trek. Overnight stay in Ulleri.

Day 3 — Trek Ulleri to Ghorepani via Banthati
An uphill trek of four to five hours (10 kilometers) ascends through Banthati village into rhododendron forest, particularly vivid in spring bloom. The route reaches Ghorepani (2,874 meters) by afternoon. Overnight at a lodge in Ghorepani.

Day 4 — Sunrise at Poonhill and Trek to Tadhapani
An early start allows a short ascent to Poonhill (3,210 meters) for sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Clear conditions reveal Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Tukuche Peak (6,920m), Nilgiri (6,940m), Varaha Shikhar (7,847m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South (7,219m), Annapurna III (7,855m), Machhapuchre (6,993m), Annapurna IV (7,525m), Annapurna II (7,937m), Lamjung Himal (6,931m), and Manaslu (8,156m). The main trek follows a six- to seven-hour (11-kilometer) route from Ghorepani to Tadhapani (2,680 meters), ascending to the Deurali viewpoint, then descending through forest and stream crossings before a gentle uphill finish. Overnight at a lodge in Tadhapani.

Day 5 — Trek Tadhapani to Ghandruk
A three- to four-hour trek (6.3 kilometers) descends to Ghandruk (1,950 meters), a Gurung community settlement. Village exploration includes a visit to the Gurung cultural museum. Overnight at a lodge in Ghandruk.

Day 6 — Trek Ghandruk to Jhinu Hot Spring
A gentle five- to six-hour trek descends through Komrong Danda (2,220 meters) toward Jhinu Hot Spring. The 9.8-kilometer route loses elevation gradually, easing muscle and joint fatigue accumulated over previous days. Natural thermal pools await at day's end, offering soothing recovery in the mountain air. Overnight accommodation sits near the springs.

Day 7 — Hike to Motkyu and Drive to Pokhara
After breakfast, we hike one hour from Jhinu Danda to Motkyu, where a jeep awaits for the drive back to Pokhara. The journey covers 55 kilometers over three to four hours, descending 822 meters. Arriving in Pokhara, the afternoon is yours for rest and personal activities.

Day 8 — Flight to Kathmandu and Rest Day
A short flight returns you from Pokhara to Kathmandu. You'll have the remainder of the day free for personal activities—perhaps last-minute shopping, visits to sites you may have missed, or simply rest before your overnight stay.

output.summary: This three-day route moves through the historical core of North India, beginning in Delhi with Mughal-era monuments — the Humayun Tomb, the Qutub Minar, and the India Gate. Day 1 — Delhi: Mughal and Modern Monuments
Arrival at Delhi and transfer to the city centre for a guided tour of the capital's principal sites. Humayun Tomb, designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas, stands as an early example of Indo-Islamic architecture. Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is a 73-metre tower begun in 1193 by Qutub-ud-din Aibak. India Gate, located on the Rajpath, functions as a war memorial on the eastern edge of New Delhi's ceremonial axis. The presidential residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan (formerly Viceroy's House), marks the western end of the Rajpath. The Lotus Temple, a Bahá'í House of Worship completed in 1986, is noted for its flowerlike architectural form. In late afternoon, transfer to Agra begins — approximately a three-hour drive. Evening check-in at the Agra hotel.

Day 2 — Agra: Taj Mahal, Fort & Fatehpur Sikri
Early morning visit to the Taj Mahal at sunrise, when light conditions are most favourable. The ivory-white marble mausoleum, commissioned in 1632 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan, stands on the south bank of the Yamuna River and was built to house the tomb of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Following sunrise views, return to the hotel for breakfast before touring Agra Fort, the main residence of Mughal emperors until the capital shifted to Delhi in 1638. In early afternoon, depart for Jaipur — approximately a four-hour journey. En route, a stop at Fatehpur Sikri allows time to walk through the remains of this 16th-century imperial capital, which Emperor Akbar established as the seat of Mughal power from 1571 to 1585. Evening arrival and check-in in Jaipur.

Day 3 — Jaipur: Palaces, Astronomy & City Architecture
After breakfast, begin a guided tour of Jaipur, the planned capital city of Rajasthan. Amber Fort, on a hillside overlooking the city, was begun by Raja Man Singh I in 1592 and completed by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century; elephant rides to the fort entrance are available. The City Palace complex, including the Chandra Mahal and Mubarak Mahal, is a blend of Rajasthani and European architecture and remains partially in use by the royal family. Jantar Mantar, a collection of astronomical instruments constructed by Sawai Jai Singh II, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and reflects observational practice. The Hawa Mahal, a five-storey pink-sandstone structure built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, is the most recognizable landmark in the city. Jal Mahal, a palace set in the centre of Man Sagar Lake, was enlarged and renovated by Maharaja Jai Singh II in the 18th century. In late afternoon, depart Jaipur for Delhi — approximately a five-hour drive. Evening transfer to Delhi Airport for departure.

tour.name: Citadel Rajasthan With Architectural Wonders And The Ganges
highlights:
Destination:- Neemrana, Samode, Jaipur, Kishangarh, Pushkar, Chandelao, Jodhpur, Narlai, Ranakpur, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Bundi, Bandarej, Agra, Mathura/Vrindavan, Gwalior, Orchha, Khajuraho, Varanasi, Delhi

Major Attractions: Old & New Delhi Sightseeing, Historical Palaces/Forts, The Taj Mahal, Ganges Boat ride, Mughal architecture, Elephant ride at Amber Fort, Camel Safari over Sand Dunes, Visit of 5 UNESCO world Heritage sites, Colourful culture of North India, Rural Villages, Ancient Temples, 1000 Years Old Step Wells, Desert Sunset & Sunrise
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 : Delhi - Neemrana: Welcome to Incredible India!

You will be welcomed at Delhi international airport and transferred straight to Neemrana. On arrival; check in at your beautiful heritage hotel. Rest of the day kept at leisure.
Day 2 : Samode

Morning you may take a village walk and visit the nearby step-well. Later proceed straightway to Samode. On arrival, check in your beautiful “Samode Palace”. Evening you may enjoy the walking tour in the village or may enjoy a camel ride at Sand Dunes. Enjoy the dusk at desert on camel’s back.
Day 3 : Excursion to Jaipur

After breakfast proceed for the excursion of Jaipur. Visit the splendid Amber Fort and Maharaja's City Palace (the home of the erstwhile royal family). Later visit the signature building of Jaipur i.e. Hawa Mahal (the Palace of winds) and then enjoy rickshaw ride in the old city. Stay overnight at your palace hotel.
Day 4 : Kishangarh

After a leisurely breakfast proceed towards Kishangarh. Enroute you may enjoy lunch at ‘Pachewargarh Fort’- a 300 years old Fort, situated in a lively little village namely Pachewar. Later you will be transferred straightway to your beautiful heritage hotel named as ‘Phool Mahal’. Kishangarh is mainly known for its world famous Miniature Paintings & Handicrafts. It also has the largest marble and granite cutting industry in India. During the day you may enjoy a visit of many old havelis (mansions) and local colourful makets.
Day 5 : Excursion to Pushkar

Morning proceed to visit the famous Dev Narayana Temple at Dev Doongri. It is believed to be the only place in the world with a temple of nine planets. Later proceed for an excursion to one of the holiest cities of Rajasthan i.e. Pushkar. On arrival, take a walk on the street around the sacred pond and ghats up to Brahma temple. Later visit the Akbar's Palace and Mausoleum. Return to Kishangarh by evening and stay overnight in your hotel.
Day 6 : Chandelao

Morning after breakfast drive to Chandelao. Chandelao village is located just 40 kms ahead from Jodhpur city on the edge of the Thar Desert. On arrival, check in at ‘Chandelao Garh Fort’. Evening you may enjoy a visit to the local village to get a first hand impression of 'Rural India'. Chandelao Village is a typical Rajasthani village where you will find Tibel community. You may get to see the local craftsmen at work viz. the goldsmith, the blacksmith and the weaver during your visit. The village also has three beautifull lakes where you may see a modest variety of birds.
Day 7 : Excursion to Jodhpur

Morning proceed for an excursion to the sun city of India “Jodhpur”. On arrival, visit the magnificent Mehrangarh fort and Jaswant Thada. Later you may enjoy a walking tour to the old markets around Clock Tower. Return back to Chandelao by the evening. After brief leisure you may visit the famous bazaars of Pipar. The Pipar Bazaar is renwoned for ethnic items and local crafts. Here you may also visit the Block Printers. Stay overnight at your heritage hotel.
Day 8 : Narlai

Morning proceed to Narlai passing through scenic landscape of Aravalli hill ranges. On arrival, check in your beautiful palace hotel, situated in the serene forest. After brief leisure enjoy a visit to Khejarla Village where Bishnoi community habitats in multitude. It is really interesting to observe their rustic way of life and rituals. Later you will be visiting a nearby village namely Salawas. It is well known for producing durries, bed covers, carpets, rugs and tents using Camel/Goat hair, wool & cotton. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 9 : Excursion to Kumbhalgarh & Ranakpur

Morning move for an excursion to Kumbhalgarh. On arrival visit the beautiful Kumbhalgarh fort.

Later you will be driven to Ranakpur to visit the incomparable Ranakpur Jain temple- the huge 15th century Adinatha Temple. It is among the biggest Jain Temples in India. Return back to Narlai by evening and stay overnight at your palace hotel.
Day 10 : Udaipur - Chittorgarh

Morning after breakfast drive to Udaipur- one of the most romantic cities of India (also known as the Lake City). After checking in, you may visit the Bharatiya Lok Kala Museum (has an interesting collection of dresses, turbans, musical instruments, dolls, paintings, the traditional puppets etc.) and Shilpgram craft village.

In the second half, visit the City Palace & Saheliyon ki Bari. Later drive to Chittorgarh and check in at your heritage hotel.
Day 11 : Chittorgarh

Morning proceed to visit Chittaurgarh Fort - the symbol of Rajput pride and honour. Also visit the Vijay Stambh & Sanwalia Seth temple – a famous temple of ‘lord Krishna’. Interestingly, the local farmers here make the deity partner in their earnings & very religiously donate the share of the deity to the temple on a regular basis. Later you may visit a village school.
Day 12 : Bundi

After breakfast drive towards Bundi - a charming old town. En route visit the Mendalgarh Fort and beautiful temples of Bijalyan & Menal. On arrival, check in at your heritage hotel. Remaining day is at leisure till next morning.
Day 13 : Bundi

Post breakfast proceed to visit Bundi which includes the impressive Taragarh Fort and the characteristic palace complex where the Chitrashala has some of the finest miniature paintings in India. Later visit the nearby temple village of Keshorai Patan for an interesting Deep Daan ceremony in which women chant songs and prayers and float diya candle lamps on the river. Bundi is also famous for its stepwells and water buildings which can be visited in the evening and there are also tribal villages nearby.
Day 14 : Bhandarej

Morning drive to Bhandarej passing through small towns/villages and a series of fields. On arrival, check in at Bhandarej Palace which has an excellent blend of Mughal & Rajputana architecture. The nearby Bhangarh village with its temples and historical sites has a history which dates back to 11th century. After brief leisure enjoy a visit to Abhaneri village to see the most famous step well of Rajasthan.
Day 15 : Agra

Morning after breakfast drive to Agra en route visiting Fatehpur Sikri – once the capital city of Mughal Empire. Finally reach Agra and check in at your hotel. After brief leisure enjoy a guided sightseeing tour of Agra Fort.
Day 16 : Excursion to Mathura & Vrindavan

At dawn proceed to visit the magnificent Taj Mahal. Later proceed for the excursion to Mathura- one of the biggest pilgrimage destinations in India Mathura is believed to be the place where Lord Krishna had grown up. Later you will be visiting Vrindavan. You will visit Govind Dev Temple, Rangaji Temple, Madan Mohan Temple, Glass Temple and Bankey Bihari Temple (one of the oldest temples in India) during the day.
Day 17 : Orchha

Early morning, you may visit the amazing backside view of Taj Mahal across the Yamuna River. Post breakfast you will be driven to Orchha. En route visit the marvelous Gwalior Fort. Later drive towards Orchha - a historical site located on the banks of Betwa River. On arrival, check in your hotel and stay overnight.
Day 18 : Orchha

Morning after breakfast enjoy a sightseeing tour of Orchha including visit of Raj Mahal Palace, Raj Praveen Mahal Palace, Jehangir palace and the Royal Chhattries (cenotaphs). Later visit the Raja Ram temple - only place in India where Lord Rama is worshipped as a king. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 19 : Khajuraho

Morning after breakfast drive straightway to Khajuraho. On arrival, check in at your hotel. After brief leisure enjoy the visit of western group of temples. Later visit the eastern group of temples famous for their erotic sculptures. Evening Sound & Light show (English version) is highly recommendable here. Interestingly, Khajuraho is also a nice place for someone who loves Wood-fire Pizzas as it has some nice roof-top Italian restaurants.
Day 20 : Khajuraho - Fly to Varanasi (Kashi)

Morning board a flight to Varanasi. Varanasi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities of the world and also known as 'Kashi' & 'Banaras'. After brief leisure, visit Sarnath to visit the Buddhist temple and Stupa. Evening enjoy a boat ride over mighty river Ganga to witness the Ganga worship ceremony from a close quarter. Stay overnight at your hotel.
Day 21 : Varanasi (Kashi)

Morning enjoy a boat ride over river Ganges. Later proceed for a sightseeing tour of Varanasi city, which includes visit to Bharat Mata temple, Durga temple, Benaras Hindu University, Vishwanath Temple and a museum i.e. 'Bharat Kala Mandir' which has collection of 12th century’s old manuscripts, miniature painting and sculptures. Evening at appropriate time you will be transferred to Varanasi railway station to board an overnight train to Delhi.
Day 22 : Delhi

On arrival at Delhi railway station you will be assisted and will be transferred to your hotel/guest house to wash-change & brief leisure. Later at appropriate time you will be transferred to Delhi international airport for your onward journey. The tour ends here.

output.name: Rajasthan & the Ganges: Forts, Temples & River — 22 Days
output.subtitle: From Delhi through Rajasthan's palaces and deserts to Varanasi on the Ganges, visiting five UNESCO World Heritage sites across 22 days.
output.summary: This 22-day itinerary traverses northern India from Delhi through Rajasthan's network of fortified cities, temple towns, and desert villages, before descending to the Ganges Valley and Varanasi. The route connects ten major stops—Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Agra, and others—each hosting significant architecture from Mughal, Rajput, and Jain periods. Travellers visit five UNESCO World Heritage sites including the Taj Mahal, Khajuraho temples, and multiple fort complexes. The journey balances large towns with smaller heritage hotels in lesser-known towns like Narlai, Bundi, and Orchha, and includes optional activities in rural villages, camel safaris in desert regions, and boat rides on the Ganges. The final leg moves by train from Varanasi to Delhi.

Morning excursion to Jaipur. Visit Amber Fort, a hilltop complex overlooking the city, with optional elephant rides available. Tour the City Palace, the former residence of the royal household and still partly inhabited. Visit Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds), the five-storey pink sandstone structure well-known to Jaipur's skyline. Afternoon rickshaw ride through the old city market areas. Overnight at a heritage hotel in Jaipur.

Day 4 — Jaipur to Kishangarh: Pachewar Fort and Marble Country
Travel from Jaipur to Kishangarh Lunch stop at Pachewargarh Fort, a 300-year-old structure in Pachewar village. On arrival in Kishangarh, check-in at a heritage hotel. Three nearby lakes support modest bird populations. The village environment offers views of typical rural Rajasthani settlement patterns and agricultural land.

Day 7 — Jodhpur Excursion: Mehrangarh Fort and Clock Tower Markets
Morning excursion to Jodhpur, approximately 40 kilometres away. Visit Mehrangarh Fort, a large fortified complex dominating the city's skyline, and Jaswant Thada, a 19th-century marble cenotaph nearby. Walking tour of the old city markets around the Clock Tower. Optional visit to Pipar Bazaar, known for local textiles and block-printing workshops. Return to Chandelao by evening. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 8 — Narlai: Aravalli Foothills and Community Villages
Travel to Narlai through the Aravalli hill ranges, passing agricultural and forested terrain. Check-in at a heritage palace hotel in a forest setting. Afternoon visit to Khejarla Village, where the Bishnoi community resides. The Bishnoi practice specific agricultural and spiritual traditions centred on environmental protection and animal welfare; visitors may observe village routines and daily life. Evening visit to Salawas village, known for production of traditional carpets, rugs, and textiles woven from camel hair, goat hair, wool, and cotton. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 9 — Kumbhalgarh & Ranakpur: Forts and Jain Temples
Morning excursion to Kumbhalgarh Fort, a fortified hilltop complex in the Aravalli range. Afternoon travel to Ranakpur to visit the Adinatha Temple, a large 15th-century Jain structure The temple is one of the largest Jain temples in India. Return to Narlai by evening. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 10 — Udaipur: City Palace, Museums & Lake City
Travel to Udaipur Check-in at a hotel. Visit Bharatiya Lok Kala Museum, housing traditional dress, turbans, musical instruments, puppets, and paintings from Rajasthani culture. Visit Shilpgram, a craft village with demonstrations and sales of local textiles and handmade items. Late afternoon travel to Chittorgarh Check-in at a heritage hotel.

Day 11 — Chittorgarh: Fort and Temple Complex
Morning visit to Chittorgarh Fort, a large hilltop structure with multiple palaces, temples, and water tanks spanning several centuries of Rajput architecture. Visit Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory), a tall commemorative tower within the fort complex, and Sanwalia Seth Temple, dedicated to Lord Krishna. Optional visit to a local village school. Day 12 — Bundi: Journey to the Old Town
Travel to Bundi En route, visit Mendalgarh Fort and temples at Bijalyan and Menal. Check-in at a heritage hotel in Bundi's old quarter. Remainder of day at leisure.

Day 13 — Bundi: Palaces, Miniature Paintings & Stepwells
Morning visit to Taragarh Fort, a fortified hill structure, and the adjacent palace complex featuring the Chitrashala, a room with miniature paintings from the Bundi school. Afternoon visit to Keshorai Patan village temple. Evening optional viewing of the stepwells and water structures for which Bundi is known. These include Raniji ki Baoli, a multi-storey stepwell. Optional visit to nearby tribal villages. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 14 — Bhandarej: Mughal and Rajput Architecture
Travel to Bhandarej, passing small towns, villages, and agricultural fields. Check-in at Bhandarej Palace, a structure blending Mughal and Rajput architectural styles. Optional afternoon visit to Bhangarh village, featuring temples and historical structures dating to the 11th century. Evening visit to Abhaneri village to see Chand Baoli, a large stepwell with multiple levels of arched recesses, among the largest stepwells in Rajasthan. Overnight at heritage hotel.

Day 15 — Agra: Fatehpur Sikri & Agra Fort
Travel to Agra En route, visit Fatehpur Sikri, a walled city built in the 16th century as a Mughal capital and later abandoned. The site contains palaces, courtyards, and mosques. Arrival in Agra and check-in at a hotel. Afternoon guided tour of Agra Fort, a large riverside complex with multiple palaces and walls. Overnight at hotel.

Day 16 — Taj Mahal, Mathura & Vrindavan: Religious Sites
Early morning visit to the Taj Mahal, a marble mausoleum built in the 17th century. The structure is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Travel to Mathura, a major pilgrimage destination believed to be associated with Krishna's childhood Visit temples including Govind Dev Temple, Rangaji Temple, Madan Mohan Temple, and Bankey Bihari Temple, one of the oldest temples in the town. Afternoon or evening visit to Vrindavan, an adjacent pilgrimage town. Optional visit to Glass Temple. Overnight in Agra.

Day 17 — Gwalior Fort & Orchha: River Palace Towns
Optional early morning visit to the Taj Mahal from the Yamuna River's far bank. Midday travel to Orchha En route, visit Gwalior Fort, a large hilltop fortress with palaces and temples. Arrival in Orchha, a historical settlement on the Betwa River. Check-in at a hotel. Overnight at hotel.

Day 18 — Orchha: Palaces and Royal Temples
Morning sightseeing tour of Orchha, including Raj Mahal Palace, Raj Praveen Mahal Palace, and Jehangir Palace, all part of a palace complex built over centuries. Visit the Royal Chhatris, cenotaphs of former rulers. Afternoon visit to Raja Ram Temple, a shrine where Lord Rama is worshipped as a ruling monarch rather than a deity alone. Overnight at hotel.

Day 19 — Khajuraho: Temple Complexes and Sculptures
Travel to Khajuraho Check-in at a hotel. Afternoon visit to the Western Group of temples, a cluster of structures built between the 10th and 11th centuries. Visit the Eastern Group of temples, also dating to the medieval period and notable for their sculptural detail. Evening Sound and Light show (English narration) at one of the temple complexes. Overnight at hotel.

Day 20 — Varanasi: Flight, Sarnath & Ganges Boat Ride
Morning flight to Varanasi, a city on the Ganges River and one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in the world. Check-in at a hotel. Afternoon visit to Sarnath, approximately 10 kilometres away, home to a Buddhist temple and stupa marking the location where Buddha taught. Evening boat ride on the Ganges to observe the Ganga Aarti, an evening ritual performed at the water's edge. Overnight at hotel.

Day 21 — Varanasi: City Temples, University & River
Early morning boat ride on the Ganges to observe sunrise and ghats (riverside steps). Morning sightseeing tour of Varanasi including Bharat Mata Temple, Durga Temple, Vishwanath Temple, and Banaras Hindu University. Visit Bharat Kala Mandir, a museum housing manuscripts, miniature paintings, and sculptures from the 12th century onward. Evening transfer to Varanasi railway station to board an overnight train to Delhi.

Day 22 — Delhi: Arrival and Departure
Morning arrival at Delhi railway station. Transfer to a hotel or guest house for rest and wash. Afternoon or evening transfer to Delhi International Airport for onward travel. Tour concludes.

output.subtitle: From Athirapally's waterfalls through Kumarakom's backwaters to the Arabian Sea coast, with nights aboard a traditional houseboat.
output.summary: This nine-day itinerary moves through Kerala's three primary landscape zones: the forested highlands of Athirapally, the lagoon systems of Kumarakom and Alleppey, and the Arabian Sea beaches of Marari. The route traces a south-westward path from Kochi through waterfalls and tea country, descends into the backwater region where traditional houseboats still operate as accommodation, and concludes on a palm-lined coast. The journey alternates between resort-based stays and a night aboard a kettuvallam—a wooden houseboat with cabin and deck—allowing travellers to move through the same waters that have defined Kerala's trade and settlement patterns for centuries. Most days include optional activities; several nights emphasize stillness and water-based movement rather than structured excursions.
highlights: Athirapally Waterfall—an 80-foot drop at the edge of the Sholayar forest range
Houseboat cruise through narrow backwater canals between Kumarakom and Alleppey
Thumpurmuzhi Gardens and Vazhachal Waterfalls near Athirapally
Vembanad Lake from a resort base in Kumarakom
Fisherman village walks on the Marari beach
Kathakali dance performance in Kochi's evening
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Kochi
Arrival at Kochi airport is followed by transfer to the hotel. The afternoon allows time to visit the old spice market district and the commercial streets of M.G. Road. The evening typically includes a sunset cruise on the backwaters and a screening of Kathakali, the classical dance-drama form native to Kerala, performed in traditional costume and makeup.

Day 2 — Kochi to Athirapally Waterfall
A two-hour drive inland (78 kilometers) leads to Athirapally, a settlement at the edge of the Sholayar forest range. The primary feature is the Athirapally Waterfall—an 80-foot drop often compared to Niagara Falls in scale—which flows year-round from a catchment in the surrounding hills. Check-in occurs at the hotel; the remainder of the day is unstructured.

Day 3 — Athirapally Forests and Falls
The day encompasses visits to Thumpurmuzhi Gardens and the Vazhachal and Charpa waterfalls, both within the same forest system as Athirapally. River fishing and visits to nearby tribal settlements are available as optional activities.

Day 4 — Athirapally to Kumarakom
A four-hour drive south (150 kilometers) descends from the forested highlands into the Kuttanad region and the Vembanad Lake system. Kumarakom sits on the lake's banks and serves as the base for the backwater portion of the itinerary. Resort accommodation is situated on the water's edge, surrounded by lagoon and narrow canals lined with coconut palms. The afternoon and evening allow for optional water sports and Ayurvedic massage treatments at the resort.

Day 5 — Kumarakom Backwaters
A day at the resort, with optional water sports and Ayurvedic massage available.

Day 6 — Houseboat Cruise Through Backwaters
A kettuvallam—a traditional wooden houseboat with cabin, sitting deck, and onboard cooking facilities—departs from the resort at a predetermined time. The vessel follows narrow canals linking Kumarakom to Alleppey, passing through a landscape of lagoons, coconut groves, and fishing settlements. The houseboat serves as both transport and overnight accommodation, allowing travellers to move slowly through the backwater system without daily transfers. A full night is spent aboard.

Day 7 — Alleppey to Marari Beach
After breakfast on the houseboat, a 35-minute drive (22 kilometers) leads to Marari, a beach village on the Arabian Sea coast south of Alleppey. Check-in occurs at a beach resort. A walking tour of the resort's shoreline is typically offered in the late morning or afternoon.

Day 8 — Marari Beach
Morning visits to a fisherman village adjacent to the resort provide a view of local fishing practices and daily life along the coast. Water sports and Ayurvedic treatments remain available at the resort throughout the day.

Day 9 — Marari to Kochi Departure
After breakfast, you'll check out from the resort and transfer to Kochi airport for your onward journey. The drive north covers 58 kilometers and takes approximately one hour, marking the end of your Kerala tour.

output.seo_meta: Nine days tracing Kerala's waterfalls, backwater lagoons and Arabian Sea beaches, including a night aboard a traditional houseboat and visits to forest.
