tour.name: Rupin Pass Trek
tour.summary:
Rupin Pass trek is one such experience that all adventure lovers should indulge in. Located at an altitude of around 15250 feet, the mountain pass is in the beautiful state of Himachal Pradesh. The trek is fairly undulating, but it will allow you to be pleasantly surprised by the change in scenery at every other corner. The state itself is known for its pristine natural beauty and the trek to Rupin Pass will take you among some of the best landscapes here. Meandering rivers, dense forests and snow-clad mountain ranges make for a perfect feast for the eyes.

 

The Rupin Pass trekking tour starts at Dhaula in the state of Uttarakhand. From here, head to the Sewa village where you will come across a Kinnauri-style temple. The ethnicity of the inhabiting tribe is symbolised by this captivatingly beautiful temple. Cross a few more charming villages, such as Saruwas thatch and Jakha, to reach the Rupin Valley camp. Capture a few shots of the scenic waterfall positioned here. Further, proceed towards Rati Pheri before the ultimate climb to the pass begins. The views of hanging glaciers and the Kinnaur Kailash Mountain Range from the summit will be more than enough to mesmerise you.

 

The last phase of the Rupin Pass trekking experience starts when you head towards Sangla. Pay attention to every scenic detail of the lushness surrounding you, so that you can forever cherish this memory. A trekking trip such as this will stay with you for a long period of time. Plan the trip to breathe in the fresh scent of mountain air, infused with sweetness of apples and apricots. A million more reasons including the chance to witness the nature in an absolute un-spoilt form will compel you to take up the challenge of this thrilling vacation.
tour.itineraries:
Day 01: Arrival in Dehradun | Dehradun to Dhaula
Upon arrival in Dehradun by a train from Delhi, you can choose between driving to Dhaula and taking a bus from Dehradun to Naitwar. Upon reaching here, take a shared Jeep ride to the village of Dhaula. On arrival in the village, enjoy an overnight stay at the campsite.
Day 02: Dhaula to Sewa (7 KM | 6300 ft | 7 hours)
The adventurous Rupin pass trek starts today from a site, located a little outside Dhaula. Along the trail, you will encounter a few human settlements, and after sometime the pristine Rupin River will be visible flowing through a gorge about 500 feet below. The trek continues as you walk along the left side of the valley and pass through fragrant apple and apricot trees.

Carry on with the walk till you reach a shop, selling refreshments, on the way. Relish a steaming cup of tea, complemented with some light snacks, here. This break will refresh you enough to continue the Rupin pass trekking tour further. Today’s excursion ends at Sewa – a village, which a little uphill from the floor of the Rupin River. Upon reaching Sewa, you will come across a small temple that reflects the exquisite Kinnauri traditions and beliefs. Stay on the trail until you hear the rippling sounds of the stream.
 
Post hiking for sometime along the gushing rivulet, come across a bridge, which acts as a passage between the states of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Cross the bridge to reach the bank of the river, and set up tents here for an overnight stay.
Day 03: Sewa to Jhaka (9 KM | 8700 ft | 7 hours)
In the morning, walk along the crop fields as we enter lush forest. As you walk through the thick verdant forest, you will reach a wooden bridge which is commonly known as the "No man's Place" as the bridge does not belong to any state. After reaching Gosangu, continue walking to Kwar .Walk on the bridge, across a river, and then take the track leading up to the village. Climb up to Kwar and reach the rapidly ascending trail, which will take you to the village of Jiksun. The trail heads along the right bank of the river, as you tackle the demanding climb to Jiksun. Another one hour walk will talk you to Jhaka Village, this village is your camping destination for the night.
Day 04: Jhaka to Saruwas Thatch (6 KM | 11150 ft | 5 hours)
Resume the Rupin Pass trekking venture by descending along the trail that becomes more demanding and steep as it leads towards a tributary of the main river. Admire the breathtaking views and cross forest and reach a beautiful snow fields. Follow the snow bridge which will take you to another forest of Rhododendron. Another walk for a few kilometers will take you to campsite of Saruwas Thatch. Admire the amazing views of the Rupin waterfall from your campsite and spend the night.
Day 05: Saruwas Thatch to Dhanderas Thatch (5 KMS| 11680 ft | 4 hours)
In the morning, continue the trek to Rupin Pass by walking through picturesque and thick maple and blue pine forests. After strolling for a while, you will eventually start to descend towards a river. Cross the bridge to reach the left side of the valley from the right side. Maple forests now give way to those of silver birch and rhododendrons, and finally to alpine meadows. In the blooming seasons, the vivid colours of the wild flowers and blue poppies come alive and turn the meadow into something enchantingly beautiful. Reach the campsite for an overnight stay.
Day 06: Dhanderas Thatch to Upper Waterfall camp (13120 ft | 2-3 hours)
After acclimatizing at Dhanderas, start walking to the Upper Waterfall camp. Cross the patches of snow and fields of marigold flowers, to reach a thick snow trail. After a short sharp climb reach your campsite and relax for the night.
Day 07: Upper water fall to Rupin Pass to Ronti Gad (10 KM | 15250 ft | 11 hours)
Rupin Pass trekking tour now becomes a bit more challenging as you move along a trail, less in width and having a high angle of ascent. Continue to make progress on the expedition while passing through perilous boulders. For your safety, take the support of a rope if these have snow. On reaching the summit of the pass, enjoy the spectacular views of the Kinnaur Kailash Range of the Himalayas. Finally, descend towards alpine meadows to set up camps for at Ronti Gad for an overnight stay.
Day 08: Ronti Gad to Sangla Via Sangla Kanda. Overnight drive to Shimla (12 KM | 8800 ft | 6 hours)
All the while, continue enjoying enthralling views of the Sangla Valley. Descending towards Sangla, the trail grows steeper, so walk downhill carefully and maintain a comfortable pace. Hike downhill for around one and a half hour and experience an elevation decline of more than 1500 feet. The Rupin Pass trek comes to an end upon reaching Sangla. Having reached here, you will find that the town has excellent links to other cities. Either stay in Sangla in any of the numerous accommodation options offered in the form of hotels, and bed and breakfasts; or travel to Shimla by road.

output.name: Rupin Pass Trek — 8 Days in the Himachal Himalayas
output.subtitle: Dhaula to Sangla across a 15,250-foot mountain pass, through river valleys, alpine meadows, and Kinnauri villages
output.summary: The Rupin Pass trek traverses the high country between Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, rising to 15,250 feet along a route that descends into river gorges, crosses into rhododendron and maple forests, and climbs to views of the Kinnaur Kailash Range. The journey begins at Dhaula in Uttarakhand, follows the Rupin River through settlements and agricultural land, and ascends through successive forest zones — first mixed broadleaf, then silver birch and rhododendron, finally alpine meadows dotted with marigold and wild blue poppy. The pass itself sits at the border of two states; the descent beyond leads to Sangla Valley and onward links to Shimla. Eight days of progressive acclimatization and terrain change account for the varied altitude and exposure.
highlights: Kinnauri temple architecture at Sewa village, reflecting local tribal traditions
Rupin River gorge walk with 500-foot elevation above the water's surface
Alpine meadows in bloom season (blue poppy, marigold, wild flowers) between Dhanderas Thatch and Upper Waterfall camp
Rupin Pass summit at 15,250 feet with views of Kinnaur Kailash Range and hanging glaciers
Descent into Sangla Valley through rhododendron forests and steep alpine terrain
Snow bridge and forest transitions at higher elevations (Saruwas Thatch area)
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival at Dehradun; Transfer to Dhaula Base
Arrival in Dehradun by train from Delhi. From the station, transfer options include a direct drive to Dhaula or a bus journey to Naitwar followed by a shared jeep to Dhaula village. Dhaula sits at the official start of the trek route. Overnight stay at the campsite.

Day 2 — Dhaula to Sewa — First Trek Day Along Rupin River Gorge
The Rupin Pass trek begins just outside Dhaula, starting at moderate elevation before the landscape opens into views of the Rupin River cutting through a gorge some 500 feet below. The trail follows the left side of the valley, winding through fragrant apple and apricot orchards that characterize this stretch of Himachal Pradesh.

As the day progresses, you'll pass through a few human settlements dotting the hillside. A wayside tea shop offers a natural break point—a chance to rest with a cup of tea and light snacks before the terrain steepens. From here, the trail climbs steadily uphill to Sewa, a small village perched above the river floor itself.

Sewa holds quiet cultural significance: a small temple here reflects the exquisite architectural and spiritual traditions of the Kinnauri people. Beyond the village, the sound of the stream draws trekkers onward to a bridge that serves as the official passage between Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. After crossing, you'll descend to the riverbank to establish camp for the night.

Today's distance is 7 kilometers over approximately 7 hours, gaining elevation to 6,300 feet.

Day 3 — Sewa to Jhaka — Forest Ascent to Mid-Trek Base
The route leaves Sewa through crop fields and enters thick forest. A wooden bridge, locally called 'No Man's Place' because it belongs to neither state, marks a transition point. The trail continues through Gosangu and Kwar, crossing a river bridge before climbing the right bank toward Jiksun village. From Jiksun, a demanding ascent leads to Jhaka, the day's destination at 8,700 feet. This 9-kilometer section takes approximately 7 hours and introduces steeper terrain that continues through the next stages of the trek.

Day 4 — Jhaka to Saruwas Thatch — Snow Fields and Rhododendron Forest
The trek descends along increasingly steep terrain toward a river tributary, crossing dramatic snow fields before a snow bridge leads into a rhododendron forest. The demanding 6-kilometer route climbs to 11,150 feet over approximately 5 hours, traversing varied landscapes as the trail winds through forest and open terrain. Several kilometers of walking through this mixed scenery bring you to Saruwas Thatch campsite, where you can settle in and take in the remarkable views of the Rupin waterfall before nightfall.

Day 5 — Saruwas Thatch to Dhanderas Thatch — Alpine Forest Transition
The route climbs through thick maple and blue pine forest, then descends toward a river and crosses to the valley's left side. Forest composition changes progressively: maple and blue pine give way to silver birch and rhododendron, then transition to alpine meadows. During flowering season, wild blue poppy and other alpine flowers cover the meadows. The 5-kilometer trek to Dhanderas Thatch takes approximately 4 hours, reaching 11,680 feet. This day marks the start of genuine high-altitude terrain.

Day 6 — Dhanderas Thatch to Upper Waterfall Camp — Final Approach to Pass
After acclimatization rest, the trek continues toward Upper Waterfall camp at 13,120 feet. The route crosses snow patches and fields of marigold flowers before reaching thick snow trail. A short sharp climb leads to the campsite.

Day 7 — Upper Waterfall Camp to Rupin Pass to Ronti Gad — Summit Day
The ascent to Rupin Pass becomes substantially more demanding. The trail narrows and increases in angle of ascent, passing over perilous boulder fields. Rope support is necessary on snowy sections for safety. At 15,250 feet, the summit offers views of the Kinnaur Kailash Range and hanging glaciers. The summit marks the passage between states. Descent follows alpine meadows to Ronti Gad for overnight camp. This 10-kilometer day involves 11 hours of trekking and represents the trek's physical peak.

Day 8 — Ronti Gad to Sangla via Sangla Kanda — Final Descent and Trek End
The final day descends 12 kilometers toward Sangla Valley, taking approximately 6 hours with an elevation loss of more than 1,500 feet. The trail grows steep as it approaches Sangla; descend carefully and maintain a comfortable pace. Sangla marks the trek's official end at 8,800 feet. The town has road links to Shimla and other regional centers. Accommodation options in Sangla include hotels and bed-and-breakfast properties. Alternatively, an overnight drive to Shimla is available.

tour.summary: Explore, hike, and cycle through India on this 15-day odyssey where every moment will feel like a dance between tradition and enchantment. You’ll wander the bustling streets of Delhi, where saris twirl in a vibrant dance of colours and the air is a tantalizing blend of exotic spices. Next, Agra and Pushkar await, with their bold forts and ancient temples spinning tales that echo through the ages. Ranthambore National Park invites you to discover animals roaming freely, peacocks putting on dazzling dance moves and maybe even a tiger or two. Pack your sense of wonder and let India unfold in all its glory.

From yoga to Bollywood, sacred temples to exotic wildlife, and bold textiles to complex vegetarian cuisine, experience every side of India in this incredible adventure that takes you through the very heart of Rajasthan. We welcome you to Delhi, and to India, and invite you to bring your curious nature to a country that is ready to inspire and impress. Get ready for a spirited and breathtaking two weeks.

You will be met at the airport by your included arrival transfer through the G Adventures-supported Women With Wheels project. After a welcome meeting with your CEO and group, go on an orientation walk and then head to a local restaurant for a welcome dinner.

Day 2         Delhi: Historic & Modern India
Delhi, the vibrant capital of India, offers a captivating blend of rich history and modern tradition that charms every traveler. Set out on foot to discover a treasure trove of iconic landmarks such as the majestic Mehrauli Archeological Park, Humayun's Tomb and the intricate architecture of the India Gate, each narrating a story of India's diverse heritage. Delhi's bustling markets, divine cuisine and warm hospitality provide an immersive cultural experience, making it the perfect destination for the start of your trip.

Join your CEO on a walking tour of some of the oldest parts of Delhi, through ancient ruins and diverse religious sites. In the afternoon, discover Old Delhi and its narrow bylanes of Kinnari bazaar and the old havelis of Chandni Chowk. Wander through bazaars, spice markets and even ride a rickshaw to dive straight into daily life in India's biggest city.

        Namaste Delhi Walking Tour             Delhi   2h45m-3h
Visit G Values Fund project, Namaste Delhi. Start your walking tour of Qutab Complex and the Mehrauli archeological park. Go back in time as you walk through the oldest parts of historical Delhi and explore ancient ruins, monuments and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Wander through a park scattered with time-ravaged tombs and mosques.

        Old Delhi Guided Walk                      Delhi    4h-4h
Visit historic Old Delhi. Explore Jama Masjid, the "Great Mosque," and enjoy its massive courtyard, which can hold up to 25,000 worshippers. Also, visit the ancient Sikh temple of Gurdwara SisGanj, which was established in 1783.

No India itinerary is complete without a stop at two of the most iconic spots in the world, let alone India. The Taj Mahal and the Agra Fort are just a train ride away for today's adventure. The Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World and a world renowned symbol of love and craftsmanship. And the legendary Agra Fort stands as a testament to the significance of India's grand Mughal Empire. We make sure these two world famous stops are checked off your India bucket list today.

You don't need to venture deep into the jungle to experience India's vibrant wildlife. Grab your binoculars and join your guide in search of not just tigers but leopards, bengal foxes, langurs and other amazing species. While the city is beautiful to gaze at, it's not just a pretty facade. Together we have the next two days to explore all this city has to teach us. First up, try your hand at block printing with the women of the Anoothi Project before an orientation walk through town.

After an early morning safari, you'll drive to one of the most colorful cities in India, Jaipur. Known for its colored gems and pink buildings, take it all in on a walking tour of the city.

Your G for Good Moment: Anoothi Block Printing Experience
Women from marginalised communities outside Jaipur came together to create the Anoothi Project. In Hindi, Anoothi means 'unique and extraordinary' and by teaching these women to master the traditionally male handicraft of block printing, the collective shines a light on the unique and extraordinary within each individual. At this G for Good visit, engage in a hands-on block printing activity with the local women as you indulge in some local snacks prepared by your hosts.

Day 7         Jaipur: Astrological Observations
Your Jaipur explorations start with the Amber Heritage walk. Step into what feels like a painting at the intricate Panna Meena before climbing onward to the majestically perched fortress of Amber Fort. The afternoon continues with a guided exploration of Jantar Mantar. This architectural wonder is marveled for its accurate observation of celestial bodies, showcasing the advanced astronomical knowledge of its time and the world's largest sundial.

Today is jam packed with OMG worthy moments. Pushkar is one of the oldest and holiest cities in India and home to one of the only temples in the world dedicated to Brahma, the Hindu creator god. After a visit to this esteemed temple, you get the honor of choosing how the rest of your day unfolds. Connect with your spiritual side with a yoga class and a wellness and spirituality discussion or hike the famed pilgrimage path to Savitri Temple Hill and visit this picturesque hilltop. Come together in the evening again for sundowners with a show, to watch traditional Kalbeliya dancers alongside a local feast under the stars.

Your OMG Day starts in the holy town of Pushkar with a visit the famed Brahma Temple to meet a local pandit to understand and partake in ancient rituals. The state of Rajasthan is famed for its historic forts and fortresses, handicrafts and its bright and beautiful block printing and tie-dye techniques. Visit small hamlets whose traditions remained unchanged over the last hundred years, and overnight at a heritage property outside Jodhpur.

output.name: Northern India: Taj Mahal, Forts & River Safaris — 15 Days
output.subtitle: Delhi to Mumbai via Agra, Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur, with safaris on the Chambal River and in Ranthambore National Park
output.summary: This 15-day itinerary moves through northern India's principal architectural and natural landmarks, beginning in Delhi and concluding in Mumbai. The route traces colonial and Mughal heritage through Agra's Taj Mahal and Fort, follows the Chambal River by boat near Dholpur, enters Ranthambore National Park for wildlife safaris, and examines the astronomical instruments at Jantar Mantar in Jaipur. The journey incorporates village visits in Rajasthan, textile workshops in Chandelao and Jodhpur, the marble temples of Ranakpur, lakefront stays in Udaipur, and concludes with the rock-cut caves of Elephanta Island near Mumbai. Throughout, the trip includes guided walks in historic quarters, interactions with artisan communities supported by nonprofit initiatives, and transfers by private vehicle, train, and domestic flight.
highlights: Guided tour of the Taj Mahal in Agra
Boat safari on the Chambal River searching for gharials and migratory birds
Jeep safari in Ranthambore National Park for leopards, deer, and Bengal tigers
Amber Fort and Panna Meena stepwell walk near Jaipur
Jantar Mantar Observatory in Jaipur — astronomical instruments dating to 1727
Brahma Temple visit in Pushkar with local pandit and optional Savitri Temple hike (900 steps, 650 feet elevation)
Mehrangarh Fortress overlooking Jodhpur's blue-painted old city
Ranakpur Jain Temple — 15th-century white marble structure with 1,444 individually carved pillars
Sunrise cycle to Badi Lake in Udaipur with breakfast
Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola, Udaipur
Elephanta Caves UNESCO World Heritage site near Mumbai — 5th-century rock-cut Hindu temples
Block printing workshop with artisans in Jaipur and Chandelao
Cooperative craft market visit in Jodhpur supporting 35+ women artisans
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Delhi
Arrival in India. You will be met at Delhi airport by your included arrival transfer.

Once settled at your accommodation, The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar), you will meet your trip leader and fellow travellers for an orientation meeting. This provides an opportunity to connect with the group and receive information before the adventure.

The afternoon includes an orientation walk through Delhi's streets. As evening falls, you will head to a local restaurant for a welcome dinner with your group.

Meals included: Dinner

Day 2 — Delhi: Mehrauli Archaeological Park and Old City Bazaars
Begin your Delhi experience with a morning walking tour through Mehrauli Archaeological Park, one of the city's oldest quarters. The park contains ancient ruins, tombs, and historic mosques across its grounds, each structure marking different periods of Delhi's history. You will walk through the Qutab Complex alongside your trip leader, moving through centuries of architectural history.

In the afternoon, navigate Old Delhi's narrow bylanes and markets. Visit Kinnari Bazaar and the historic havelis of Chandni Chowk. The Jama Masjid, known as the Great Mosque, dominates this section with its large courtyard, with capacity for up to 25,000 worshippers. Visit this structure alongside the Gurdwara SisGanj, a Sikh temple established in 1783.

Ride an auto-rickshaw through the spice markets and narrow commercial streets to observe daily trading activity and community commerce.

You will stay at The Metropolitan Hotel & Spa (or similar). Breakfast is included.

Day 3 — Train to Agra: Taj Mahal and Agra Fort
A train departing Delhi travels south to Agra, approximately 2–3 hours. Upon arrival, a guided tour of the Taj Mahal is included. Built by Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, this white marble structure is a monument of Mughal architecture. Your trip leader and local guide will provide architectural and historical context during the tour.

After the Taj Mahal, the group visits Agra Fort, constructed from red sandstone and white marble. This fort documents the reach and organization of the Mughal Empire.

In the afternoon, a private vehicle carries the group on a 90-minute drive to Dholpur. You will stay at Narsingh Bagh, a collection of stone cottages providing accommodation outside the city activity.

Day 4 — Dholpur: Chambal River Safari and Bicycle Birding
The morning begins with a motorboat safari on the Chambal River, 1–1.5 hours in duration. The landscape is observed from the water, with migratory birds present along the banks. Gharials (narrow-jawed crocodilians) inhabit the river, and the area shows traditional riverside settlement.

The afternoon includes a 6-kilometer bicycle route with no elevation gain, departing from Narsingh Bagh to Talab-E-Sahi through surrounding jungle. A guide leads stops for bird observation and photography. The route is accessible for all cycling levels. Return to the hotel for afternoon tea.

Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included.

Day 5 — Ranthambore National Park: Tiger and Leopard Safaris
A four-hour private transfer from Dholpur delivers you to Ranthambore National Park. Upon arrival, you will stay at Jungle Vilas Resort before heading out for an afternoon safari.

Your jeep safari, 2–3 hours in duration, is led by local rangers through dense forest interspersed with historical ruins. Wildlife in the park includes Bengal tigers, leopards, Bengal foxes, wild boar, langurs, and various deer species. Tiger sightings are not guaranteed. Return to the lodge as daylight fades.

Day 6 — Ranthambore Safari to Jaipur: Pink City Arrival and Block Printing Workshop
The day begins before dawn with an early morning safari through Ranthambore National Park, 3–4 hours in duration, led by local rangers. Departure for Jaipur follows the safari.

The drive to Jaipur spans approximately 165 kilometers, requiring 3 hours 45 minutes to 4 hours 15 minutes by private vehicle.

Upon arrival in Jaipur, a brief walking orientation introduces the city's layout and its distinctive pink-coloured buildings.

A hands-on block printing activity is included at a local artisan workshop, where you will learn block printing techniques and receive local snacks prepared by your hosts.

You will stay at Narain Niwas Palace, a heritage hotel. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 7 — Jaipur: Amber Fort, Panna Meena Stepwell, and Jantar Mantar
Your Jaipur exploration begins with a walking tour that includes the Panna Meena stepwell and Amber Fort, a fortress perched on elevated terrain showcasing Hindu and Muslim design elements throughout its halls, courtyards, and chambers.

Before heading to Amber Fort, visit the Hawa Mahal, or Palace of the Winds. Its distinctive honeycomb façade features small windows. The carved pink sandstone is photographable.

After lunch, a guided tour of Jantar Mantar includes an astronomical observatory containing a collection of astronomical instruments, some dating to 1727. The complex houses the world's largest stone sundial. Walking among these structures provides information about pre-modern astronomical observation and calculation.

You will stay at Narain Niwas Palace or a similar heritage hotel.

Day 8 — Pushkar: Brahma Temple, Optional Activities, and Desert Sunset with Traditional Dancers
A 2.5–3.5 hour private drive from Jaipur delivers you to Pushkar, one of India's oldest cities. The city is home to a temple dedicated to Brahma, the Hindu creator deity.

Your morning begins with a guided orientation walk through Pushkar's landmarks, including lakes and ghats. At the Brahma Temple, you will meet a local pandit who guides you through ritual practices.

The afternoon offers two options:
Option 1: A one-hour yoga class followed by a wellness and spirituality discussion.
Option 2: A visit to Savitri Temple, accessed via 900 steps climbing 650 feet in elevation along a mostly paved path. The ascent becomes uneven toward the summit and provides views across Pushkar and the surrounding desert landscape.

As daylight approaches dusk, the group reconvenes on sand dunes for refreshments and a cultural performance. Traditional Kalbeliya dancers perform as the sun descends. A barbecue dinner follows.

Accommodation is at Atithi Luxury Resort or similar. Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Day 9 — Chandelao: Historic Fortress and Village Textile Traditions
A 3.5–4 hour private drive from Pushkar brings you to Chandelao, a small settlement anchored by an ancient fortress. The property has been home to the same family for generations.

After settling in, a jeep excursion takes you into surrounding hamlets, culminating in Pipar village. Families here practice block printing and tie-dye techniques that have been largely unchanged for over a century. Conversations with the artisans reveal how these methods persist in rural India.

You will stay at Chandelao Garh, a heritage property within the fortress grounds. Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Day 10 — Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fortress and the Blue City
The morning includes a half-day exploration of Jodhpur city and Mehrangarh Fortress, which sits at the summit of a dramatic cliff. Its honey-coloured stone walls contain a museum documenting the fortress's strategic importance across centuries of Rajasthani history. From the ramparts, the Blue City unfolds below in its distinctive palette. The tour includes Jaswant Thada, a marble memorial located nearby.

In the afternoon, visit a local craft enterprise operated by women, producing textiles, jewelry, and handmade items. This visit provides opportunity to understand community-based production and to purchase items directly from producers.

You will stay at Chandelao Garh or a similar guesthouse. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 11 — Ranakpur's Marble Temples and Udaipur's Lakefront
The journey begins with a 3.5-hour drive from Chandelao across 160 kilometers. Ranakpur Jain Temples are white marble structures devoted to Adinath, a central deity in the Jain faith. The main temple features 1,444 individually carved marble pillars, each distinct, supporting the sanctuary. These pillars reflect the Jain principle of ahimsa, non-violence toward all living beings.

After exploring the temple complex, the route continues south toward Udaipur, another 2.5-hour drive across 90 kilometers. Upon arrival, a guided orientation walk leads through the old city's winding lanes, introducing local markets and key landmarks. The day concludes with a group dinner at a lakeside restaurant.

You will stay at Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection. Meals included: Breakfast, Dinner

Day 12 — Udaipur: Badi Lake Cycle, Jagdish Temple & Pichola Lake Sunset
Start before dawn with a 12-kilometer bicycle ride through Udaipur's ancient hills and village tracks to Badi Lake, taking 2–3 hours on a traditional bike at a gentle pace. Breakfast is provided on the lake's bank.

Return to the city for a guided visit to Jagdish Temple, built in 1651. The shrine features intricately carved stonework and a black stone image of Vishnu housed within. Your trip leader will provide context on the temple's role in the city's spiritual life.

The afternoon is unscheduled, allowing time for independent exploration of the city.

As evening approaches, board a boat for a 1–2 hour tour on Lake Pichola. The water reflects the city's palaces, most notably the City Palace, and the hills beyond.

You will stay at Fateh Niwas by Fateh Collection.

Day 13 — Flight to Mumbai: Dhobi Ghat, Malabar Hill, and Marine Drive
After a relaxed morning in Udaipur, depart on a flight of 1 hour 15 minutes to Mumbai. Upon arrival at Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport, an airport transfer takes you directly into a driving tour.

The route includes a photo stop at Dhobi Ghat, where hundreds of workers wash textiles daily by hand in orderly rows of concrete tanks. The drive ascends Malabar Hill to the Hanging Gardens, a topiary-covered reservoir. From here, the vantage point offers views across the Arabian Sea and the bay below.

The tour descends through Marine Drive, a curved coastal road, leading to your hotel, the Trident at Nariman Point (or similar).

Breakfast is included.

Day 14 — Elephanta Caves and Gateway of India
Begin the day at the Gateway of India, an architecturally splendid colonial-era arch built during British rule. This monument overlooks the Arabian Sea.

From here, board a private boat for a one-hour journey to Elephanta Island, home to a UNESCO World Heritage site. The island's cave temples were carved into rock during the 5th century and were dedicated to Lord Shiva. Walking through the columned passages, you will encounter sculptures and carvings depicting Hindu iconography and cosmology.

A half-day visit allows time to move through the caves at a deliberate pace.

The afternoon is yours to structure as you wish—rest at your accommodation, visit local markets, or enjoy a meal. As evening settles, join your trip leader and fellow travellers for a farewell dinner.

Day 15 — Departure from Mumbai
Your adventure concludes today. Depart at a time that suits your schedule. Breakfast is included before you leave. Your trip leader remains available to assist with any onward travel arrangements you may require.

output.name: Dagala Thousand Lakes Trek — 9 Days
output.subtitle: High-altitude alpine circuit through Bhutan's remote lake country, crossing two passes above 4,300 metres
output.summary: This trek traverses Bhutan's least-visited high country, a region of alpine meadows, glacial lakes, and unobstructed views of the eastern Himalaya. The route crosses two substantial passes—Pagalabtsa at 4,250 metres and Talela at 4,180 metres—with the highest camp situated at 4,100 metres. Between passes lies a full day of exploration around the Thousand Lakes plateau, a landscape of shallow tarns and open grassland where few trekkers venture. Thick conifer forests, rushing snowmelt streams, and evidence of traditional yak herding anchor the higher sections. The trek requires sustained fitness and comfort at altitude; weather in the alpine zone changes rapidly.
highlights: Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery at 3,120 metres above Paro Valley
Ascend Pagalabtsa Pass (4,250 metres) for views of Mount Kangchenjunga
Day of lake exploration on the Thousand Lakes plateau at 4,100 metres
Traverse high-altitude meadows and rhododendron forests above 4,000 metres
Cross Talela Pass (4,180 metres) with descent through juniper woodland
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Paro
Arrive at Paro International Airport at 2,200 metres. Check into accommodation and visit Paro town.

Day 2 — Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
A steep dirt track climbs 520 metres over 4 hours to Tiger's Nest Monastery at 3,120 metres. The route passes a halfway café, then descends and climbs stone steps along the cliff face to the monastery.

Day 3 — Genekha Village to Gur Campsite
A 90-minute drive reaches Genekha village and the trek's start. The route crosses a suspension bridge, then climbs gradually on dirt trail through forest, descends to river level, and climbs again to the Gur campsite at 3,290 metres. The day covers 7 kilometres and 230 metres of elevation gain over 4 hours.

Day 4 — Gur to Labatama: Ascent to Pagalabtsa Pass
The route climbs across open ridges and grassy slopes, gaining 1,010 metres in 6 hours over 12 kilometres. Pagalabtsa Pass at 4,250 metres offers clear sightlines to Mount Kangchenjunga and the eastern Himalayan crest. Beyond the pass, the trail descends through alpine meadows dotted with yak herder shelters, reaching Labatama camp at 4,100 metres.

Day 5 — Labatama Halt: Highland Lakes Exploration
Visit multiple glacial lakes surrounding camp on the Thousand Lakes plateau at 4,100 metres. Open grassland and untracked terrain offer stillness and solitude across the alpine highlands.

Day 6 — Labatama to Panka
A steep ascent over open meadows with unobstructed Himalayan views precedes a rocky descent along a river to Panka campsite at 4,000 metres. The day gains 220 metres, covers 8 kilometres, and takes 5 hours.

Day 7 — Panka to Talela Pass and Thimphu Road Head
The trek climbs gradually on dirt track to Talela Pass at 4,180 metres, then walks along ridges through alpine meadows. A long descent through juniper and rhododendron forest on rocky and dirt trail leads to a feeder road at 2,300 metres. Despite a 100-metre elevation gain, the day involves 14 kilometres and 7 hours of hiking due to the steep descent and trail surface.

Day 8 — Thimphu: Museums and City Centre
Morning visit to Buddha Dordenma statue (54 metres high), the Folk Heritage Museum, and Textile Museum. Afternoon includes the Craft Bazaar and Kaja Throm Farmers Market, with time for independent exploration.

Day 9 — Departure from Thimphu
Depart.

tour.name: THE BEST OF WEST & CENTRAL BHUTAN
tour.subtitle: Route: Paro → Thimphu → Punakha → Trongsa → Bumthang → Tang Valley → Gangtey → Wangdi → Paro
tour.itineraries:
DAY 1   Arrival in Paro.
Your tour guide will meet you and take you on a short one-hour drive along the Paro and Thimphu river valleys to Thimphu, Bhutan's capital, at 2320 metres. You can stop on the way to take in the magnificent Tamchhog Lhakhang, the hereditary place of worship for Bhutan's iron bridge builder.
Overnight in Thimphu
DAY 2   Sightseeing in Thimphu.
We can visit the weekly market, the National Memorial Chorten, the Buddha Dordenma, Changangkha Temple, Takin Reserve, the School of Traditional Arts and Crafts, the Folk Heritage Museum, and the National Library. Browse the striking collection of intricate textiles at the National Textile Museum and visit the craft bazaar. Discuss your preference for the day with the guide.
Overnight in Thimphu
DAY 3   Drive to Punakha via Dochu La Pass, where we will stop for a hot drink and enjoy views of the Eastern Himalayan range.
In the afternoon visit Chimi Lhakhang (Temple of Fertility), built in the 15th century by the 'Divine Mad Man' (Lama Drukpa Kunley) and Punakha Dzong.
Overnight in Punakha
DAY 4   Drive from Punakha to Bumthang via Trongsa, the gateway to central Bhutan.
You can stop to visit the impressive Trongsa Dzong which commands the eye from miles away. Visit the museum in the watchtower dedicated to the Royal Wangchuk dynasty, which tells the stories of the Dzong and features personal belongings of the Kings and Queens of Bhutan. Continue your journey through some of Bhutan's most beautiful landscapes to Bumthang.
Overnight in Trongsa
DAY 5   A day of sightseeing in the Bumthang valleys.
Your guide will take you on a fascinating tour of a variety of sacred sites including Jamba Lhakhang, Kurjey Lhakhang and Tamshing Lhakhang. Visit Jakar Dzong (Bhutan's largest) and you may be interested to see Bumthang's famous Swiss cheese factory or the Red Panda Brewery.
Overnight in Bumthang
DAY 6   Today we take an excursion to the remote Tang valley.
Stop to visit Membar Tsho (the burning lake), which is one of Bhutan's most important pilgrimage sites. Then on to Drangchel, Pema Lingpa's birthplace. You will also see some picturesque villages and temples and can walk up to visit Ugyencholing Palace, which is now a museum and gives an interesting insight into life in an aristocratic family in the last century.
Overnight in Tang Valley
DAY 7   Start your journey back west to Gangtey in the remote Phobjikha valley.
Visit Gangtey Gompa (one of Bhutan's oldest monasteries and extensively renovated) and explore the valley where the villagers continue to live a traditional Bhutanese rural lifestyle. This is the site where black-necked cranes visit in their hundreds in November each year after spending the summer in Tibet.
Overnight in Gangtey
DAY 8   Today can be a day of leisure in this beautiful rural valley.
If it is winter you can view the black-necked cranes. If you like hiking your guide will suggest a day or half day hike in the valley.
Overnight in Gangtey
DAY 9   Return to Paro via Wangdi.
Wangdi Dzong, built by the Shabdrung in 1638 on an auspicious site where four ravens were seen flying in four different directions, was badly damaged in a fire in June 2012 but has been painstakingly renovated over 12 years and is now open to visit. When you reach Paro you can visit the local handicraft shops for souvenirs of your trip.
Overnight in Paro
DAY 10   Sightseeing in Paro.
Visit Dumtse Lhakhang, The National Museum, Paro Rinpung Dzong and Kyichu Lhakhang (temple).
Overnight in Paro
DAY 11   Take a day hike to the 'Tiger's Nest', the sacred Taktshang Monastery.
You can stop at the Taktshang cafeteria viewpoint on the way up for a wonderful view of the monastery.
Overnight in Paro
DAY 12 (Departure)
Depart from Paro International Airport with a full heart.

output.name: West and Central Bhutan: Dzongs, Valleys and Mountain Passes — 12 Days
output.subtitle: From Paro through Punakha, Bumthang and Gangtey, following dzongs and sacred sites
output.summary: This 12-day circuit moves systematically through Bhutan's administrative and spiritual core, beginning in the Paro valley and moving east through the country's major dzongs — fortress-monasteries that anchor each region's governance and religious practice. The route crosses Dochu La Pass into Punakha, continues east to Bumthang's valleys and the Tang region, then descends west through Phobjikha's black-necked crane habitat before returning to Paro. Days are structured around named sites — Trongsa Dzong's royal museum, Jakar Dzong (Bhutan's largest), Taktshang Monastery's clifftop setting — rather than generic scenic loops. The itinerary accommodates seasonal variation: winter visitors may see black-necked cranes in Phobjikha; summer travellers encounter clearer mountain views and accessible higher trails.
highlights: Trongsa Dzong's museum, featuring personal belongings of Bhutan's royal dynasty
Taktshang Monastery, the sacred monastery above Paro valley
Jakar Dzong, Bhutan's largest fortress, dominating Bumthang's agricultural plains
Membar Tsho (Burning Lake), a pilgrimage site associated with Pema Lingpa's treasure revelation
Phobjikha valley's black-necked crane habitat and Gangtey Gompa, one of Bhutan's oldest monasteries
Dochu La Pass crossing with views of the Eastern Himalayan range
Ugyencholing Palace museum in Tang valley, preserving aristocratic life from the last century
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Paro to Thimphu via Tamchhog Lhakhang
A one-hour drive from Paro valley northward along the Paro and Thimphu rivers reaches Bhutan's capital, positioned at 2,320 metres. The route passes Tamchhog Lhakhang, a temple and hereditary residence associated with Bhutan's legendary iron bridge builder. Thimphu itself spreads across a high valley floor without walls or administrative boundaries—an administrative capital designed around Buddhist planning principles rather than colonial precedent.

Day 2 — Thimphu: Temples, Museums and Markets
Thimphu's sightseeing options centre on the capital's religious and cultural institutions. The National Memorial Chorten anchors the city's centre; the colossal Buddha Dordenma statue overlooks the valley from a ridge; Changangkha Temple sits on a hilltop with city views. The National Textile Museum houses an extensive collection of traditional Bhutanese weaving, while the Folk Heritage Museum and School of Traditional Arts document rural craftsmanship. The weekly market and craft bazaar provide context for understanding local textiles, produce and handicrafts. Your guide will recommend a selection based on your interests.

Day 3 — Dochu La Pass to Punakha Dzong
The drive south crosses Dochu La Pass, with stops for views of the Eastern Himalayan range and a hot drink. Descending into Punakha's warmer valley, visit Chimi Lhakhang, the 15th-century temple built by Lama Drukpa Kunley, and Punakha Dzong, where two rivers converge.

Day 4 — Trongsa and the Gateway to Central Bhutan
The eastward drive from Punakha moves into Bhutan's central region via Trongsa, a fortress-town positioned on a dramatic ridge overlooking river gorges. Trongsa Dzong commands landscape views for kilometres in all directions. The site includes a watchtower museum dedicated to the royal Wangchuk dynasty, displaying personal possessions of Bhutan's kings and queens alongside the dzong's architectural and political history. From Trongsa, the road continues through forested, steep terrain toward Bumthang's valleys.

Day 5 — Bumthang's Sacred Sites and Jakar Dzong
The day's sightseeing visits three major temples—Jamba Lhakhang, Kurjey Lhakhang and Tamshing Lhakhang—each connected to Bhutanese Buddhist history and pilgrimage practice. Jakar Dzong, Bhutan's largest fortress-monastery, dominates the valley centre. The region supports a Swiss cheese factory and Red Panda Brewery, both established by expatriates and now integrated into local agricultural routines. Your guide can suggest time allocation based on your interests.

Day 6 — Tang Valley: Remote Pilgrimage Sites and Palaces
A full-day excursion into the remote Tang valley visits Membar Tsho, a lake with rock overhangs that pilgrims associate with the treasure revealer Pema Lingpa. The site is one of Bhutan's most important pilgrimage destinations. Continuing deeper into the valley reaches Drangchel, Pema Lingpa's birthplace, and Ugyencholing Palace, now a museum documenting aristocratic family life in rural Bhutan during the last century. The valley itself contains scattered villages and smaller temples. A walk to Ugyencholing requires modest hillside climbing.

Day 7 — Gangtey Gompa and Phobjikha Valley
The westward journey returns to Phobjikha valley, where Gangtey Gompa sits on a hillside overlooking the wetland. The monastery, one of Bhutan's oldest, underwent extensive renovation in recent decades. The surrounding valley remains largely rural, with farming communities maintaining traditional agricultural practices and settlement patterns. Phobjikha is notable as the winter habitat for black-necked cranes, which arrive in November from their summer grounds in Tibet and depart in March.

Day 8 — Phobjikha Valley: Rest Day or Optional Hiking
This day accommodates seasonal variation and individual pacing. Winter visitors can observe black-necked cranes in their hundreds across the valley floor. Summer travellers, or those preferring active time, can hike a half-day or full-day route suggested by your guide through the valley's rural landscape and forests.

Day 9 — Return to Paro via Wangdi Dzong
The westward drive to Paro passes through Wangdi, site of Wangdi Dzong, built by the Shabdrung (Bhutan's unification figure) in 1638. The fortress sustained severe fire damage in 2012 and underwent twelve years of restoration before reopening. The drive continues west and downward into Paro valley. Upon arrival, handicraft shops in Paro offer souvenirs and locally produced textiles, art and crafts.

Day 10 — Paro Valley Temples and Museums
Paro's sightseeing includes Dumtse Lhakhang, the National Museum of Bhutan, Paro Rinpung Dzong and Kyichu Lhakhang, one of Bhutan's oldest temples.

Day 11 — Taktshang Monastery Hike

tour.name: All Inclusive Xi'an Heritage Tour from Beijing
tour.summary: Discover Xi'an's historic highlights over this 3-day all inclusive tour with your private guide. Board an included bullet train to Xi'an, explore the fascinationg Muslim Quarter. Visit the Great Mosque, walk around the Ancient City Wall, tour the Terracotta Warriors and admire Big Wild Goose Pagoda.
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 Beijing/Xi'an - Bullet train to Xi'an, Great Mosque, Muslim Quarter
Your guide in Beijing will greet you in your hotel lobby at 07:30 am, and then you'll head to the train station for a 6-hour journey to Xi'an. Arriving in Xi'an check into the hotel. Then today’s adventure starts with a visit to the Great Mosque which is the most significant mosque in China and is a fascinating blend of Chinese and Islamic architecture and aspects. It was constructed during the Hongwu reigion of the Ming dynasty, with further additions during the Qing dynasty. Previous religious complexes are known to have stood on the same site, dating back as far as the Tang dynasty.
Later, take a walk around the Muslim quarter, home to the Hui Muslim community for centuries. Stroll through these narrow streets dotted with small shops, halal butchers, sesame-oil factories, small mosques markets and restaurants.

Day 2 Xi'an - Terracotta Warriors & Big Wild Goose Pagoda
Morning set off to visit the Terracotta Warriors. You will learn about this incredible archaeological find, discovered in 1976 by farmers digging a well, after being buried for 2,000 years. Three main pits are open for you to view, where just under 2,000 of the total 6,000 warriors – each individually sculpted from clay, each having a different costume, height, and even facial expression – stand in battle formation.
After marveling at this incredible display we will enjoy lunch in a local village before our private transport takes us to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda. Once, the pagoda held old Buddhist relics and classics brought from India by the hierarch Xuanzang. If you are lucky you may catch a fantastic musical fountain show at the north square of the temple.

Then it's a 6-hour journey back to Beijing by bullet train. In late afternoon, you will arrive Beijing West Railway Station where the trip ends.

output.summary: This three-day journey moves from Beijing to Xi'an by high-speed rail, anchoring on three distinct historical layers. The Great Mosque — constructed during the Ming dynasty on foundations laid in the Tang — sits at the centre of the Muslim Quarter, where narrow streets still hold sesame-oil factories, halal butchers, and small restaurants. The Terracotta Warriors, discovered by farmers in 1976 after two millennia underground, number roughly 6,000 across three open pits; each figure was individually sculpted with distinct costume, height, and facial expression. The Ancient City Wall, 13 kilometers in circumference, remains the most significant and best-preserved example in China. The itinerary includes private ground transport, a local English-speaking guide, and return passage to Beijing by bullet train.
highlights: Great Mosque: Ming dynasty structure blending Chinese and Islamic architecture, standing on religious foundations from the Tang dynasty
Muslim Quarter streets: narrow lanes lined with sesame-oil factories, halal butchers, small mosques, and markets
Terracotta Warriors: approximately 6,000 individually sculpted clay figures in battle formation, discovered in 1976
Big Wild Goose Pagoda: former repository of Buddhist relics and texts brought from India by the Tang dynasty monk Xuanzang; musical fountain show at north square

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Beijing to Xi'an: Great Mosque and Muslim Quarter
Your guide meets you in your Beijing hotel lobby before dawn to reach the train station for a six-hour journey south on the high-speed rail to Xi'an. On arrival, you settle into your accommodation, then begin with the Great Mosque, the most significant mosque in China. The structure dates to the Hongwu period of the Ming dynasty, with subsequent additions during the Qing; earlier religious complexes occupied this same ground as far back as the Tang dynasty, creating a palimpsest of architectural intent. The building fuses Chinese and Islamic elements throughout. Afterward, a walk through the Muslim Quarter introduces the narrow streets where the Hui Muslim community has lived for centuries. Sesame-oil factories, halal butchers, small neighbourhood mosques, market stalls, and restaurants line the passageways, creating a self-contained commercial and cultural enclave distinct from the surrounding city.

Day 2 — Terracotta Warriors and Big Wild Goose Pagoda
The morning is devoted to the Terracotta Warriors, the clay army discovered in 1976 when local farmers dug a well and broke through a buried vault. Of the estimated 6,000 warriors created for the emperor's afterlife, just under 2,000 stand visible across three main excavated pits. Each figure was hand-sculpted from clay with individual costume, height, and facial expression — a staggering exercise in repetition and variation carried out over two millennia ago. After examining the site, lunch takes place in a local village restaurant. Your private transport then carries you to the Big Wild Goose Pagoda, a seven-story structure that once held Buddhist relics and classical texts brought westward from India by the Tang monk Xuanzang. If timing allows, the musical fountain performance at the temple's north square provides a contemporary counterpoint to the ancient site.

Day 3 — Ancient City Wall and Return to Beijing
The final morning visits Xi'an's Ancient City Wall on foot or by bicycle. The wall extends 13 kilometers in circumference and ranks as China's most significant and best-preserved example of its type, running the perimeter of the historic centre. A bicycle circuit takes roughly two hours. By afternoon, you depart Xi'an on a six-hour northbound high-speed rail journey, arriving at Beijing West Railway Station in late afternoon where the tour concludes.

tour.name: One day hike on Great Wall Mutianyu
tour.summary:
Overview
Mutianyu Great Wall located in Huairou County 70 km northeast of central Beijing. The Wall of Mutianyu is connected with Jiankou in the west and Lianhuachi in the east. As one of the best-preserved parts of the Great Wall, Mutianyu section used to serve as the northern barrier defending the capital and the imperial tombs. First built in the mid-6th century during the Northern Qi, the Mutianyu section is older than the Badaling section of the Great Wall. During the Ming dynasty, under the supervision of General Xu Da, construction of the present wall began, building over the past wall. 



In 1404, a pass built in the wall. In 1569, the Mutianyu Great Wall rebuilt and till today most parts of it are well preserved. The Mutianyu Great Wall has the most significant construction scale and best quality among all sections of Great Wall. Follow your knowledgeable guide along the wondrous weave of the wall and marvel at the 2- or 3-story towers from ancient origins. Admire spectacular views of the Chinese countryside and gain a fascinating insight into this magnificent monument.  Sip bottled water and capture fantastic photographs throughout your exploration and note the perpetually changing perspective achieved by dipping gradients and steep inclines.
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 Beijing – Mutianyu – Beijing (L)
Your guide comes and picks you up at your hotel in Beijing at 08:00Am. Travel to Mutianyu Great Wall in private van. The drive will take about 1. 5 hours. On arrival you will start to hike on the wall.

Follow your expert local guide to Mutianyu Great Wall. It will take you 30 mins walk up from entrance to enter the Wall. We will walk up to the Watchtower 8, takes about 30 mins staright up on the staris. Once we are on the Wall, we will do a loop walk from Watchtower 8 to Watchtower 20 and then come back to Watchtower 6. There are three options downhill: By walking, by Cable Car or by Tobaggan.

After the hike, we will head to local farmer's restaurant to have lunch. Meet and chat with the farmers over a home-cooked Chinese meal and learn the surrounding community developement. Then we will drive back to Beijing and drop you off at your hotel.

output.summary: Mutianyu, located 70 kilometers northeast of Beijing in Huairou County, represents one of the most intact stretches of the Great Wall. Built initially during the Northern Qi dynasty in the mid-6th century and substantially reconstructed under Ming general Xu Da, this section connected the capital's northern defense line with the imperial tombs. The wall's 2- and 3-story watchtowers rise across steep terrain, their preservation notably superior to many other accessible sections. A day hike here moves from the entrance through rising switchbacks to Watchtower 8, then traverses the wall itself via Watchtower 20 before circling back to Watchtower 6. The surrounding countryside reveals both the defensive logic of the wall's placement and the rural communities that have inhabited these slopes for centuries.

tour.name: Mardi Himal Treks
tour.summary:
The Mardi Himal Trek is an absolute choice for those who are seeking for an adventurous trekking experience in the peaceful parts of the Annapurna region of Nepal, spectacularly situated in the east of popular treks of Nepal.  Thin Numbers of trekkers make their way to the Mardi Himal Base Camp out positioned exceptionally at the base of Mardi Himal and the Annapurna region´s most exemplary mount Machapuchhre actually gives meaning "Fish tail", leading mesmerizingly up to with maximum altitude of 4500m. After reaching at high camp (3850m), it takes 3-4 hours to arrive. Mardi Himal base camp.

On top of this, we’ll get to pass by the solitary trails complete with verdant forests, beautiful villages, valleys, terraced farms, dazzling rivers and the extraordinary views of the Annapurna, Machhapuchre (Fishtail) and Himchuli mountains. Another merit about this trekking route is that the trail makes a small circuit up to the base camp of Mardi Himal so that we don’t have to backtrack over the same terrain. Therefore, Mardi Himal Trek a moderate to adventurous trip without the problem of getting AMS (Acute Mountain Sickness.  Because of amalgamation of the adventure and natural delights, it is the brilliant journey.

Accommodation

In our package, accommodation in Kathmandu, 3 star categories of Hotels are made available. Likewise, accommodation in trekking days is in Tea Houses. Our guide will choose a best and regular using normal guest houses, lodges and home stay as per necessity if any. Besides, your guide will help you to choose foods. We ensure you the quality services.

Physical fitness and experiences required

For its completion based on your schedule or fitness level, this trek requires a moderate level of fitness as we’ll have to trek through rocky section near base camp and high camp. Our clients are recommended to see a doctor before they go for a check-up and to talk about dealing with altitude sickness. Trekkers will have to initially decide on their self adjustment of weather changes and also schedule changes in itinerary beyond our control. Experience would be plus point for trekkers. Basic medical helps are our responsibility. Besides, trekkers are advised to carry their medicines if any prescribed earlier by doctors.

Best time to trek

October to May is the most visited season to Mardi Himal base camp. This trek is suitable all year round as the winter brings out the real beauty of the snow-capped peaks and the summer brings out the beauty of the pine, rhododendron and bamboo forest. Hence, October is the best time to start with.

Day 1 — Arrival in Kathmandu
Arrival at Tribhuwan International Airport followed by hotel transfer. An evening briefing outlines the trek itinerary and logistics. Overnight accommodation in Kathmandu.

Day 2 — Kathmandu to Pokhara by Road
A 6- to 7-hour drive westward from Kathmandu to Pokhara passes through towns including Thankot, Naubise, Baireni, Muglin, and Maleku. The journey is typically scheduled early to avoid daytime traffic. Pokhara, situated at the base of the Annapurna range alongside Phewa Lake, serves as the launching point for the trek. Overnight accommodation in Pokhara.

Day 3 — Kande to Pitam Deurali and Forest Camp
A drive from Pokhara reaches Kande, where the trek begins. The initial ascent to Dhampus is steep; the path then eases as it continues to Pothana, passing through mixed forest. Overnight at a tea house in Pothana.

Day 4 — Pothana to Low Camp
A 5-hour trek climbs from Forest Camp to Low Camp at 3,150 meters through rhododendron and moss-covered forest, with occasional glimpses of ferns and lichen on the trees. As elevation increases, the forest composition shifts noticeably. Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) comes into view up the valley. Overnight at Low Camp tea house.

Day 5 — Low Camp to High Camp on the Mardi Himal Ridge
The trail climbs approximately one hour to 3,700 meters, where it breaks above the tree line onto grass slopes and ridges. The route continues along the Mardi Himal ridge, mostly on open grass with scattered rhododendron bushes. Views open westward to Annapurna South and Himchuli. Danphe pheasant are observed on this section. Accommodation is in well-maintained tea houses or lodges at High Camp.

Day 6 — Mardi Himal Base Camp and Return to Low Camp
An early start allows for sunrise views before breakfast. From High Camp, the path follows the ridge crest toward Mardi Himal Base Camp at 4,500 meters, with a few steeper sections through grass. Dzokpo (yak-cow crossbreds) and Danphe pheasant inhabit the high pastures; sheep and goats from lower villages are brought up to graze seasonally. At 4,500 meters, the Annapurna Sanctuary spreads into view—the south face of Annapurna, surrounding peaks, Himchuli, and Machhapuchhre fill the panorama. The return to Low Camp allows for overnight rest and acclimatization.

Day 7 — Low Camp to Siding via Circuit Descent
A 6-hour trek descends from Low Camp along a different route from the ascent, completing the circuit. The path drops to Siding, a traditional Nepalese settlement that remains apart from main trekking circuits. Overnight accommodation is often in a homestay, allowing direct contact with village life and daily routines. Evening meals typically include dal bhat (lentil rice), the staple of Nepalese home cooking.

Day 8 — Siding to Pokhara via Lumre
The trek descends 3 hours from Siding to the roadhead at Lumre, passing through the villages of Kalimati and Ghalel. Kalimati is primarily Brahmin, with mixed populations in Ghalel and Siding. A jeep or similar vehicle completes the 2-hour drive back to Pokhara. Overnight accommodation in Pokhara.

Day 9 — Pokhara to Kathmandu
After breakfast, a tourist bus returns travelers to Kathmandu (approximately 6 hours). A farewell dinner at a local restaurant features Nepalese food and traditional dance. Overnight in Kathmandu.

Day 10 — Departure
Transfer to Tribhuwan International Airport for departure, or onward travel within Nepal if arranged.

tour.name: Lhasa Namtso Lake Tour
tour.summary:
The Lhasa Namtso Lake Tour is an exploration of the historical city of Lhasa and Namtso Lake. Namtso Lake in Tibet is the second-largest lake in Tibet. It is situated 250 Km northern from Lhasa. Namtso lake extent 70 km from east to west and 30 km from south to west. This lake is covering as area of 1920 sq km and is situated at an altitude of 4748 m. Small Himalayan peaks are surrounding and well hanging of Tibetan prayer flags makes more beautiful. This lake is also regarded as a holy Lake in Tibet. Namtso Lake from Lhasa can be a day tour or a night stay at a simple guest house near the lake.

The historical city of Lhasa and sightseeing around is exploring important Tibetan monuments. Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, Barkhor Street, Drepung Monastery, and Sera Monastery are the listed of most visiting place in Lhasa. Lhasa is connecting with international airport. Flight is only possible from any part of China and from Nepal. It is also connected with the train route from the main cities of China. Touch Kailash Travels and Tours offer a private Lhasa Namtso Lake Tour either direct from China or from Nepal.
highlights:
Historical city Lhasa and sightseeing in the main monuments of Lhasa
Exploration of the 2nd largest and holy Namtso Lake
tour.itineraries:
Day 01: Arrive in Lhasa (3650 m/11972ft). Overnight at Hotel
Arrive in Lhasa (Gonggar) airport or train station and be greeted by our airport representative who will escort you to the hotel with 1.5 hrs drive. The rest of day is leisured, acclimatized yourself to high latitude. 

Day 02: Sightseeing in Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
We begin our sightseeing tour that includes Potala Palace, the greatest monumental structure in Tibet, and it was once the center for both spiritual and temporal power of Tibet. You will be attracted deeply by rooms, halls, chapels, and furnishings of Potala Palace. And the stories that took place there will convulse you absolutely. In the afternoon, we will visit Jokhang Temple which is the holiest Tibet's temples. A palpable sense of reverence accompanies a visit here. The constant bustle, dazzling paraphernalia of worship, flickering butter lamps and wreaths of heady incense make the Jokhang Temple one of Tibet's most memorable experiences. Finally we will visit fascinating Barkhor Street which is Lhasa's liveliest place and it is also the main route for prayer wheels rotating. 

Day 03: Sightseeing in Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
This morning we make sightseeing tour of the Drepung Monastery which was once Tibet's richest Monastery, with four colleges and 10,000 monks in its heyday in the 17th century. A group of white buildings stands on the hillside and out against the majestic Mt. Gambo Utse, here you can get a wonderful view of the Lhasa City and surrounding scenery. The next sightseeing spot is Sera Monastery. It is famous for its warrior monks, Dob-Doa. After that, we will visit Norbulingka which was once the summer palace of the Dalai Lamas. It contains several palaces, chapels, and buildings. Finally we drive back to the hotel. 

Day 04: Drive Lhasa to Namtso Lake & back to Lhasa. Overnight at Hotel
Drive to visit the second largest salt water lake in China.Namtso Lake is the biggest lake located at the highest altitude in the world. The Lake maintains its levels from rainfall and melted snow flowing from high mountains. Namtso is also popular for being a sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site where Zhaxi Temple is situated. The Lake's beauty should not be missed by any traveler during the visit in Tibet. 

Day 05: Departure from Lhasa
After breakfast you will be transferred to airport to connect flight to Kathmandu or other destinations OR drop to train station.

output.summary: This five-day itinerary moves between Lhasa's monastic architecture and Namtso Lake, Tibet's second-largest body of water, situated 250 kilometers north of the capital at an altitude of 4,748 meters. The route begins with acclimatization in Lhasa before progressing through the city's major religious sites—Potala Palace, the former seat of temporal and spiritual authority; Jokhang Temple, regarded as Tibet's holiest sanctuary; and the monasteries of Drepung and Sera, which historically housed thousands of monks. A full day is devoted to the drive north to Namtso Lake, where the water body extends 70 kilometers east to west and 30 kilometers south to north, covering an area of 1,920 square kilometers. The lake is encircled by Himalayan peaks and marked as a sacred Buddhist pilgrimage site, with Zhaxi Temple situated on its shores. The itinerary accommodates both day-excursion and overnight options at guesthouses near the lake, returning to Lhasa by evening or the following morning.

Drepung Monastery — historically one of Tibet's largest monastic centers, with views across Lhasa valley from its hillside position
Sera Monastery — known for its scholarly tradition and monastic debate practices
Namtso Lake at 4,748 meters — the second-largest saltwater lake in China, ringed by Himalayan peaks and prayer flags

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Lhasa
Arrival at Lhasa Gonggar Airport or the main train station, followed by a 90-minute transfer to accommodation in the city. Lhasa sits at 3,650 meters above sea level. The first day is reserved for acclimatization to the altitude; no structured activities are scheduled.

Day 2 — Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, and Barkhor Street
The morning begins with a visit to Potala Palace, a multi-story complex that served as the winter residence and seat of religious authority for the Dalai Lamas. The structure contains numerous halls, chapels, and chambers arranged across its hillside location. In the afternoon, the itinerary moves to Jokhang Temple, the foremost pilgrimage destination in Tibet. The temple interior is animated by continuous religious activity—devotees circumambulating, butter lamps burning, and incense rising through the galleries. A final stop is Barkhor Street, the principal circumambulation route in central Lhasa, lined with shops, prayer wheels, and pilgrims on circuit.

Day 3 — Drepung, Sera, and Norbulingka
The morning is spent at Drepung Monastery, situated on a hillside overlooking Lhasa. In its seventeenth-century peak, the site housed four distinct colleges and approximately 10,000 monks; its white buildings are clustered against the backdrop of Mount Gambo Utse. The location provides extended views across the Lhasa valley. In the afternoon, the route proceeds to Sera Monastery, recognized for its scholarly monastic tradition and the practice of structured debate among monks. A final stop is Norbulingka, the summer palace complex of the Dalai Lamas, which contains multiple residential and ceremonial buildings arranged as a formal compound.

Day 4 — Namtso Lake Excursion
A full day devoted to the drive north to Namtso Lake, positioned 250 kilometers from Lhasa. The lake, Tibet's second largest, covers 1,920 square kilometers and sits at an altitude of 4,748 meters. The water body is fed by rainfall and snowmelt from surrounding Himalayan peaks, which ring the shoreline. Zhaxi Temple stands on the lake's edge, marking the site as a major Buddhist pilgrimage destination. The route returns to Lhasa by evening, or accommodation at a nearby guesthouse may be arranged for an overnight stay.

Day 5 — Departure from Lhasa
Transfer to Lhasa airport or train station for onward travel to Kathmandu or other destinations.

output.subtitle: Village trekking, temple exploration, and tea estates from Sigiriya to Yala National Park
output.summary: This 11-day itinerary moves through Sri Lanka's interior and southern regions, staying in community-based lodges and family-run guesthouses rather than resort chains. The route connects Sigiriya's archaeological zone with Kandy's temple district, then ascends into the central highlands via train to the tea-growing regions of Bandarawela and Haputale, before descending to the wildlife sanctuary at Yala and the coastal village of Bentota. Days center on walking—village trekking, tea estate trails, mountain passes, and monastery approaches—alongside stays in local homes and conservation-focused lodges. The pace is deliberate, with transfers by road, rail, and foot, and with participation in local activities: lake fishing, cookery in a private residence, early-morning game drives, and overnight treks through mist-covered terrain.

Tea estate trails in Bandarawela and Haputale, walking through working plantations

output.name: Sri Lanka: Wildlife Safari and Bird Trails — 7 Days
output.subtitle: Jeep safaris through four national parks tracking elephants, leopards, and endemic birds across wetland, savanna, and forest habitats
output.summary: This seven-day itinerary moves through Sri Lanka's primary wildlife reserves, beginning in the montane forests of Kitulgala and progressing through the lowland parks of Udawalawe, Bundala, and Yala. The route centers on morning and evening safari drives and bird-watching walks, timed to coincide with peak animal activity. Kitulgala's forest trails yield endemic species—Orange-billed Babblers, Chestnut-backed Owlets, Green Pit Vipers—and a diversity of butterflies and reptiles. Udawalawe's open grassland and reservoir support a permanent population of approximately 250 Sri Lankan elephants, among the easiest on the island to observe. Bundala's wetlands attract around 100 water bird species, including seasonal Greater Flamingos in flocks exceeding 1,000 birds, alongside resident Lesser Whistling Ducks, Little Cormorants, and waders. Yala, the largest reserve, holds all four members of Sri Lanka's 'big four' wildlife: elephant herds, sloth bears, leopards (elusive and primarily nocturnal), and wild buffalo. Transfers between parks involve three to four-hour drives; accommodation is provided in safari lodges positioned near park gates. All meals, park entrance fees, and English-speaking guide services are included.

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Colombo and Transfer to Kitulgala
Meet your representative at Colombo International Airport and transfer to Kitulgala, a 2-hour drive inland. An evening bird-watching trail visits the village surroundings. Overnight at Kitulgala Adventures.

Day 2 — Kitulgala Bird Watching and Forest Wildlife
Start early with a bird-watching trail through Kitulgala's forests, a destination prized by nature enthusiasts for its concentration of endemic species. The region consistently yields sightings of Sri Lanka Orange-billed Babblers and Chestnut-backed Owlets, along with reptiles including Green Pit Vipers and Earless Lizards. A variety of butterfly species inhabit the trails as well. After breakfast at the camp site, spend the rest of the day at leisure or exploring the immediate surroundings. An evening bird-watching walk in the village provides another opportunity to observe local wildlife as light conditions shift. Return to Kitulgala Adventures for the night.

Day 3 — Udawalawe National Park Safari
After breakfast, a transfer takes you south to Udawalawe National Park, a reserve centered on its reservoir and surrounding grassland. The landscape here favors wildlife viewing across open terrain. You'll visit the park on an evening safari drive, searching for elephants, buffalo, and other inhabitants as light begins to soften. The day concludes at Nil Diya Mankada Safari Lodge.

Day 4 — Udawalawe Elephants to Bundala's Waterbirds
Begin with a morning safari at Udawalawe National Park, where Sri Lankan elephants congregate around the reservoir. The park's open habitats make these animals relatively easy to locate—roughly 250 are permanently resident here. The elephants' attraction to the water creates reliable sighting opportunities across the landscape.

Mid-morning, transfer south to Bundala National Park, a coastal wetland system of lagoons and shallow waters. An evening safari follows, focusing on Bundala's avian wealth. The park hosts approximately 100 bird species, with half being seasonal migrants. Greater Flamingos from India's Rann of Kutch arrive in massive flocks exceeding 1,000 individuals, though their numbers fluctuate seasonally. Year-round residents include Lesser Whistling Ducks, Garganey, Little Cormorants, Indian Cormorants, Grey Herons, Black-headed Ibises, Eurasian Spoonbills, Asian Openbills, and Painted Storks. Medium and small wading species of Tringa and Charadrius subspecies are common. Rarer sightings include Black-necked Storks, Lesser Adjutants, and Eurasian Coots. Overnight stay at Yala Lake Camp.

Day 5 — Full-Day Safari in Yala National Park
A full-day safari in Yala National Park covers the island's largest wildlife reserve and its primary habitat for all four members of Sri Lanka's 'big four': elephants, sloth bears, leopards, and wild buffalo. Elephant herds move seasonally to smaller reservoirs—Butuwe and Mahaseelawa—during the dry season, where they congregate and are readily visible. Uraniya reservoir is known for aquatic birds, wild buffalo, and both Mugger and saltwater crocodiles. Sloth bears, solitary and primarily nocturnal, are harder to encounter; sightings are seasonal. Leopards remain elusive, requiring persistence and luck. The reserve spans varied terrain, and safaris follow established routes through grassland and scattered woodland. Overnight stay at Yala Lake Camp.

Day 6 — Tissamaharama Bird Walk and Return to Colombo
A morning bird-watching walk covers the forest and reservoir system at Tissamaharama, near Yala's boundary. After breakfast, the journey north begins with a transfer back to Colombo by road. Overnight accommodation is at Cinnamon Red hotel in the capital.

Day 7 — Departure
After breakfast, transfer to Colombo International Airport for departure, approximately 1 hour from the hotel.

output.subtitle: A three-hour cycling route through the residential neighborhoods and everyday haunts of central Tokyo, following local commute paths and established gathering spots.

The route covers roughly three hours of cycling on flat terrain, with regular stops at foot-traffic destinations. A guide accompanies the group throughout, and bicycles with helmets are provided.
