tour.name: NORTHERN LAOS - HILLTRIBES & JUNGLES
tour.subtitle: HOUAY XAY - VIENG PHOUKA - LUANG NAMTHA - MUANG KHUA - NONG KHIAW - LUANG PRABANG
tour.summary: Trek through the mountains and Valleys of rural Northern Laos, cruise rivers and truly engage with local hilltribes. Starting from your pick up at the Laos/Thailand Border you will be taken on an adventure through tiny villages, which are home to many of the different ethnic groups in Laos. The Nam Ha National Protected Area will be your base to set out on a trek of a lifetime through the jungle. Visit the emerging towns in the area where farmers and local artisans come to trade their wares Before reaching the former Royal Capital and UNESCO world heritage site Luang Prabang.
tour.itineraries:
DAY 1  |THAI BORDER – HOUAY XAY - VIENG PHOUKHA (L)
After transferring on your own from Chiang Rai to the Thai-Lao border crossing at Houay Xai, our guide will meet you at the Lao immigration office and assist you with the visa process. Then we'll drive to Vieng Phouka, stopping along the way at a Lanten village - the name 'Lanten' is a Chinese term meaning “the people who dye," as they are known for their natural dye traditions; they're also one of the few ethnic minorities in Lao PDR who follow Daoism and read Chinese script.
Our journey today will end in Vieng Phouka. a rural village in the heart of northern Laos. Take time to discover the area and meet some of the local people. You'll spend the night in a local, very basic guesthouse. 

DAY 02  | VIENG PHOUKHA – LUANG NAMTHA (B/L)
Today we continue our journey on to Luang Namtha, heading over the mountain route to take in the stunning views. Upon reaching Luang Namtha take a stroll around the town, visit the busy night market where locals come together to trade goods and handicrafts and also delicious street food.
Overnight in Luang Namtha 

DAY  03 | TREKKING IN NAM HA NPA (3 DAYS / 2 NIGHTS) (B/L/D)
We'll embark on 3 days of trekking through the forests, fields, rivers and mountains that surround Luang Namtha. Many interesting and challenging treks in this area await you, so you'll choose among a selection of routes to suit your fitness and stamina. Our guides will then arrange the most interesting route, points of interest and resting points for you. 
Overnight in village homestay 

DAY 04 | TREKKING IN THE NAM HA NPA (B/L/D)
Spend another day exploring the stunninging Nam Ha Protected area. Your guide will lead you off the beaten path to discover the natural beauty and wildlife that abounds in this region.
Overnight in village homestay 

DAY 05 | TREKKING IN NAM HA NPA - LUANG NAMTHA (B/L)
Continue with your trekking adventure in the wilds of Luang Namtha. We’ll end the day back at the city in a clean and comfortable room.
Overnight in Luang Namtha 

DAY 06 | LUANG NAMTHA  – MUANG KHUA (B/L)
Rise early like the locals and take a walk to the local market, where you may see members of hill tribes in traditional clothing buying and selling their products.
After breakfast, you'll take a private minivan through the countryside to Muang Khua.  You can enjoy the beautiful landscape along the way.  Northern Laos is very ethnically diverse and the mountains surrounding Oudomxay, near the Chinese border, are home to groups like the Akha, Iko, Hmong, Khmu and more.  Despite modernization many of these hill tribes still live traditional lifestyles and follow local and ethnic customs. You're likely in these regions to see people in beautiful traditional clothing. 
Overnight in Muang Khua 

DAY 07 |  MUANG KHUA - MUANG NGOY (B/L)
The boat ride from Muang Khua to Muang Ngoy winds through mountainous jungle. The Nam Ou River, one of the most important in the Lao PDR, offers some of the best scenery. The river runs 448 km from Phongsaly in the north of the country all the way to Luang Prabang where it merges with the Mekong. On board the traditional Lao longtail boat we’ll journey slowly downstream, allowing you to take in the view and relax along the way. The boat will pass many remote villages, rugged mountain terrain and impressive limestone cliffs. We'll stop at a few of the villages, most of which are only accessible by boat, and get a unique look into traditional daily village life along the river. The day's journey will end in Muang Ngoy, a relaxing little village where we’ll spend the night.
Overnight in Muang Ngoy 

DAY 08 |  MUANG NGOY - NONG KHIAW (B/L)
After a short boat ride you'll reach the village of Ban Hat Sao, with a mixed population of Lao Lum and Lao Thung. From the village we will follow little trails on a jungle trek through a preserved part of the jungle and into the nearby mountain area. We’ll pass rice fields, forests and agricultural land on our way to the next highlight, a refreshing waterfall. Much of our route follows the stream and we’ll walk through the river and small waterfalls. After an extended break we’ll hike back to the river area. A small walking trail following the Nam Ou River will bring us to Nong Khiaw.
Overnight in Nong Khiaw 

DAY 09 |  THE 100 WATERFALLS TREK (B/L)
After a one-hour boat trip on the Nam Ou we'll start exploring and hiking through the "100 waterfalls," a recently discovered jungle waterfall. A village visit is included as well, where you learn more about life along the Nam Ou River. In the evening we’ll ride back on our boat to Nong Khiaw.
Overnight in Nong Khiaw 

DAY 10 |  NONG KHIAW - LUANG PRABANG (B/L) 
We’ll drive a winding route following the Nam Ou River through the mountains from Nong Khiaw to Luang Prabang.  Along the way we'll visit the village of Ban Nayang, which is famous for its traditional cotton weaving.  Almost every household has its own weaving loom where the families create beautiful scarves, tablecloths and ornate wall hangings. Then we'll continue to the UNESCO World Heritage City of Luang Prabang, where we'll take you to your hotel or transfer to Luang Prabang Airport for departure. 
— END OF SERVICES —

output.subtitle: Trek the Nam Ha National Protected Area and travel by longtail boat down the Nam Ou River through remote villages and limestone terrain, ending in Luang Prabang.
output.summary: This 10-day route moves through rural northern Laos from the Thai border to the former royal capital, combining three distinct phases: initial hill-tribe village walks around Luang Namtha and the Nam Ha Protected Area; a three-day forest trek through mixed terrain; and a downriver journey by traditional longtail boat through a landscape of limestone cliffs and river villages accessible primarily by water. The itinerary passes through settlements of Lanten, Akha, Hmong, Khmu, and Lao Lum communities, with stops at local markets, a waterfall system, and Ban Nayang's cotton-weaving households. Accommodation ranges from village homestays during trekking phases to guesthouses and hotels in town bases. The pace allows time in each location without rushed transitions; guides are English-speaking and can adjust trek routes based on group fitness and conditions. The route concludes in Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
highlights: Three-day trek through Nam Ha National Protected Area, combining forest, agricultural fields, and river crossings.
Longtail boat passage down the 448-kilometre Nam Ou River from Muang Khua to Muang Ngoy, passing limestone cliffs and boat-accessible villages

Hiking through the 100 Waterfalls area near Nong Khiaw with a village visit
Market visits in Vieng Phouka, Luang Namtha, and Muang Khua where Akha, Hmong, Khmu, and Lao vendors trade goods and traditional textiles

output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Thai Border to Vieng Phouka via Lanten Village
The itinerary begins at the Lao immigration office at the Thai–Lao border crossing near Houay Xai. After visa processing assistance from your guide, a vehicle drive proceeds to Vieng Phouka, a rural settlement in the northern Laos highlands. En route, a stop is made at a Lanten village; the Lanten are an ethnic minority in Laos known for natural dyeing traditions and are among the few Lao ethnic groups who practice Daoism and use Chinese script. In Vieng Phouka, time allows for walking through the village and meeting local residents. Accommodation is in a basic local guesthouse.

Day 2 — Vieng Phouka to Luang Namtha Over Mountain Route
The journey continues by vehicle over a mountain route to Luang Namtha, a commercial town serving the surrounding agricultural region. Upon arrival, a walk through the town allows for visiting the night market, where local vendors—including hill-tribe farmers and artisans—sell handicrafts, textiles, and prepared foods. Overnight accommodation is in Luang Namtha.

Day 3 — Nam Ha Protected Area Trek — Day One
A three-day trekking phase begins today in the Nam Ha National Protected Area surrounding Luang Namtha. Multiple trek routes of varying difficulty are available; guides arrange a route suited to the group's fitness level, incorporating forests, agricultural fields, streams, and mountain terrain. Accommodation is in a village homestay.

Day 4 — Trekking Deeper into Nam Ha Protected Area
Your guide leads you off the beaten path through the Nam Ha Protected Area, where unspoiled forest and abundant wildlife define this remote landscape. See the natural beauty that characterizes this remarkable region. You'll overnight in a village homestay.

Day 5 — Nam Ha Trek — Day Three and Return to Luang Namtha
The final day of trekking concludes with a return to Luang Namtha by afternoon or evening. Accommodation upgrades to a hotel with standard amenities.

Day 6 — Luang Namtha Market to Muang Khua
An early morning walk to the local market in Luang Namtha offers the chance to observe Akha, Hmong, Khmu, and other hill-tribe community members buying and selling agricultural products and textiles in traditional dress. After breakfast, a private minivan travels through countryside to Muang Khua, a journey of several hours through terrain home to multiple ethnic groups. The northern mountains near the Chinese border support Akha, Iko, Hmong, and Khmu settlements; many households maintain traditional practices and clothing despite gradual modernization. Overnight accommodation is in Muang Khua.

Day 7 — Muang Khua to Muang Ngoy by Nam Ou Longtail Boat
Today begins a two-day river journey on the Nam Ou, one of the Lao PDR's principal waterways. The Nam Ou flows 448 kilometres from Phongsaly Province in the far north to Luang Prabang, where it joins the Mekong River. A traditional Lao wooden longtail boat carries the group downriver at a leisurely pace through mountainous jungle terrain marked by limestone cliffs and narrow gorges. The boat passes multiple villages, most accessible only by water; brief stops allow observation of daily river life and boat-based settlements. The journey ends in Muang Ngoy, a small village on the river. Overnight accommodation is in Muang Ngoy.

Day 8 — Muang Ngoy to Nong Khiaw: Jungle Trek and River Trail
A short boat ride returns to Ban Hat Sao, a mixed Lao Lum and Lao Thung settlement. From the village, walking trails lead into preserved forest and adjacent mountain areas, passing rice paddies, agricultural land, and a waterfall cascade. Much of the route follows a stream through forest; portions involve wading through water and smaller falls. After an extended break at the waterfall, the trek returns to the river area. A walking trail along the Nam Ou River bank leads to Nong Khiaw. Overnight accommodation is in Nong Khiaw.

Day 9 — The 100 Waterfalls Trek and Village Visit
After a one-hour boat trip upriver on the Nam Ou, hiking begins through the 100 Waterfalls area, a recently documented cascade system in the jungle. A village visit is included, providing context on life along the Nam Ou River corridor. The group returns to Nong Khiaw by boat in the evening. Overnight accommodation is in Nong Khiaw.

Day 10 — Nong Khiaw to Luang Prabang via Ban Nayang
A winding vehicle route follows the Nam Ou River through mountain terrain from Nong Khiaw to Luang Prabang. En route, a stop is made in Ban Nayang, known for traditional cotton weaving; nearly all households contain manually operated looms on which families produce cotton scarves, tablecloths, and decorative wall hangings. The drive continues to Luang Prabang, a UNESCO World Heritage site and former royal capital. Hotel check-in or airport transfer concludes the itinerary. End of services.

tour.name: Essential Korea
tour.summary: South Korea, here you come. Explore futuristic skyscrapers, historic markets, picturesque temples and oh-so scenic walking trails on this 13-day adventure. First things first: your tastebuds will absolutely be taken care of with traditional delicacies like green tea and crisped-to-perfection fried chicken. But you'll of course venture deep into Korean culture with visits to the DMZ and Hanok villages, peaceful stays in a mountain temple, and watching haenyeo women divers off the shore of Jeju.
highlights:
Visit the Demilitarized Zone between North and South Korea
Sleep in a temple in Gyeongju-si
Experience tranquility and tradition with an overnight stay at a historic hanok village
Witness the remarkable women divers of Jeju Island
Stroll through the serene and picturesque Damyang Bamboo Forest
tour.itineraries:
Day 1  Seoul
Welcome to Seoul! As fellow travellers are arriving throughout the day, there are no planned activities until a group meeting at 6 pm. Check into the hotel and enjoy the city.

After the welcome meeting, join your CEO for an orientation walk down Cheonggyecheon Stream to learn about Seoul while walking past small waterfalls and nearly two dozen overhead bridges. Then, enjoy the dense grid of streets found in the bustling neighbourhood of Myeongdong which is packed with people at all hours of the day looking to enjoy some of the best shopping, street food, and nightlife in all of Korea.

Opt for a group dinner to end your first night!

The most convenient way to get around South Korea is by public transportation and on foot. The country's train system is world renowned so the majority of our trips utilize this efficient train network. In this tour, you will need to be able to spend the majority of the day on your feet and carry your luggage through busy train stations and streets. Please ensure you are fit enough to carry your own luggage and spend most of the day on your feet.

Seoul Orientation Walk                           Seoul
Enjoy a brief walk with your CEO who will give you some tips on finding things like supermarkets, main squares, and ATMs. You'll be taken through Cheonggyecheon Stream which is an 8.4 kilometre (5.2 mile) waterway and public space that runs through the heart of downtown Seoul. Myeongdong is another popular spot you'll hit on your orientation walk. This exciting district features street food carts, major shopping malls, and entertainment.

Your Welcome Moment: Meet Your CEO and Group
Your opportunity to meet your CEO and fellow travellers, and learn more about your tour. Opt to join the group for a local meal afterwards. Don't forget to see the notice in the lobby (or ask reception) for the official time and place to meet up with the group.

Accommodation
Below is an example of the hotel we may use in this city. For the actual hotel your specific departure will be using, please check your voucher.

Hotel Prince (or similar)Hotel
Day 2  Seoul
Sit back and relax on a private bus and enjoy a tour of the bustling metropolis where modern skyscrapers, high-tech subways and pop culture meet Buddhist temples and street markets. Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace, the National Folklore Museum, Bukchon Hanok Village and Insadong alley.

After exploring the city, opt to see a show, explore a local museum, or hit the pavement and eat your way through street markets trying local fares such as bibimbap, soondae, and kimchi.

Gyeongbokgung Palace                          Seoul
Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace, the main royal palace of the Joseon Dynasty built in 1395. The palace has been destroyed many times over, but more than 50 per cent of the buildings are still standing or are restored. The complex is also home to the National Palace Museum and the National Folk Museum.

Insadong Alley                                         Seoul
Explore the narrow and hidden alleys of one of the most memorable places in Seoul. Now filled with antique shops, galleries, tea houses and traditional restaurants, this area once housed the royal studio for painters during the Joseon Dynasty.

National Folklore Museum                       Seoul
Located within the grounds of the Gyeongbokgung Palace, learn about the history and traditions of the Korean people during the Joseon era.

Seoul City Tour                                         Seoul
Enjoy a bus tour of the bustling capital of South Korea. Visit different areas of the city including Gyengbokgung Palace, National Folklore Museum, Jogyesa Temple, Bukchon Hanok Village and Insadong alley.

Free Time                                                 Seoul
Head out and explore.

Bukchon Hanok Village Exploration         Seoul          1h
Be transported back 600 years into Seoul's past while walking through Bukchon Hanok Village, which boasts the largest cluster of privately owned traditional Korean wooden homes (hanok) in Seoul. Keep an eye out for the half-dozen or so alleys that have beautifully restored architectural features like small courtyards, decorative outer walls, and dark tiled roofs.

Optional Activities - Day 2

Gwangjang Market Visit                           Seoul
Gwangjang Market is one of the oldest and largest traditional markets in South Korea, with more than 5,000 shops. Famous for its fabric, local treasures, and noted to be one of the best places to go for authentic Korean street food in Seoul, you don't want to miss Gwangjang Market.

Seoul Museum of History Visit                  Seoul          Free
Really get to know Seoul with a stop at the Seoul Museum of History, which highlights each segment of the city's past from the Stone Age to present day. Discover one of the museum's recent creations – a large floor map of Seoul, great for plotting out your next steps!

Accommodation
Hotel Prince (or similar)  Hotel
Meals included: Breakfast
Day 3  Seoul/Gyeongju-si
After breakfast, board a high speed bullet train for a relaxing morning ride through the countryside to Gyeongju. Once the group arrives to this old capital city for 1,000 years, they will experience an overnight stay in a local temple. During the stay the group will learn about temple etiquette, watch a monk martial arts performance, experience the daily prayer ritual and a temple style dinner.

Stay in rooms called Ondol. These rooms are very traditional, heated to be cozy and comfortable, with beds made up directly on the floor. The rooms here are multi-share, divided up by male and female rooms. Enjoy a traditional dinner and breakfast during the stay.

Have the opportunity to learn about temple etiquette, experience the daily drum and bell ritual and take an easy hike up to the only stone cave temple in Korea for morning meditation.

Enjoy a peaceful morning meditation, martial arts practice, and drum and bell ritual before exploring in Gyeongiu. On the city tour visit to the UNESCO site of Bulguksa Temple located on the slopes of Mount Toham and admire the national treasures there, such as Dabotap and Seokgatap stone pagodas, Cheongun-gyo, and two gilt-bronze statues of Buddha. Afterwards, experience the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in Asia, Cheomseongdae Observatory, and the surrounding Royal Tombs.

Cheomseongdae Observatory           Gyeongju-si
Nestled in the heart of Gyeongju, the capital of the former Silla Kingdom, Cheomseongdae may not appear to be a monumental landmark. But this observatory tower that dates back to the seventh century is actually the oldest existing astronomical observatory in all of East Asia. Cheomseongdae was used for observing the stars in order to forecast the weather in the ancient scientific hub of Gyeongju.

Daereungwon Tomb Complex            Gyeongju-si                        1h
The Daereungwon Tomb complex in Gyeongju holds 23 tombs that are found inside of large mounds. The complex is beautiful with its rolling mounds and gardens, but the real treat can be found inside the tombs, the most famous being Cheonmachong and Hwangnamdaechong. Each tomb holds thousands of relics that gives us a window into the Silla Dynasty and its royal family. The contents of these tombs are over 1,500 years old and a great treasure to anyone who enjoys Korean history and artistic beauty.

After exploring the temple, check in to your hotel and get your bearings with an orientation walk on Haeundae Beach and Dongbaek Island (APEC House). Spend the evening getting to know colourful Busan, opt to treat yourself at a Jjimjilbang spa or sing your heart out at a popular karaoke bar.

Get a fascinating look into life during the Joseon Dynasty on this visit to the Yangdong Folk Village. Founded in the early 1400s, the village boasts well-preserved buildings and has more than 160 homes displaying traditional Joseon architecture within a gorgeous natural setting.

Haedong Yonggungsa Temple Visit                   Gijang-gun
Originally built in 1376, this picturesque, cliffside Buddhist temple overlooks the East China Sea. Opt to grab a bizarre local snack at the traditional market. Legend foretells that should you pray here, at least one of your wishes will come true.

Night Yacht Ride                                      Busan

Jjimjilbang                                          Busan
Treat yourself in one of Busan's jjimjilbans, a Korean spa bath house, with an array of hot spring tubs to rejuvenate mind, body, and soul.

Day 6  Busan/Seoul
In the seaside city, Busan, visit the bustling Jagalchi fish market, Gukjesijang market, Yongdusan Park, and the colourful Gamcheon Culture Village before traveling back to Seoul. After arriving in Seoul by train, check out Korea's oldest traditional market - Namdaemun Market. Then make your way by cable car to N Seoul Tower to see this beautiful landmark and opt to make the trip up to the observation deck. Spend the rest of your day in Seoul opting to see Banpo Bridge, the floating islands, or hanging out in the Gangnam district.

Yongdusan Park Visit                                     Busan
Visit Yongdusan Park, home to more than 70 different types of trees, and see the 118m (387 ft) high Busan Tower. The park's unique shape is said to look like a dragon's head.

N Seoul Tower Visit                                       Seoul
Take the cable car to visit the most iconic landmark in Seoul! Jagalchi Fish Market                                      Busan

Gukje Traditional Market                                 Busan

Now, it's a bustling international market where loads of food, home goods, clothes, souvenirs and more can be found.

Bullet Train                                                     Busan – Seoul        2h30m
Get to your next destination faster than the speed of light (ok maybe not that fast) aboard a high-speed train.

Gamcheon Culture Village                              Busan

Namdaemun Market Visit                                Seoul
Dating back to 1414, this is Korea's oldest traditional market and it's largest, with over 10,000 vendors spanning several city blocks. Get ready to shop!

Optional Activities - Day 6

N Seoul Tower Observatory                   Seoul     16000KRW per person
Namsan Seoul Tower Observatory allows for an incredible 360 degrees panoramic view of Seoul. The top of the tower is 480m above sea level, including Namsan Mountain (243m) and the tower’s own height (236.7m). It has quickly become a well-known landmark in Seoul and has appeared in lots of smash-hit K-dramas and movies.

Gangnam District Visit                           Seoul
Gangnam has plenty to do and see in this historically rich, fast-developing neighbourhood. Gangnam Station is the busiest subway station in Seoul and has a huge underground shopping centre, so feel free to shop until you drop. Choose to visit Bongeunsa, a Buddhist Temple in the centre of Gangnam, or enjoy the nightlife and restaurants in this area.

Floating Island Visit                                Seoul
The floating island is a culture complex made up of three man-made floating islands located near one end of the Banpo Bridge. LED lights surround the islands and create a fantastic night view - a must see if you're in Seoul!

Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain           Seoul     Free
Banpo Bridge is home to the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain Show and is the world's longest bridge fountain. Nearly 10,000 LED lights and 380 water spraying nozzles make up this beautiful show of water, music, and lights. During the day, the fountain shows a hundred different configurations meant to evoke waving willow branches and willow leaves. When the sun goes down, the fountain is illuminated as it sends out dancing, rainbow-coloured jets of water in the air in synchronization with music.

Visit the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), founded in 1953, separating North and South Korea. With over a million soldiers on watch each day, it is one of the last remnants of the Cold War. With a buffer zone 4km wide and spanning 250 km long there has been very little development in the area, therefore nature and wildlife have pretty much taken over. Spend about 3-4 hours visiting the Demilitarized Zone, then head to The War Memorial of Korea. Later, return back to Seoul for another night in the city.

Opt to visit the Samsung Leeum Contemporary Gallery, explore the Itaewon neighbourhood, or prebook the Kimchi making and Hanbok experience.

output.name: South Korea: Palace, Temple & Island — 13 Days
output.subtitle: Seoul to Jeju via high-speed rail, mountain temples, DMZ, and volcanic coastline
output.summary: This 13-day itinerary moves systematically through South Korea's layered geography and history: Seoul's palace grounds and street markets, a night in a working Buddhist temple in Gyeongju, the DMZ's heavily militarized border, hanok villages in Jeonju, bamboo forests and tea fields in the southwest, and three days on Jeju Island exploring waterfalls, lava formations, and the haenyeo women divers. Travel is by high-speed train, private vehicle, and domestic flight. Most days involve substantial walking and navigation through busy transit hubs; pack accordingly.
highlights: Overnight stay in a mountain temple in Gyeongju with morning meditation and monk martial arts
Visit the Korean Demilitarized Zone, a 4-kilometre buffer spanning 250 kilometres between North and South Korea
Stroll through Damyang Bamboo Forest, South Korea's largest bamboo grove at 150,000 square metres
Watch haenyeo women divers harvest seafood from the sea using breath-hold techniques on Jeju Island
Hike Seongsan Sunrise Peak, a UNESCO World Heritage volcanic formation on Jeju created 5,000 years ago
Visit Yangdong Folk Village, a 500-year-old UNESCO site with over 160 traditionally preserved homes
Experience a traditional hanok village stay in Jeonju with Hanjeongsik multi-course Korean dinner
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Seoul: Cheonggyecheon Stream and Myeongdong Orientation
Arrive in Seoul throughout the day and check into your hotel. There are no planned activities until the evening, allowing time to settle in and navigate the city at your own pace. At 6 pm, gather for a welcome meeting with your CEO and fellow travellers. This is your opportunity to meet the group, ask questions about the tour ahead, and get oriented to the basics of moving around Seoul.

Following the meeting, join your CEO for an orientation walk through the city centre. You'll start at Cheonggyecheon Stream, an 8.4-kilometre waterway and public space that runs through downtown Seoul. The walk passes nearly two dozen overhead bridges and small waterfalls—a quieter counterpoint to the urban density surrounding it. Your CEO will point out practical essentials: where to find supermarkets, main squares, and ATMs. These details matter when navigating a city on foot and by public transport.

From Cheonggyecheon, the walk continues into Myeongdong, a neighbourhood that operates at full intensity regardless of the hour. The streets form a dense grid packed with street food carts, major shopping malls, and entertainment venues. This is where you'll encounter Seoul's retail and food culture firsthand—vendors selling traditional snacks to contemporary fashion occupy nearly every corner.

Note that this tour requires comfort with spending most of the day on your feet and carrying your own luggage through busy train stations and streets. South Korea's train system forms the backbone of inter-city travel on this itinerary, so familiarity with moving efficiently through public spaces is essential.

After the orientation walk, you have the option to join fellow travellers for a group dinner to end your first evening. Otherwise, Myeongdong itself offers numerous dining choices if you prefer to wander independently. Check the hotel lobby notice or ask reception for the exact meeting time and location before heading out.

Day 2 — Seoul's Royal Heritage: Palaces, Traditional Villages, and Historic Quarters
Begin your Seoul exploration with a guided bus tour across the city's most significant districts, where centuries of Korean history remain visible amid the modern metropolis. Gyeongbokgung Palace, constructed in 1395 as the principal royal residence of the Joseon Dynasty, anchors this journey. Despite repeated destruction over the centuries, more than half of the palace's structures remain standing or have been meticulously restored. Within its expansive grounds sit two essential museums: the National Palace Museum and the National Folk Museum, which together chronicle the traditions and history of the Korean people during the Joseon era.

From the palace, venture into Bukchon Hanok Village, a neighbourhood that reflects approximately 600 years of Seoul's history. This area contains the city's largest concentration of privately owned traditional Korean wooden homes, known as hanok. Walking through its interconnected narrow alleys reveals the architectural care invested in these structures—small courtyards, decorative outer walls, and distinctive dark tiled roofs appear around nearly every corner, with roughly half a dozen alleyways showcasing particularly careful restoration work.

Next, visit Insadong Alley, one of Seoul's most established quarters. The narrow passages that wind through this historic area once housed the royal studio for painters during the Joseon Dynasty. Today, the alley operates as a cultural destination filled with antique shops, contemporary galleries, traditional tea houses, and restaurants serving authentic Korean cuisine. The blend of old and new here reflects Seoul's character.

The afternoon offers flexibility for independent exploration and optional activities suited to your interests. Gwangjang Market, one of South Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets, houses more than 5,000 shops and is particularly renowned for its fabric selection and authentic Korean street food—an ideal destination for those seeking to experience local market culture and taste specialties like bibimbap, soondae, and kimchi. Alternatively, the Seoul Museum of History provides a comprehensive overview of the city's evolution from the Stone Age to the present day, featuring interactive exhibits including a large floor map of Seoul useful for planning further exploration.

Breakfast is included. You will stay at Hotel Prince or a similar property.

Day 3 — High-Speed Train to Gyeongju: Temple Arrival and Overnight Stay
Board a high-speed train after breakfast for a two-hour journey south through the countryside to Gyeongju, the former capital of the Silla Kingdom for 1,000 years. The ride offers views of rural South Korea at a moderate pace before arriving at this historic city.

Upon arrival, settle into Golgulsa Temple for an overnight stay in a traditional ondol room. These spaces are heated for comfort, with beds made directly on the floor. Rooms are arranged in single-gender dormitories, shared among group members.

Your first evening introduces you to temple life. A traditional dinner prepared in the temple kitchen precedes a session on temple etiquette—the customs and practices that structure daily life here. You'll also observe a martial arts performance by resident monks, gaining insight into the physical discipline that complements spiritual practice.

In the morning, participate in the daily drum and bell ritual that marks the start of the monastic day. If you wish, take an easy hike up to Korea's only stone cave temple for guided meditation as the day breaks. Breakfast follows, completing your introduction to temple routines.

This overnight stay offers direct encounter with monastic practice—not as observer, but as temporary participant in the rhythms that have sustained this community for centuries.

Day 4 — Gyeongju: Temple, Observatory, and Royal Tombs
Begin with a peaceful morning meditation and martial arts practice, followed by a traditional drum and bell ritual before venturing into Gyeongju. Travel by private vehicle to visit the city's most significant historical landmarks.

Bulguksa Temple, a UNESCO site set on the slopes of Mount Toham, serves as a head temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The complex encompasses seven National treasures of South Korea, among them the Dabotap and Seokgatap stone pagodas, the Cheongun-gyo bridge, and two gilt-bronze statues of Buddha. Each element reflects the architectural and artistic standards of the Silla period.

In the heart of Gyeongju, the former capital of the Silla Kingdom, Cheomseongdae Observatory rises as a modest but significant structure. Dating to the seventh century, it remains one of East Asia's oldest surviving astronomical observatories. This stone tower was used to observe celestial patterns and forecast weather, serving as a cornerstone of the region's ancient scientific practice.

The Daereungwon Tomb Complex concludes your exploration. Within its rolling mounds and gardens lie 23 burial sites, the most notable being Cheonmachong and Hwangnamdaechong. These tombs contain thousands of relics exceeding 1,500 years in age, offering insight into royal Silla Dynasty life and the artistic standards of the period. The artifacts within document the customs, craftsmanship, and hierarchy of this ancient civilization.

Settled at Swiss Rosen Hotel Gyeongju (or similar) for the evening.

Day 5 — Yangdong Folk Village, Haedong Yonggungsa Temple and Busan Arrival
Depart Gyeongju-si by private vehicle for the 90-minute journey to Busan, a coastal city that combines modern development with historical significance. En route, visit Yangdong Folk Village, a UNESCO site within Gyeongju National Park. Founded in the early 1400s, this 500-year-old village preserves more than 160 homes showcasing traditional Joseon Dynasty architecture. Walking through its lanes offers a window into early Joseon life, with well-maintained structures set against a natural backdrop that has remained largely unchanged for centuries.

Continue toward the coast to reach Haedong Yonggungsa Temple, a Buddhist temple built directly into cliffsides overlooking the East China Sea. Originally constructed in 1376, this 14th-century structure ranks among Korea's frequently photographed temples, its seaside location creating an atmosphere of contemplation. Local tradition suggests that prayers offered here grant at least one wish. The temple complex invites quiet exploration of its halls and courtyards, and a traditional market nearby offers local snacks for those seeking an authentic taste of the region.

Upon arrival in Busan, settle into your accommodation at Felix Hotel by STX (or similar). An orientation walk introduces you to Haeundae Beach, one of Busan's most visited coastal areas, and nearby Dongbaek Island, home to the APEC House—a modern architectural structure offering views across the shoreline.

The evening is yours to experience Busan's culture. Opt to unwind at a jjimjilbang, a traditional Korean spa bathhouse featuring an array of hot spring tubs designed to rejuvenate body and mind. Alternatively, embrace the Korean tradition of noraebang—karaoke rooms where you can sing in private with friends. For those seeking additional activities, consider a night yacht ride cruising along Busan's illuminated coastline, or visit Busan Tower Observatory, where 360-degree views from its 120-metre height reveal the city's scale and geography. The tower, standing 69 metres above sea level, features a design inspired by the baldaquin of Dabotap Pagoda in Bulguksa Temple, linking this modern landmark to Korea's architectural heritage.

Day 6 — Busan's Markets and Culture Village; Return to Seoul
This day bridges two cities, beginning in Busan before the afternoon train journey to Seoul. The morning unfolds across several distinct neighbourhoods, each revealing different layers of the port city's character and commerce.

Start at Jagalchi Fish Market, the major market anchored at Nampo Port. This is where Busan's seafaring heritage becomes visible—rows of stalls display fish, octopus, and shellfish. The market operates with particular activity as locals and fishmongers negotiate prices. The sensory environment is deliberate and direct: the salt air, the calls of vendors, the volume of marine life on display.

From there, move to Gukjesijang, commonly known as Gukje Market, which sits near BIFF Square, Busan's well-known film district. This market carries historical weight. It emerged during the Korean War as a place where refugees could earn a living, and that origin remains part of its identity. Today it functions as a bustling international market where food stalls, home goods, clothing, and souvenirs create a dense, layered shopping environment. The market's evolution from necessity to thriving commerce reflects Busan's own trajectory.

Next is Yongdusan Park, a green space with deliberate design. The park's unique silhouette is said to resemble a dragon's head, and it contains over 70 different types of trees. The 118-metre Busan Tower rises from within the park, visible from across the city. This combination of natural landscape and architectural landmark creates a distinct sense of place in the urban fabric.

Gamcheon Culture Village offers a different visual environment. Set into the side of a mountain, the village is defined by its pastel-coloured houses, hand-painted murals, intimate cafes, and small shops. The village was born from necessity—residents originally settled here without formal planning—but has developed into a cultural area while maintaining its residential character. Walking through its narrow streets reveals both the artistic interventions and the lived reality of the neighbourhood.

By late morning, board the high-speed train for the 2.5-hour journey to Seoul. This efficient transit allows the day to encompass two cities without excess travel time consuming the itinerary.

Upon arrival in Seoul, visit Namdaemun Market, Korea's oldest traditional market. Dating to 1414, it has operated for over six centuries, and that longevity shows in its scale: over 10,000 vendors operate across several city blocks, making it the oldest and largest traditional market in the country. The density of commerce and the variety of goods—food, textiles, everyday items—reflect the market's role as a genuine centre of city life, not merely a tourist destination.

The remainder of the day offers several options. The cable car ascends to N Seoul Tower, Seoul's most recognised landmark, positioned at the top of Mt Namsan at 480 metres above sea level. Originally a broadcasting station, it now functions as a public observatory. The structure itself—standing 236.7 metres tall atop the 243-metre mountain—has appeared frequently in Korean television dramas and films. An additional fee grants access to the observation deck, where a 360-degree panoramic view encompasses the entire city.

Alternatively, spend time in Gangnam District, a neighbourhood that combines historical significance with ongoing development. Gangnam Station, one of Seoul's busiest subway hubs, contains an extensive underground shopping centre. The district also offers Bongeunsa, a Buddhist temple situated in the neighbourhood's centre, providing a counterpoint to the commercial activity. Restaurants throughout the district reflect both local and international cuisines.

Two other options complete the evening: Banpo Bridge, home to the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain Show—the world's longest bridge fountain, featuring nearly 10,000 LED lights and 380 water-spraying nozzles that synchronize with music and create different configurations throughout the day. By night, the fountain transforms into a display of coloured water jets. Alternatively, visit the Floating Islands, a culture complex comprising three man-made islands near Banpo Bridge, surrounded by LED lighting that creates a distinctive night-time visual effect.

Breakfast is included. Accommodation is at Hotel Prince or similar.

Day 7 — The Korean Demilitarized Zone and War Memorial
Begin with a private vehicle transfer to the Demilitarized Zone, the de facto border between North and South Korea established in 1953. Spend about 3-4 hours visiting the Demilitarized Zone, the de facto border between North and South Korea. Created as a Cold War boundary, the DMZ's lack of civilian development has allowed natural habitat to recover, creating an unexpected wildlife refuge within one of the world's most geopolitically significant borders.

Return to Seoul for the second portion of the day. Visit the War Memorial of Korea, a substantial complex divided into indoor and outdoor exhibits. The memorial preserves approximately 9,000 artifacts documenting Korea's military history and the Korean War, offering historical context for those interested in the nation's past.

The remainder of your afternoon and evening are yours. Rest at your accommodation or venture independently through Seoul. Those seeking additional activities can visit the Samsung Leeum Contemporary Gallery, navigate the diverse Itaewon neighbourhood, or participate in a pre-booked kimchi-making and Hanbok (traditional Korean dress) experience.

Overnight in Seoul at Hotel Prince or similar. Breakfast included.

Day 8 — Seoul to Jeonju: Hanok Village and Traditional Korean Dinner
Begin with a free morning in Seoul before heading to the train station for your high-speed journey to Jeonju. The bullet train carries you across the country, delivering you to one of Korea's best-preserved traditional towns.

Upon arrival in Jeonju, enter the hanok village—a quarter of wooden-frame houses with distinctive curved tile roofs that reflect centuries of Korean residential architecture. Your guided tour takes you through the town's principal landmarks: Gyeonggijeon Shrine, an important historical site; Jeondong Catholic Church, a structure blending Eastern and Western architectural traditions; the Korean Liquor Museum, where you'll learn the history of traditional Korean beverages; and the Jeonju Handicraft Exhibition Hall, showcasing the region's artisanal production.

As evening descends, settle in for a Hanjeongsik traditional dinner—a full-course Korean meal that unfolds across multiple small banchan (side) plates. Each dish reflects Korean culinary tradition, allowing you to taste the depth and diversity of the cuisine in one sitting.

You'll spend the night in a traditional hanok accommodation within the village, allowing the experience to fully settle.

Optional activities are available if you wish to deepen your cultural engagement. Consider donning a Hanbok—the traditional Korean dress—and photographing yourself in the village streets in full regalia, with traditionally styled hair. Alternatively, visit the Hanok Village Craft Museum to engage in hands-on traditional crafts: create hanji (Korean handmade paper), shape your own ceramic piece on a pottery wheel, practise calligraphy with brush and ink, or craft and paint a traditional fan with designs inspired by flowers, birds, and landscapes.

Meals included: Breakfast and Dinner

Day 9 — Damyang Bamboo Forest and Boseong Green Tea Fields to Yeosu
Today marks a shift from urban environments to South Korea's countryside. Travelling from Jeonju in a private vehicle, you'll head toward the coast with stops at two of the region's defining landscapes.

In Damyang, visit Juknokwon Bamboo Forest, the most extensive bamboo grove in South Korea. Juknokwon is a bamboo forest in South Korea with a variety of walking trails. Join your CEO for a walk through these paths, moving beneath towering bamboo stalks, or rest in the filtered light and fresh air. Walking time: approximately 1–2 hours depending on chosen routes.

tour.name: Cross-Mountain Spine Cycling Tour
tour.subtitle: 555km & 8400m Elevation | White Sand Beaches | KOM | Hot Springs
tour.summary:
At 555km and 8400 meters of elevation, this is a tour for those wishing to truly test themselves on two wheels!
Carefully crafted from years of experience, this 5-stage route highlights why Taiwan is fast becoming Asia's top cycling destination. Expect challenging climbs, quiet roads, flowing descents, and stops at hot spring. Feast on a variety of cuisines, from Hakka and Han to Aboriginal. This unforgettable cycling adventure ends with a glass of champagne on the white sand beaches of Kenting.
highlights:
Ride from Taipei to the southern tip along the 'spine' of Taiwan
Cycle up the famed Taiwan KOM Challenge route
A day off to enjoy the beauty of Sun Moon Lake
Experience Aboriginal culture and delicious cuisine
Visit some of Taiwan's best known temples
Incredible 50km+ descents, amongst the longest in the world
Finish your trip with a couple of days at Taiwan's premier beach town
tour.itineraries:
Day One: Taipei - Yilan (109km / 221m / 5 hrs)
Riding from southern Taipei, we quickly reach the countryside. The morning has steady climbs, while the afternoon levels out along a jade river winding along a deep gorge. Passing through Chatianshan Nature Reserve; today features little traffic and lots of views. Though challenging in parts, the descent and a soak in wild hot springs makes it worthwhile.

Day Two: Yilan - Lishan (75km / 2633m / 4.5 hrs)
Today features a ride up the first 3/4 of the world famous Taiwan KOM Challenge 2024 route. A beautiful and iconic cycling route. Take your time and enjoy the views along a road that is quiet and remote. We will arrive at Lishan in the afternoon, check in and enjoy a well-earned celebratory meal.

Day Three: Lishan - Sun Moon Lake (110km / 2081m / 5.5 hrs)
The climbing starts almost straight the hotel, as we take on the last kilometres of the Taiwan KOM Challenge. Today's summit, Wuling (3275m) is the island's highest passable point. From here, we follow a 50km descent – and it is as exhilarating as it sounds! We head up to Sun Moon Lake, one of Taiwan's most iconic destinations and the largest lake in the country.

Day Four: Sun Moon Lake (Rest Day)
Today is a well-deserved rest day, with a chance for guests to relax at the hotel, visit some of the cultural sites including pagodas, temples or enjoy a unique tea-tasting experience.

Day Five: Sun Moon Lake - Alishan (128km / 2699m / 6.5 hrs)
Another challenging day in the saddle awaits as we climb towards Jade Mountain! This is a stunning climb day with breathtaking views, terraced tea fields and rice paddies! We roll into Alishan Township at the end of the day, which sits high on the central plateau in Taiwan's famous tea country.

Day Six: Alishan - Qishan (126km / 1570m / 5 hrs)
Today we move off the Central Mountain Range and down towards the plains of the southwest. A morning of descents takes us past the Tsengwen Reservoir, before finishing at Qishan Old Street, a busy market renowned for its street vendors & historic buildings with baroque-style facades.

Day Seven: Qishan - Kenting (122km / 456m / 4.5 hrs)
Today is the final ride day. We head through the southern countryside along to a coastal road and finally into the tropical resort town of Kenting, an area famed for its stunning beaches and crystal blue seas. A must is a glass of champers on the beach to celebrate the end of this wonderful tour!

Day Eight: Kenting - Taipei (Non-Riding Day)
After a leisurely morning, breakfast and a final swim in the ocean, the group will pack up and transfer back to Taipei in private transportation for the end of the tour.

output.name: Taiwan's Mountain Spine: 555km Cycling from Taipei to Kenting
output.subtitle: Eight days of high-altitude climbing, 50km+ descents, and remote mountain roads across Taiwan's central ridge.
output.summary: This eight-day cycling route traces Taiwan's mountain spine from Taipei to the southern coast—555 kilometers at 8,400 meters of cumulative elevation. The journey follows five distinct stages, including most of the Taiwan KOM Challenge route, which summits Wuling at 3,275 meters, the island's highest passable point. Days alternate between long climbing stages and extended descents; a rest day at Sun Moon Lake breaks the physical demands midway. The route passes through tea country, Aboriginal regions, and lowland farmland before finishing on Kenting's beaches. Overnight stops include mountain towns, resort areas, and cultural centers, with meals ranging from Hakka and Han regional cooking to Aboriginal specialties.
highlights: Ride the Taiwan KOM Challenge route, summiting Wuling at 3,275 meters
Descend over 50 kilometers from Wuling to Sun Moon Lake in a single day
Rest and visit Sun Moon Lake, Taiwan's largest lake, with access to historic pagodas and tea tastings
Climb through terraced tea fields and rice paddies toward Alishan Township on the central plateau
Pass the Tsengwen Reservoir and historic Qishan Old Street with baroque-style market buildings
Finish with two days at Kenting's beaches and tropical resort setting
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Taipei to Yilan: Gorge Roads and Hot Springs
The route departs southern Taipei into the countryside, climbing steadily through the morning before the terrain levels into afternoon riding along a jade river that winds through a deep gorge. The Chatianshan Nature Reserve provides most of the day's scenery on a road with minimal traffic. Late afternoon brings a descent to lower elevation and a soak in wild hot springs.

Day 2 — Yilan to Lishan: Taiwan KOM Challenge Begins
The famous Taiwan KOM Challenge route begins here. This 75-kilometer stage climbs 2,633 meters over the first three-quarters of the challenge course—a quiet, remote road that gains elevation steadily through the afternoon. Arrival in Lishan comes as the day's light fades, followed by a celebratory meal at the hotel.

Day 3 — Lishan to Sun Moon Lake: Wuling Summit and the 50km Descent
Climbing resumes immediately from the hotel as the route tackles the final kilometers of the KOM Challenge, reaching Wuling at 3,275 meters—Taiwan's highest passable summit. From the peak, a 50km descent follows to Sun Moon Lake, one of Taiwan's largest lakes.

Day 4 — Sun Moon Lake: Rest Day
A full day off. Guests can remain at the hotel or wander nearby cultural sites, including pagodas and temples, or participate in a tea-tasting experience at one of the lakeside facilities.

Day 5 — Sun Moon Lake to Alishan: Tea Country Climbing
This 128-kilometer stage climbs 2,699 meters toward Jade Mountain through Taiwan's famous tea country. Terraced tea fields and rice paddies line the ascending road. The route ends at Alishan Township, situated on the central plateau at high elevation, after a full day of climbing with sustained views across the surrounding highlands.

Day 6 — Alishan to Qishan: Descent to the Plains
The route leaves the Central Mountain Range, descending 1,570 meters over 126 kilometers toward the southwestern plains. Morning descending passes the Tsengwen Reservoir before the route flattens into the lowlands. The day ends at Qishan Old Street, a busy market district known for street vendors and historic baroque-style buildings.

Day 7 — Qishan to Kenting: Final Coastal Ride
The last full riding day covers 122 kilometers through southern countryside and along the coast to Kenting, Taiwan's main beach resort. Elevation gain is minimal—only 456 meters across the day—as the route moves through farmland before reaching the tropical setting of Kenting's renowned beaches.

Day 8 — Kenting to Taipei: Final Morning and Return
After a leisurely morning and a final swim in the ocean, the group enjoys breakfast before packing up. Private transportation then carries everyone back to Taipei, bringing the tour to a close.

tour.name: Highlights Of Thailand
tour.summary: This is a Thailand trip jam-packed with experiences and destinations that ventures beyond where other trips go. Thailand's stunning beauty and charismatic culture are ever present on this ExoAsia adventure - discover the exquisite 'Land of Smiles' in style. Thailand conjures up images of spicy delicacies, majestic elephants, golden Buddhas, colourful hilltribe villages, fantastic shopping and exotic hideaways - and we experience it all on this trip. Witness traditional hilltribe life in a H'mong village, support the rehabilitation of the endangered Asian elephant, step back in time in the ancient kingdom of Sukhothai and try your hand at creating some gastronomic delights. This is your chance to capture the adventure and essence of timeless Thailand.
highlights:
Whip up a culinary storm and taste delicious local dishes in a Thai cooking class in Chiang Mai
Travel like the locals do on an overnight sleeper train, the best way to travel long distances, meet locals and maximise time at destinations
Immerse yourself in the wonders of an ancient tribal culture with a night in the Hmong Lodge, treated to a BBQ dinner and Hmong Cultural show
Make some new pachyderm pals at the unique Friends of the Asia Elephants Hospital and learn about the great work they do to protect these magnificent creatures
Uncover the ancient charms of Sukhothai as you leisurely cycle around the ruin-filled Historical Park, and feel your own cheerfulness increasing in the city named ‘Rising Happiness’
Pay your respect at the memorials by the infamous ‘Bridge over the River Kwai’ – learn about its dark history and the construction of the death railway in Kanchanaburi during the war
tour.itineraries:
Day 1 – Bangkok - Arrival
Sa-wat dee! Welcome to Thailand. Thailand's bustling capital, Bangkok is famous for its tuk tuks, khlong boats and street vendors serving up delicious Thai food. Your adventure begins with a welcome meeting at 6pm on Day 1. Please ask the hotel reception where it will take place.
Overnight in Bangkok

Day 2 – Bangkok - Overnight Train To Chiang Mai
Begin the day with a river cruise down the Chao Phraya River to explore the famous ‘khlongs’ (canals) (approximately 1 hour). Life along these canals seems a world away from the chaotic streets of the capital. Pay a visit to the magnificent Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha. The sprawling royal complex houses numerous ornate structures that highlight the grand architectural traditions of Thailand. The rest of the afternoon is free.
Overnight train
Meals: Breakfast

Day 3 – Chiang Mai
The most vibrant city in northern Thailand, Chiang Mai has many famous temples and an interesting old city area. Renowned for dazzling beauty and extremely welcoming locals, the ‘Rose of the North’ will leave you spellbound. Chances are, you won’t want to leave. Embark on a scenic, winding drive up a mountain (approximately 45 minutes) to one of the country's most stunning temple complexes, Doi Suthep. A 300-step naga-guarded stairway leads you to the temples, and the climb is well worth the effort. The hypnotic atmosphere of chanting Buddhist monks and sweeping views of the city make this a most memorable experience. Your leader can help you to arrange optional activities for your free time today and tomorrow – you can get active with a bicycle tour to discover the city and surrounding countryside from a different perspective, indulge in a Thai massage or a spa treatment, or just read a book by the pool. This evening you’ll enjoy a traditional khantohk dinner while being entertained by Akha, Yao, Lahu, H'mong, Lisu and Karen tribal dances. The term Khantohk comes from many small dishes (khan) served on a small or low table (tohk) that evolved from communal meals with honoured guests.
Overnight in Chiang Mai
Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 4 – Chiang Mai
Discover some of the secrets of Thai cuisine by joining a cookery course. Learn about the main ingredients of Thai cuisine, how they are used and stored and what alternatives you can substitute if you can't get them at home. Questions are welcome and you are provided with a comprehensive book of recipes and ingredient details. For lunch, sit down and feast on the delicious results of your tuition. The meal is usually rounded off with a tasting of seasonal Thai fruit. 
Overnight in Chiang Mai
Meals: Breakfast / Lunch

Day 5 – Chiang Mai - Hmong Lodge
Board a minivan for the drive north to the Hmong Hilltribe Lodge, set in picturesque hilly countryside (approximately 1.5 hours). Set in a peaceful valley of a scenic mountain range and surrounded by stunning natural landscapes of jungle with misty mountain views, the Hmong lodge offers a unique and tranquil experience. It's a great escape from the hustle and bustle of busy tourist spots. The rooms are simple and rustic, fitting perfectly with the natural environment. Be sure to pack a warm jumper as the weather will be mild and cool weather year-round due to the lofty mountain locale. The Hmong are an ethnic minority in Thailand who originated in the south of China. Today they comprise the second largest hilltribe group in Thailand. After a barbeque dinner in the lodge's open-air dining area, the day concludes with a cultural performance by the Hmong people. You'll gain an insight into the traditional lifestyle of the tribe, with a wedding ceremony enactment, shamanic ritual and makong (cotton ball) throwing.
Overnight in Hmong Lodge
Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 6 – Hmong Lodge - Sukhothai
Depart the hilltribe village this morning and head on to Lampang (approximately 2 hours). Lampang, also known locally as 'mueang rot ma' meaning Horse Carriage City, is considered by some Thais as the last paradise in Thailand. Here you’ll pay a visit to the Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre, the first elephant hospital in the world established to care for sick and abused elephants. They aim to protect and conserve the welfare of elephants both domesticated and wild, and preserve the animals' natural habitat and lifestyle. You’ll learn more about this important initiative and become acquainted with some of its resident patients. After spending time with the elephants, farewell your new pachyderm pals and head to Sukhothai (approximately 3.5 hours) for the night.
Overnight in Sukhothai
Meals: Breakfast

Day 7 – Sukhothai - Kanchanaburi
Located on a fertile plain, Sukhothai was established in the 13th century as one of the first ancient capitals of Siam, and the name means the 'Dawn of Happiness'. It’s now famous for its World Heritage-listed historic park that celebrates the Golden Age of Thai civilisation. Head out to the historical ruins of Old Sukhothai, set amid beautiful lakes and gardens. The religious art and architecture of the Sukhothai era are considered to be the most classic of Thai styles, and the Sukhothai Historical Park contains the remains of 21 historic sites, with awe-inspiring Buddha images and four large ponds often filled with stunning lotus flowers in full bloom. Upon arrival at the park, hire bicycles and enjoy a few leisurely hours feeling the breeze in your hair and learning about the history of this fascinating place. Enjoy a home-cooked picnic lunch somewhere along the way, and if you have enough free time, visit a local ceramics factory. You’ll then hop on a private minibus south to Kanchanaburi (approximately 6 hours). Located where the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai rivers converge, Kanchanaburi is home to the infamous 'Bridge on the River Kwai'.
Overnight in Kanchanaburi
Meals: Breakfast / Lunch

Day 8 – Kanchanaburi
This morning you’ll get an insight into the darker side of Kanchanaburi’s history with a moving visit to the Hellfire Pass Memorial, built to honour the Allied POWs and Asian conscripts who died while constructing some of the most difficult stretches of the Thai-Burma Death Railway. You can head out to a teak observation deck and look across to Myanmar just 25 miles away. You’ll also see the eponymous pass, cut through rock 18 metres deep, that got its name from the hellish fires used to light the work at night. Boarding at Nam Tok station, the main terminal of the Death Railway, take a ride along the historic tracks along the Kwai Noi River and travel over the original wooden viaduct (the Bridge on the River Kwai) constructed by the allied POWs. Pass through magnificent scenery and spend a moment reflecting on those who were forced to give their lives in the process of bending this environment to man’s will. Tonight you can explore the rows of street vendors in town and grab a drink overlooking the River Kwai.
Overnight in Kanchanaburi
Meals: Breakfast

Day 9 – Kanchanaburi - Bangkok
Return to the bustling capital Bangkok by private minivan today (approximately 3 hours). The rest of the day (until the evening) is free
Overnight in Bangkok
Meals: Breakfast

Day 10 – Bangkok - Departure
There are no activities planned for the final day and you are able to depart the accommodation at any time.
Meals: Breakfast

output.name: Thailand: Bangkok, Chiang Mai & Kanchanaburi — 10 Days
output.subtitle: Northern temples, hilltribe culture, Death Railway history, and a cooking class in Chiang Mai across 10 days by train, minivan, and bicycle.
output.summary: This 10-day route moves through Thailand's three most distinct regions: Bangkok's river life and palace architecture, Chiang Mai's temple complexes and northern hilltribe territories, and Kanchanaburi's war history along the River Kwai. You'll spend nights in a Hmong village lodge in the mountains north of Chiang Mai, cycle through the 13th-century ruins of Sukhothai's historical park, study Thai cooking techniques in a Chiang Mai kitchen, visit an elephant hospital in Lampang, and travel the Death Railway tracks over the Bridge on the River Kwai. An overnight sleeper train connects Bangkok to Chiang Mai, and a private minivan handles the longer southern legs. Guides are local English speakers, and meals—including a khantohk dinner with tribal performances and a home-cooked picnic in Sukhothai's gardens—are built into each day's rhythm.
highlights: Khao Phraya River cruise and Grand Palace complex in Bangkok, including the Temple of the Emerald Buddha
Doi Suthep temple complex: 45-minute mountain drive from Chiang Mai, accessed by 300-step naga-guarded stairway with city views
Thai cooking class in Chiang Mai: learn ingredient preparation, storage, and substitutions; prepare and eat a full lunch
Overnight stay in a Hmong Lodge in the mountains north of Chiang Mai, with traditional barbecue dinner and cultural performance
Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre in Lampang: hands-on time with rescued and rehabilitated elephants
Sukhothai Historical Park: bicycle tour of 21 historic sites, Buddha images, lakes, and lotus ponds from the 13th-century Golden Age
Hellfire Pass Memorial: World War II site honouring Allied POWs and Asian conscripts; observation deck overlooking Myanmar 25 miles away
Death Railway journey: ride original wooden viaduct over the Bridge on the River Kwai between Nam Tok and Kanchanaburi stations
output.itineraries:
Day 1 — Arrival in Bangkok
Welcome to Bangkok. Thailand's capital centres on the Chao Phraya River, where longtail boats navigate the khlongs—canal networks that run parallel to main streets. A welcome meeting is scheduled at your hotel at 6 p.m., where your guide will brief you on the itinerary and logistics for the week ahead.

Day 2 — Chao Phraya River, Grand Palace & Overnight Train to Chiang Mai
Start with a one-hour river cruise down the Chao Phraya, observing the khlongs and waterside life. You will visit the Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha—a royal complex with ornate structures built in Thai architectural traditions. The afternoon is free. In the evening, board the overnight sleeper train north to Chiang Mai. You will arrive in the north the following morning.

Day 3 — Doi Suthep Temple & Tribal Performances in Chiang Mai
Chiang Mai is the regional centre of northern Thailand, known for its temples and historic old city. This morning, a 45-minute drive ascends the mountain to Doi Suthep, a major temple complex. A 300-step stairway with naga (serpent) railings leads to the temple structures, offering views of the city and access to the courtyard where Buddhist monks chant. The afternoon offers flexibility. Your leader can help arrange optional activities: a bicycle tour through the city and countryside, a traditional Thai massage, or rest at the hotel. This evening, a khantohk dinner is served—a traditional meal where multiple small dishes are presented on low tables. Performances by Akha, Yao, Lahu, Hmong, Lisu, and Karen dancers accompany the meal. Overnight in Chiang Mai. Meals: Breakfast / Dinner

Day 4 — Thai Cooking Class in Chiang Mai
Spend the day in a hands-on Thai cooking course. You will learn the main ingredients used in Thai cuisine, their storage, and available substitutions. You will prepare several dishes and eat lunch of your own cooking. A tasting of seasonal Thai fruit is typically included. A comprehensive recipe book and ingredient guide are provided. The rest of the day is free.

Day 5 — Minivan to Hmong Lodge in the Northern Mountains
A 1.5-hour minivan journey carries you north into hilly countryside to the Hmong Hilltribe Lodge, set in a mountain valley surrounded by jungle. The Hmong are an ethnic minority group now the second-largest hilltribe population in Thailand. Lodge rooms are rustic and designed to fit into the local landscape. Cool mountain weather year-round requires a warm layer. After a barbecue dinner in the open-air dining area, the Hmong people offer a cultural performance including a wedding ceremony enactment, a shamanic ritual, and the makong (cotton ball) throwing game. Overnight at Hmong Lodge.

Day 6 — Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre & Journey to Sukhothai
Depart the hilltribe lodge and drive two hours to Lampang, known locally as 'Horse Carriage City.' The Friends of the Asian Elephant Centre, the first hospital dedicated to treating sick and abused elephants, is located here. You will spend time observing elephant residents and learning about rehabilitation work. Continue south to Sukhothai by minivan, approximately 3.5 hours.

Day 7 — Sukhothai Historical Park by Bicycle
Sukhothai was founded in the 13th century as one of Siam's first capitals. The World Heritage-listed historical park contains the remains of 21 historic sites. The park sits on a fertile plain with lakes and gardens. Upon arrival, you will hire bicycles and spend several hours riding through the ruins, observing Buddha images and religious architecture of the Sukhothai era. A home-cooked picnic lunch is arranged along the route. An optional visit to a local ceramics factory can be arranged. Late afternoon, board a private minivan south toward Kanchanaburi, approximately 6 hours. Kanchanaburi sits where the Khwae Noi and Khwae Yai rivers converge.

Day 8 — Death Railway, Hellfire Pass & Bridge on the River Kwai
This morning you visit the Hellfire Pass Memorial, built to honour Allied prisoners of war and Asian conscripts who died constructing the Thai-Burma Death Railway during World War II. The pass is cut 18 metres deep through rock; it earned its name from fires used to light night work shifts. Boarding at Nam Tok station, you will ride historic tracks along the Khwae Noi River and cross the original wooden viaduct known as the Bridge on the River Kwai, constructed by Allied prisoners. The evening is free to visit the town or rest by the river. Meals: Breakfast

Day 9 — Kanchanaburi to Bangkok
A three-hour private minivan journey returns you to Bangkok. The remainder of the day is free. Overnight in Bangkok. Meals: Breakfast

Day 10 — Bangkok Departure
Breakfast is included. You depart at your own pace.

output.name: North India: Mughal Courts, Rajput Forts & the Ganges in 15 Days
output.subtitle: Delhi to Varanasi via Agra, Rajasthan, and Khajuraho: fifteen days through India's deepest layers of heritage
output.summary: This fifteen-day journey moves through the architectural and spiritual heart of North India, giving each place the time and context it deserves. Delhi opens the itinerary with its full sweep of Mughal power: the Red Fort, the Jama Masjid, Humayun's Tomb, and the 12th-century Qutub Minar. From there, Agra yields the Taj Mahal and the Agra Fort before the route passes through Fatehpur Sikri, the Mughal capital abandoned within a generation of its founding, on the drive into Jaipur. Rajasthan unfolds across several days: the astronomical precision of Jantar Mantar and the hilltop drama of Amber Fort in Jaipur; the indigo city of Jodhpur commanded by Mehrangarh; the 15th-century marble colonnades of the Ranakpur Jain temples; and Udaipur's City Palace above Lake Pichola, where Rajput court culture reached its most sophisticated expression. The final stage moves east to Khajuraho, whose 11th-century carved temples represent one of the subcontinent's great medieval achievements, and then to Varanasi, where the ghats and the evening Aarti ceremony at Dashashwamedh bring the journey to a contemplative close on the banks of the Ganges. Private transport and English-speaking guides accompany the journey throughout.

Mehrangarh Fort looming over the blue-washed rooftops of Jodhpur, with the Jaswant Thada cenotaph and Umaid Bhawan Palace nearby
Ranakpur's 15th-century Jain temple complex, its carved marble colonnades encountered en route between Jodhpur and Udaipur
The City Palace and Jagdish Temple in Udaipur, with time at Pichola and Fateh Sagar lakes
The Western Group of 11th-century temples at Khajuraho, one of medieval India's most remarkable ensembles of carved sandstone
Dashashwamedh Ghat and the evening Ganges Aarti ceremony in Varanasi
Sarnath's deer park and museum, where the Buddha delivered his first teaching, just outside Varanasi

output.itineraries:
Day 1 · Arrival in Delhi
Arrival at Delhi airport, with a private transfer to your hotel for the night.

Day 2 · Mughal and Imperial Delhi: Red Fort, Jama Masjid & Qutub Minar
The day traces Delhi's layers of power through the Red Fort, Jama Masjid, India Gate, Humayun's Tomb, Lotus Temple, and the 12th-century Qutub Minar. Overnight in Delhi.

Day 3 · Agra: The Taj Mahal, Agra Fort & Itmad-ud-Daulah
A drive of approximately 200 kilometres brings you to Agra. The day takes in the Taj Mahal, whose white marble and proportional harmony repay unhurried attention, alongside the Agra Fort, the delicate Itmad-ud-Daulah, and the Mughal mausoleum at Sikandra. Overnight in Agra.

Day 4 · Agra to Jaipur via Fatehpur Sikri
The drive to Jaipur passes through Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's 16th-century red sandstone capital, now eloquently abandoned. Evening at leisure. Overnight in Jaipur.

Day 5 · Jaipur: Amber Fort, Jantar Mantar, Hawa Mahal & City Palace
Jaipur holds some of the finest Rajput architecture in India. The day moves through Amber Fort on its ridge above the city, the City Palace, the Jantar Mantar observatory whose stone instruments calculated celestial movements with precision, the five-storey Hawa Mahal, and the Albert Hall Museum. Overnight in Jaipur.

Day 6 · Jaipur to Khejarla via Pushkar's Sacred Lake and Temple
The day's drive (approximately 270 kilometres) passes through Pushkar, where a sacred lake and ancient temple have drawn pilgrims for centuries. Overnight in Khejarla.

Day 7 · Khejarla to Jodhpur: Mehrangarh Fort, Jaswant Thada & Umaid Bhawan Palace
A short drive of approximately 85 kilometres reaches Jodhpur. Mehrangarh Fort commands the city from a sheer rock outcrop, its scale and state of preservation making it among Rajasthan's most formidable fortresses. The day also takes in the white marble Jaswant Thada cenotaph, the Umaid Bhawan Palace, and the Clock Tower and Sadar Market in the old quarter below. Overnight in Jodhpur.

Day 8 · Jodhpur to Udaipur via the Ranakpur Jain Temples
The drive to Udaipur (approximately 260 kilometres) pauses at Ranakpur, where a 15th-century Jain temple complex of extraordinary carved marble colonnades remains an active site of worship and scholarship. The evening is free to settle beside the lakes, with Jag Mandir visible across the water. Overnight in Udaipur.

Day 9 · Udaipur: City Palace, Jagdish Temple, Pichola & Fateh Sagar Lakes
Udaipur's City Palace represents the apogee of Rajput courtly culture, its layered galleries and terraces built across three centuries above Lake Pichola. The day also takes in the Jagdish Temple, Fateh Sagar Lake, the Crystal Gallery, and the graceful Gangaur Ghat. Overnight in Udaipur.

Day 10 · Udaipur to Delhi: A Quiet Morning, then Onward by Air
A quiet morning in Udaipur precedes a flight to Delhi. Transfer to hotel and overnight in Delhi.

Day 11 · Khajuraho: The Western Group Temples
Fly to Khajuraho and explore the Western Group's 11th-century sandstone temples, celebrated for their intricate carving. Attend the evening light and sound show. Overnight in Khajuraho.

Day 12 · Khajuraho to Varanasi: Arrival on the Ganges & the Dashashwamedh Aarti
A flight brings you to Varanasi, one of the world's continuously inhabited cities. The evening is given to Dashashwamedh Ghat, where the Ganges Aarti ceremony unfolds against the river at dusk. Overnight in Varanasi.

Day 13 · Varanasi & Sarnath: Ancient Temples and the Site of the Buddha's First Teaching
The day moves between Sarnath, where a deer park and museum mark the place of the Buddha's first discourse, and the ancient temples of Varanasi, whose layered religious traditions span millennia. Overnight in Varanasi.

Day 14 · Varanasi to Delhi: Return Flight and Evening at Leisure
A flight returns you to Delhi. Transfer to hotel, with the evening left open. Overnight in Delhi.

Day 15 · Departure from Delhi
Transfer to Delhi airport for your onward flight.
